recipes.name: Ulte Tawe Ka Paratha
recipes.subtitle: wafer-thin layered paratha cooked on the back of an upturned tawa

ingredients.note: a little wholemeal gives the paratha some backbone

ingredients.qty: 6 tbsp, melted, plus more for cooking

prepNotes: The dough needs 45 minutes covered at room temperature. Unrested dough will not roll thin enough and springs back.
You need an upturned kadhai or a heavy iron tawa turned convex side up. The curve is what lets the bread drape and cook evenly.
Melt the ghee for laminating and keep it liquid but not hot beside your rolling board.

steps.text: Mix the maida, atta, salt and sugar, rub in 2 tbsp of the melted ghee, then bring together with the warm milk and enough warm water to make a soft dough.
Knead 10 minutes until smooth and elastic, then cover with a damp cloth and rest 45 minutes.
steps.tip: Ten minutes of kneading is what builds the stretch. Under-kneaded dough tears when you roll it thin.

steps.text: Divide into 8 and roll one ball into a 20cm disc.
Brush it all over with melted ghee, dust lightly with dry maida, then cut a slit from centre to edge and roll it tightly into a cone.
steps.tip: Ghee then flour, in that order. That pairing is what separates the layers.

steps.text: Press the cone down onto its point into a flat pastry and rest 10 minutes. Repeat with the rest.
Roll each pastry out to a very thin disc, 22–24cm across, working from the centre outwards.
steps.tip: Light pressure and lots of small strokes. Leaning on the pin squashes the layers together.

steps.text: Set the tawa upside down over medium heat and let it get properly hot, 4 minutes.
Drape a paratha over the convex surface and cook 60–90 seconds until the underside is spotted brown and it lifts freely.
Flip with tongs, brush with ghee and cook 60 seconds more, pressing the edges down onto the metal.
Crush the hot paratha lightly between your palms to open the layers and serve at once with galouti or korma.
steps.tip: That crumpling is the point of the whole exercise. Do it while it is too hot to be comfortable.

recipes.storage: Best within minutes of cooking. The rolled, un-cooked pastries keep a day refrigerated between sheets of paper. Cooked parathas go leathery in the fridge; refresh on a hot tawa with a little ghee.

recipes.name: Warqi Paratha
recipes.subtitle: a many-layered flaky paratha that shatters into thin leaves, the Lucknow bread for korma

ingredients.note: plain flour; atta will not give the leaves
2 in the dough, 4 for layering and cooking
beaten with ghee into the layering paste, or sata

prepNotes: The layering paste (sata) is 3 tbsp soft ghee beaten with the rice flour until it is white and fluffy. Do this first and keep it at room temperature.
Rest the dough a full 30 minutes covered with a damp cloth. Unrested dough springs back and the layers tear.
Work in a cool kitchen if you can; warm ghee melts into the dough instead of separating the leaves.

steps.text: Rub 2 tbsp ghee into the maida with the salt and sugar until the flour looks like damp breadcrumbs and holds when squeezed.
Add the warm milk, then water a little at a time, and knead 6-8 minutes to a soft, smooth dough that is slightly stickier than chapati dough.
Cover with a damp cloth and rest 30 minutes.
Divide into 4 balls. Roll one out into a thin round about 22cm across, as even as you can get it.
Spread 1 heaped tsp of the ghee-and-rice-flour paste right to the edges, then pleat the round into a narrow fan, folding it back and forth in 1.5cm concertina folds.
steps.tip: Spread the paste thin and to the very edge. Bare patches glue the layers shut.

steps.text: Stretch the pleated strip gently, then coil it into a spiral like a snail shell and tuck the end underneath. Rest 10 minutes.
Press the coil flat with your palm and roll it out to about 15cm, using the lightest pressure you can. Repeat with the rest.
steps.tip: Roll from the centre outwards and stop while it still looks thick. Pressing hard crushes the layers you just built.

steps.text: Cook on a medium-hot tawa 1.5 minutes a side until pale brown spots appear, then brush with ghee and press the edges down with a cloth as it puffs.
Lift off and immediately clap the paratha between your palms once. The leaves separate and fan out.

recipes.storage: Best within an hour. Cooked parathas keep a day wrapped in a cloth in an airtight box; revive on a dry tawa for 40 seconds a side. The dough keeps 24 hours refrigerated.

recipes.name: Zarda
recipes.subtitle: saffron sweet rice studded with nuts and raisins, served at the end of a dastarkhwan

ingredients.qty: a generous pinch, steeped in 3 tbsp warm milk
ingredients.note: the colour comes from saffron, not food dye

prepNotes: Soak the rice 30 minutes and drain it well. Aged long-grain basmati holds its shape; new-crop rice turns to porridge.
Steep the saffron in warm milk for 20 minutes before you start.
Have the nuts fried and drained before the rice goes on. The last stage moves quickly.

steps.text: Fry the almonds, pistachios, cashews and coconut in 2 tbsp ghee until just gold, 2 minutes, then the raisins for 20 seconds until they puff. Drain and set aside.
steps.tip: Raisins go in last and come out fast; they burn in seconds.

steps.text: Boil 1.2 litres of water with the salt, half the saffron milk, the cardamom and cloves.
Add the drained rice and cook uncovered for 6–7 minutes, until the grains are 80 percent done and still firm at the core.
steps.tip: Bite one: it should give but leave a chalky centre. It finishes cooking in the syrup.

steps.text: Drain thoroughly in a colander and leave 5 minutes to steam dry.
In a heavy pan melt the remaining 3 tbsp ghee, add the sugar and 100ml water and stir until it dissolves into a thin syrup, 3 minutes.
Fold the drained rice gently into the syrup with the remaining saffron milk, using a flat spoon and lifting rather than stirring.
steps.tip: Stirring smashes the grains. Lift and fold from underneath.

steps.text: Cover tightly, put a heavy lid or a weight on top and cook on the lowest possible heat for 15 minutes.
Uncover: the syrup should be absorbed and the grains separate and glossy. If wet, cook uncovered 3 minutes more.
Scatter over the fried nuts, raisins, crumbled khoya and kewra water, cover again and rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving warm.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. Reheat covered with a teaspoon of water and a knob of ghee, on low or in short bursts in the microwave. It stiffens when cold and loosens as it warms.

recipes.name: Zarda Pulao
recipes.subtitle: sweet saffron rice with dried fruit, served at weddings

ingredients.qty: a generous pinch, soaked in warm milk
ingredients.note: zarda means yellow; this is where it comes from

prepNotes: The rice is boiled first and only then met with sugar. Sugar added to raw rice stops it softening.
It should be dry and separate, not sticky. Zarda is a pulao, not a kheer.

steps.text: Boil the soaked rice in plenty of water with the cardamom and cloves until 80 per cent done. Drain well.
Fry the nuts and raisins in the ghee until golden and lift out.
Add the drained rice to the ghee with the saffron milk and fold gently.
Scatter the sugar over the top, cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat 12 minutes.
steps.tip: The sugar melts down through the rice. Do not stir it in or you will break the grains.

steps.text: Fold in the fried nuts, raisins and khoya with a fork.
Rest 10 minutes covered before serving.

recipes.name: Aam Doi
recipes.subtitle: mango folded into set yogurt, the summer version of mishti doi

ingredients.note: ripe and sweet, despite the ingredient name

prepNotes: Use a sweet, fibreless mango and pass the puree through a sieve. Fibres ruin the texture.
The mango carries a lot of water, so the yogurt has to be hung longer than for plain bhapa doi.

steps.text: Hang the yogurt 2 hours until quite firm.
Puree the mango and pass it through a sieve.
Whisk the yogurt with the condensed milk, cardamom and mango puree until even.
Pour into a dish, cover with foil and steam 20 minutes until just set at the edges.
Cool and refrigerate 4 hours before serving.
steps.tip: It sets in the fridge, not in the steamer. Do not overcook it looking for firmness.

recipes.name: Aloo Posto
recipes.subtitle: potatoes cooked down in a nutty poppy seed paste, mild and quietly rich

ingredients.note: posto. The whole point of the dish

ingredients.qty: 4, 2 ground with the posto and 2 slit

ingredients.note: kalonji
rounds off the bitterness of the poppy seeds

prepNotes: Soak the poppy seeds in just-boiled water for 30 minutes. Dry seeds will never grind smooth.
Drain the seeds well before grinding, then blend with 2 green chillies and 4 tbsp water to a thick, pale paste.
Cut the potatoes and keep them in cold water so they do not brown while the paste is going.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then take it off the heat for 30 seconds to lose its raw bite.
steps.tip: Bengali cooking almost always starts with mustard oil taken to smoking point.

steps.text: Return to medium heat, add the nigella seeds and let them sputter for 10 seconds.
Drain the potatoes, pat dry, and add them with the turmeric and salt. Fry 6-7 minutes, turning, until the edges are pale gold.
steps.tip: Dry potatoes fry; wet potatoes steam and go mushy.

steps.text: Pour in 180ml water, cover, and simmer 10-12 minutes until a knife slides through the potato with slight resistance.
Stir in the poppy seed paste and the slit green chillies. Cook uncovered on low for 6-8 minutes.
steps.tip: Keep the heat low. Posto catches and turns bitter over a high flame.

steps.text: The gravy is ready when it clings to the potatoes and you can see oil at the edge of the pan.
Add the sugar, check the salt, and finish with the remaining 1 tbsp raw mustard oil off the heat.
steps.tip: That last spoon of raw oil is what makes it taste Bengali rather than merely mild.

steps.text: Rest 5 minutes before serving with plain rice.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat gently with 2 tbsp water; the posto thickens hard as it cools.

recipes.name: Basanti Pulao
recipes.subtitle: sweet saffron-yellow ghee rice studded with cashews and raisins

ingredients.note: gobindobhog is traditional; basmati works if you shorten the cooking by 3 minutes
this, not the saffron, is what makes it yellow

ingredients.qty: a large pinch, soaked in 2 tbsp warm water

prepNotes: Wash the rice gently in three changes of water until it runs clear, then drain and spread it on a cloth for 30 minutes until the grains are dry to the touch.
Toss the dried rice with 2 tbsp of the ghee, the turmeric and 1 tsp salt and leave it 30 minutes. This coats each grain and keeps them separate.
Have the water hot on the side. Adding cold water to hot rice makes it break.

steps.text: Heat the remaining 2 tbsp ghee in a heavy pan and fry the cashews until golden, about 90 seconds. Lift out.
steps.tip: Cashews go from gold to burnt in about ten seconds. Watch them.

steps.text: Fry the raisins in the same ghee for 20 seconds until they swell, then lift them out too.
Add the bay leaves, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves and let them puff for 20 seconds.
Add the grated ginger and stir for 30 seconds.
Tip in the marinated rice and fry very gently for 3 minutes, folding rather than stirring.
steps.tip: Turmeric-coated rice grains are fragile. A flat spoon and slow folds keep them whole.

steps.text: Pour in 500ml hot water with the sugar, the saffron and its soaking water, and the rest of the salt.
Bring to a boil, then cover tightly and cook on the lowest possible heat for 12 minutes.

Roll tight, wrap the base in paper, and eat standing up.

steps.text: Boil the colocasia in salted water with the turmeric until completely soft, about 20 minutes. Drain thoroughly.
steps.tip: Thoroughly. Any water left makes a sloppy bata.

steps.text: Mash it smooth while hot, or pulse briefly in a blender.

Beat the mustard paste through the mash with the raw mustard oil and salt.

the perfume that marks a Kolkata biryani
for the potatoes

Layer rice over meat and potato, add the boiled eggs, and top with birista, saffron milk, kewra water and ghee.

recipes.subtitle: Mutton slow-fried in its own masala until almost dry and very dark

ingredients.note: for colour, a Bengali habit
optional but expected in Bengal

prepNotes: Kosha means to fry slowly and persistently. The dish is defined by that process, not by a sauce. You are looking for near-dry meat coated in dark masala.
Marinate the mutton in yogurt and turmeric for at least an hour; overnight is better.

steps.text: Marinate the mutton with yogurt, turmeric and salt for an hour.
Heat the mustard oil to smoking, cool slightly, then caramelise the sugar until it darkens. This is where the colour comes from.
steps.tip: Seconds, not minutes. Burnt sugar is bitter.

steps.text: Add the whole spices and sliced onion and fry until genuinely brown, 12-15 minutes.

steps.tip: Add a splash of hot water whenever it catches, and keep frying. This is the whole recipe.

steps.text: When the oil separates and the meat is deep brown, add just enough hot water to cover, cover the pan and simmer 30-40 minutes until tender.
Add the fried potatoes for the last 10 minutes, finish with garam masala, and reduce until the gravy clings.

recipes.name: Kumror Chokka
recipes.subtitle: sweet pumpkin and chickpeas tempered with panch phoron, cooked until the edges collapse

ingredients.note: or 250g tinned, drained and rinsed
use compounded-free hing to keep the dish gluten-free
for the finish

prepNotes: Soak the dried chickpeas overnight in plenty of water, then pressure-cook them with a little salt for 4 whistles. They should be tender but still hold their shape.
Choose a dense, sweet pumpkin. A watery one dissolves into soup; if yours is very ripe, cut the chunks a size larger.
Measure the panch phoron and chillies into a small bowl before you start. The tempering burns in seconds and there is no time to fetch things.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadhai to smoking point, then take it off the heat for half a minute to settle.
Fry the potato chunks with a pinch of the turmeric over medium heat for 5 minutes, until the edges are golden, then lift them out.
steps.tip: Frying the potato separately keeps it from breaking up later in the pumpkin.

steps.text: Into the same oil add the panch phoron, broken chillies and bay leaf and let them pop for about 20 seconds.

Add the turmeric, chilli, cumin and coriander powders with 2 tbsp water and fry this paste for 2 minutes, until the oil beads at the edges.
steps.tip: Spices added to a splash of water instead of dry oil will not scorch.

steps.text: Return the potato and add the pumpkin, cooked chickpeas, salt and sugar. Toss everything in the masala for 2 minutes.
Pour in 100ml water, cover, and cook on low for 15 minutes until the pumpkin gives way under a spoon.
Mash four or five pieces of pumpkin against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy, add the coconut and cook uncovered for 3 minutes.
steps.tip: This is what makes it a chokka: half mash, half chunks.

steps.text: Sprinkle over the garam masala, cover and rest 5 minutes off the heat before serving with luchi or rice.

recipes.name: Labra
recipes.subtitle: a soft mixed vegetable torkari fragrant with panch phoron and ginger

ingredients.note: the sweetness that holds labra together
for a gluten-free dish use compounded-free hing. Most brands are cut with wheat flour

prepNotes: Cut everything to roughly 3cm so the hard and soft vegetables finish at the same time.
Toast 1 tsp of the panch phoron in a dry pan and crush it. This goes in at the end as a finishing powder.
Labra wants to be stirred with a light hand; use a wide kadhai so you can fold rather than mash.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil to smoking in a wide kadhai, then reduce the heat.
Add the bay leaves, dried red chillies and the remaining 1/2 tsp whole panch phoron. Let them crackle 15 seconds.
steps.tip: The fenugreek in panch phoron turns bitter if it darkens past golden brown.

steps.text: Add the asafoetida and the grated ginger and stir for 30 seconds.
Tip in the potato and sweet potato and fry 4 minutes until the edges are translucent.
Add the pumpkin, raw banana, beans and cabbage with the turmeric, cumin powder and salt. Fold gently for 3 minutes.
Add the eggplant last, along with 200ml water. Cover and cook on low for 18-20 minutes.
steps.tip: Do not stir while it steams. Shake the pan by the handle instead.

steps.text: Uncover: the pumpkin should have collapsed and be binding everything into a rough mash.
steps.tip: That collapsing pumpkin is the texture you are after. If it still holds cubes, give it 5 more minutes covered.

steps.text: Cook uncovered 4-5 minutes to drive off the last of the water.
Stir in the sugar, garam masala and the crushed toasted panch phoron. Rest 5 minutes and serve with khichuri or rice.

recipes.name: Lau Ghonto
recipes.subtitle: bottle gourd cooked down to a soft mash with roasted moong dal and ghee

ingredients.note: dry-roasted, then rinsed
balances the gourd, do not leave it out
stirred in off the heat
optional, but the way most homes finish it

prepNotes: Dry-roast the moong dal in a hot pan for about 4 minutes, until it darkens a shade and smells nutty, then rinse and drain. That roasting is what makes this a ghonto rather than an ordinary gourd curry.
Taste a raw sliver of the bottle gourd before you commit to it. One in twenty is bitter, and a bitter lau will ruin the whole pot.
Bottle gourd throws off a lot of water. Add no extra liquid until the dal goes in, or the dish will never dry down.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it just begins to smoke, then pull it off the flame for 30 seconds.
steps.tip: Taking it to smoking point first burns off the raw pungency; skipping this leaves a harsh edge.

steps.text: Return the pan to medium heat and drop in the bay leaf and cumin seeds. They should crackle within 20 seconds.
Add the grated ginger and slit chillies and stir for 30 seconds, until the ginger smells sweet rather than raw.
Tip in the diced gourd with the turmeric and salt, stir to coat, then cover and cook on medium-low for 12 minutes.
steps.tip: The gourd should sweat out enough water to cook itself. Lift the lid only to stir, or you lose that steam.

steps.text: Uncover, add the roasted moong dal and the water, and simmer uncovered for 12 to 15 minutes until the dal is soft and the mixture mounds on a spoon.
Stir in the sugar and grated coconut and cook another 2 minutes, mashing a few pieces of gourd against the side of the pan to thicken it.
Take the pan off the heat, stir through the ghee and garam masala, and cover for 5 minutes before serving with plain rice.
steps.tip: Ghee added off the heat keeps its aroma; boiled into the dish it disappears.

recipes.name: Luchi
recipes.subtitle: small white maida puris that puff into balloons, the sunday-morning bread

ingredients.note: plain white flour. Atta makes a puri, not a luchi
the moyan, which keeps the luchi tender

prepNotes: Rub the ghee into the flour first and check it. A fistful should hold its shape when squeezed. That is the correct amount of moyan.
Knead to a dough firmer than chapati dough, then rest it covered with a damp cloth for 20 minutes.
Roll all the luchis out before you start frying and keep them under a cloth; frying goes too fast to roll between batches.

steps.text: Mix the maida, salt and sugar, then rub in the ghee with your fingertips for 2 minutes until it looks like damp sand.
Add the lukewarm water a little at a time and knead 6-8 minutes into a smooth, firm, non-sticky dough.
steps.tip: A soft dough will soak up oil. Luchi dough should feel tight, almost stubborn.

steps.text: Cover and rest 20 minutes.
Divide into 20 balls the size of a large marble and roll each into a 9cm circle, greasing the board with a drop of oil rather than dusting with flour.
steps.tip: Dry flour on the surface burns and clouds the frying oil. Always oil the board for luchi.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a deep kadhai to 180C. A scrap of dough should rise to the surface within 2 seconds.
Slide in one luchi. It will sink, then float within 3 seconds.
Press the centre down gently with the back of a slotted spoon for 3-4 seconds and it will balloon.
steps.tip: That gentle press is the trick to a full puff. Without it you get a flat disc.

steps.text: Flip and fry the second side 15 seconds only. Luchi should stay white and blond, never brown.
steps.tip: If they are colouring, your oil is too hot. Drop the heat between batches.

steps.text: Drain upright in a colander rather than flat on paper so they stay puffed.
Serve straight away with cholar dal or aloo dum.

recipes.storage: Luchi are at their best within 20 minutes. They will keep soft for a few hours in a covered container but will not re-puff; do not refrigerate.

recipes.name: Macher Jhol
recipes.subtitle: a thin turmeric and ginger fish broth built around fried rohu steaks

ingredients.qty: 600g rohu or katla, cut into 2cm cross-section steaks
ingredients.note: any firm freshwater fish on the bone

prepNotes: Rub the fish steaks with 1 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp salt then cover and refrigerate 15 minutes.
Pat the steaks completely dry before they go in the oil, or they will stick and tear.
Mix the remaining turmeric, chilli powder, cumin powder and ginger with 4 tbsp water into a loose paste so it does not scorch in the pan.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then lower to medium-high.
Slide in the fish steaks and fry 3 minutes a side until the surface is firm and browned.
steps.tip: Do not move the fish for the first 3 minutes. It releases from the pan when it is ready.

steps.text: Lift the fish out onto a plate and leave the oil in the pan.
Fry the potato wedges in the same oil for 5 minutes until golden at the edges, then add the eggplant for 2 minutes.
Push the vegetables aside, add the nigella seeds to the clear space and let them pop for 10 seconds.
Stir in the spice paste and fry 2-3 minutes until it darkens and stops smelling raw.
steps.tip: If it sticks, add a tablespoon of water rather than more oil.

steps.text: Add the tomato, slit chillies, 700ml water and salt. Bring to a boil and simmer 12 minutes until the potato is tender.
Return the fish steaks, spooning gravy over them, and simmer 4 minutes only.
steps.tip: Overcooked fish goes cottony. Four minutes is enough. It finished cooking in the frying stage.

steps.text: Turn off the heat, scatter the coriander, and rest 5 minutes before serving with plain rice.

recipes.name: Mishti Doi
recipes.subtitle: milk boiled down with caramelised jaggery and set into a thick fudgy curd

ingredients.qty: 150g, date palm (nolen gur) if you can get it, chopped

ingredients.note: for caramelising, which gives the colour

ingredients.qty: 3 tbsp, live and at room temperature
ingredients.note: the starter

prepNotes: Take the starter yogurt out of the fridge at least an hour ahead. Cold starter sets slowly and unevenly.
Soak an unglazed earthenware bowl in water for 30 minutes if you have one; the porous clay draws out moisture and gives mishti doi its texture.
Plan around the setting time: 6-8 hours undisturbed in a warm place after the cooking is done.

steps.text: Bring the milk to a boil in a heavy pan, then lower the heat and simmer 30-35 minutes, scraping the skin at the sides back in each time, until it reduces to about 900ml.
Meanwhile melt the 2 tbsp sugar in a small dry pan over medium heat until it turns the colour of dark honey, about 4 minutes.
steps.tip: Take it off the heat the moment it darkens. Burnt caramel makes the whole batch bitter.

steps.text: Stir the caramel into the reduced milk (it will hiss) and cook 2 minutes more.
Add the chopped jaggery and cardamom and stir off the heat until fully dissolved.
steps.tip: Add the jaggery off the heat. Boiling acidic jaggery into hot milk is the classic way to curdle it.

steps.text: Cool the milk to 45C. Warm to a fingertip but not hot enough to sting.
steps.tip: Too hot and you kill the culture; too cool and it never sets. Blood-warm is the target.

steps.text: Whisk the starter yogurt smooth in a cup, then whisk in a ladle of the warm milk.
Pour that back into the pan, stir twice only, and pour into the earthenware bowl or ramekins.
Cover and leave in a warm, draught-free place (a switched-off oven with the light on works well) for 6-8 hours without moving it.
steps.tip: Moving the bowl while it is setting breaks the curd and you get whey at the bottom.

steps.text: When it is set firm enough that the surface does not wobble as a whole, chill for at least 4 hours before serving.

recipes.storage: Keeps 4 days refrigerated, covered. Serve cold, straight from the setting bowl; it does not travel or freeze well.

recipes.name: Muri Ghonto
recipes.subtitle: fish head cooked down with rice and potato, the dish that wastes nothing

ingredients.qty: 1 large head, halved, plus 200g of steaks
ingredients.note: rohu or katla; the head is the dish, not a garnish
gobindobhog is traditional; any short fragrant rice works

prepNotes: The head is fried hard first and then broken up in the pot. That breaking is the technique.

steps.text: Rub the fish head with turmeric and salt and fry in the hot mustard oil until dark and crisp. Break it into pieces in the pan.
Fry the potato cubes until golden. Lift out.
Temper the bay leaves, add the onion and fry until brown, then the ginger paste and cumin.
Return the fish and potato, add the drained rice and toss 3 minutes so every grain is coated in oil.
Add 400ml hot water, cover and cook 15 minutes until the rice is done and almost dry.
Finish with the garam masala, green chillies and sugar. Rest 10 minutes.

recipes.name: Panch Mishali Chorchori
recipes.subtitle: five vegetables cooked dry in their own steam with panch phoron and ground mustard

ingredients.note: soaked, then ground to a paste

ingredients.qty: 3, one for the mustard paste and two slit
4 tbsp, added a spoon at a time

prepNotes: Soak the mustard seeds for 20 minutes in warm water with one green chilli and a pinch of salt, then grind to a fine paste with a little of that water. Ground dry, or ground too long, mustard turns bitter.
Cut every vegetable to roughly the same 5cm baton so they finish together. The radish and potato go in first because they are the slowest.
Chorchori is a dry dish cooked in the vegetables' own moisture. Keep a small cup of water beside the pan and add it a spoon at a time, only when the pan catches.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a wide kadhai until it smokes, then rest it off the heat for 30 seconds.
Add the panch phoron and dried chillies and let them crackle for 20 seconds.
steps.tip: A wide pan matters here. Crowded vegetables steam grey instead of catching colour.

steps.text: Add the potato and radish batons with the turmeric and salt and stir-fry uncovered for 5 minutes.
Add the pumpkin, beans and eggplant with the slit green chillies, toss well, then cover and cook on low for 10 minutes.
steps.tip: Do not stir more than twice or the batons break down into mush.

steps.text: Uncover and check: the vegetables should be nearly tender and the pan almost dry. Add a spoon of water only if it is sticking.
Stir in the mustard paste, chilli powder and sugar, and cook uncovered for 5 minutes so the raw mustard cooks off.
steps.tip: Keep the heat low once the mustard is in; boiled hard, it goes bitter.

steps.text: Raise the heat for a final 2 to 3 minutes to let the edges of the vegetables catch and brown a little.
Take off the heat, spoon over the last teaspoon of raw mustard oil if you like it sharp, and serve with rice and dal.

recipes.name: Patishapta
recipes.subtitle: thin rice-flour crepes rolled around coconut and jaggery, the sweet of poush month

ingredients.note: gives the crepe enough stretch to roll without tearing
nolen gur if you can get it, in which case use 175g
for a richer filling

prepNotes: Make the filling first and let it cool to just warm. Hot filling tears the crepe as you roll it.
Whisk the batter and rest it 30 minutes. Rice flour needs that time to hydrate or the crepes come out brittle at the edges.
The batter should coat the back of a spoon and run off in a thin, unbroken line, roughly the consistency of single cream. Add the water a tablespoon at a time if it is thicker.
Have a small bowl of ghee and a folded paper towel beside the tawa for wiping the pan between crepes.

steps.text: Cook the grated coconut with the jaggery in a kadhai over medium-low heat for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring, until the mixture pulls away from the sides in a single mass.
steps.tip: Jaggery liquefies first and then reduces. Stop while it is still moist; cooked hard it sets into candy.

steps.text: Stir in the khoya, 2 tbsp milk and half the cardamom and cook 3 minutes more, then spread the filling on a plate to cool.
Whisk the rice flour, maida, rava, sugar, salt and remaining cardamom with the milk until completely lump-free, then rest the batter 30 minutes.
Divide the cooled filling into 8 portions and shape each into a short log about 8cm long.
Heat a tawa over medium-low and wipe it with ghee. It is ready when a drop of batter sets in about 3 seconds without hissing violently.
steps.tip: Too hot and the crepe sets before it spreads; too cool and it sticks. Medium-low the whole way.

steps.text: Pour a small ladle of batter into the centre and spread it with the back of the ladle into a 15cm oval, thin at the edges.
Cook undisturbed for about 90 seconds, until the surface looks dry and matte and the edges lift away on their own.
steps.tip: Do not flip it. Patishapta is cooked on one side only.

steps.text: Lay a log of filling along one edge and roll the crepe over it into a tight cylinder using a spatula.
steps.tip: Roll while it is still on the hot tawa; off the heat it stiffens and cracks.

steps.text: Slide the roll onto a plate seam-side down and repeat, wiping the tawa with ghee between each.
Serve warm, or at room temperature with a spoonful of warmed nolen gur poured over.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in an airtight box in the fridge. Bring to room temperature and warm briefly on a dry tawa; do not microwave, which turns the crepes leathery.

recipes.name: Payesh
recipes.subtitle: rice cooked slowly down in milk with cardamom and date palm jaggery

ingredients.note: gobindobhog is traditional; any short-grain rice works
use 120g sugar instead if you cannot find it

prepNotes: Wash the rice and soak 20 minutes, then drain and toss with the 1 tsp ghee. This keeps the grains from clumping.
Use the heaviest pan you own and rinse it with water before adding the milk; the film of water stops the milk catching.
Chop the jaggery finely so it dissolves quickly at the end without needing extra heat.

steps.text: Bring the milk to a boil with the bay leaf and bruised cardamom, then lower to a bare simmer.
Simmer 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes and scraping the skin from the sides back in, until it has reduced by about a quarter.
steps.tip: Scrape the sides. The reduced milk stuck there is the best part of the payesh.

steps.text: Add the drained, ghee-coated rice and the pinch of salt.
Cook on low for 30-35 minutes, stirring every 3-4 minutes so nothing sticks, until the grains are completely soft and the milk has thickened to the consistency of pouring cream.
steps.tip: It thickens a lot more as it cools, so stop while it still looks loose.

steps.text: Fry the cashews and raisins in a dry pan for 90 seconds until the cashews are gold and the raisins swell.
Stir them into the payesh and cook 2 minutes more.
Take the pan off the heat and let it cool for 8-10 minutes. The surface should no longer be steaming hard.
steps.tip: This is the critical pause. Jaggery in hot milk will curdle the whole pot.

steps.text: Stir in the chopped jaggery and the sugar if using until fully dissolved. Do not put the pan back on the heat.
steps.tip: If it does split, whisk hard off the heat and it will usually come back together.

steps.text: Cool to room temperature, then chill at least 2 hours before serving.

recipes.name: Peyaji
recipes.subtitle: crisp onion fritters shot through with nigella and green chilli

ingredients.qty: 4 medium (about 400g), sliced as thin as you can

ingredients.note: this is what makes them stay crisp
optional, for a lighter fritter

prepNotes: Slice the onions along the grain into long thin strips. Rings fall apart in the oil.
Salt the sliced onions and leave 15 minutes; they will release enough water that you need almost none extra.
Mix the batter only 2 minutes before frying, or the onions weep and it turns soupy.

steps.text: Squeeze the salted onions lightly with your hands to bring out their water, keeping the liquid in the bowl.
steps.tip: That onion water is your only liquid. Do not throw it away and do not add tap water.

steps.text: Add the besan, rice flour, nigella, green chilli, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander leaves and mix with your fingers.
The mixture should just cling together in a ragged clump. Add 1 tsp water at a time only if it is genuinely dry.
steps.tip: A loose batter gives you a pancake instead of a fritter. Err on the dry side.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then bring it down to a steady 170C.
Drop in irregular clumps the size of a walnut, six or seven at a time.
steps.tip: Craggy shapes fry crisper than neat balls. Do not pat them smooth.

steps.text: Fry 4-5 minutes, turning once at the halfway point, until deep amber and no longer bubbling hard.
steps.tip: The bubbling slowing down tells you the moisture has cooked out and they will be crisp.

steps.text: Lift onto a wire rack, not paper, so the undersides stay crisp.
Fry the next batch, letting the oil come back up to temperature between batches, and serve hot with rice and dal or on their own with mustard.

recipes.storage: Best within 30 minutes of frying. Leftovers can be re-crisped in a hot oven for 5 minutes but never in a microwave.

recipes.name: Potoler Dorma
recipes.subtitle: hollowed pointed gourd stuffed with paneer and coconut in a delicate poppy seed gravy

ingredients.qty: 8 large, about 500g, lightly scraped and hollowed

ingredients.note: soaked, then ground to a smooth paste
for the stuffing
use compounded-free hing to keep the dish gluten-free
for colour without heat

prepNotes: Soak the poppy seeds in warm water for 30 minutes before grinding, or the paste stays gritty no matter how long you blend it.
Scoop the potol out with the handle of a small spoon, working from the cut end. Keep the scooped flesh, chop it fine and add it to the stuffing.
Whisk the yogurt smooth and leave it out of the fridge for 20 minutes. Cold yogurt splits the moment it hits a hot pan.
Stuff the gourds while the filling is still warm and pliable, and pack it firmly so they do not empty out in the gravy.

steps.text: Rub the hollowed gourds with 1/4 tsp turmeric and a little salt and leave 10 minutes, then pat dry.

Heat 2 tbsp mustard oil and fry the crumbled paneer with the ginger, minced chillies, coconut, raisins, chopped gourd flesh, a pinch of salt and 1/4 tsp garam masala for 5 minutes, until dry and crumbly. Cool slightly.
steps.tip: The stuffing must be dry. Wet filling turns the gourd soggy and leaks into the gravy.

steps.text: Pack the stuffing tightly into the gourds, pressing it in with the back of a teaspoon.
Heat the remaining mustard oil to smoking, cool it 30 seconds, then shallow-fry the stuffed gourds for 5 to 6 minutes, turning carefully, until blistered and golden. Lift out.
steps.tip: Turn them with two spoons rather than tongs, which split the skin.

steps.text: Into the same oil add the bay leaf, cumin seeds, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves, then the asafoetida, and let them crackle 20 seconds.
Add the pureed tomato with the turmeric, kashmiri chilli, cumin and coriander powders and cook for 5 minutes until the oil separates.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the whisked yogurt, then return it to the lowest flame and cook for 3 minutes without letting it boil.
steps.tip: Off the heat first, then low: this is the only reliable way to keep yogurt from splitting.

steps.text: Stir in the poppy seed paste, the sugar and salt, and cook 2 minutes more.
Pour in the water, bring to a bare simmer, then slide the stuffed gourds in and cook covered on low for 12 minutes, spooning gravy over them twice.
Finish with the ghee and remaining garam masala and rest 5 minutes before serving with basanti pulao or luchi.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat covered on low with 2 tbsp water; do not stir once the gourds are in the pan or they will break apart.

recipes.name: Radhaballavi
recipes.subtitle: puffed white bread stuffed with fennel-scented ground urad dal

ingredients.note: soaked 4 hours, then ground coarse
for the moyan, worked into the flour

prepNotes: Soak the urad dal 4 hours, then drain well and grind it coarse with the green chillies and almost no water. A wet paste will not dry out in the pan and the bread will tear.
Rub the ghee into the maida until the flour holds its shape when squeezed, then bring it together with water into a soft dough and rest it 30 minutes under a damp cloth.
Cook the filling until it is properly dry and crumbly, then cool it completely. Warm filling steams inside the dough and blows holes in the bread.

steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp of the frying oil in a pan, add the asafoetida, crushed fennel seeds and grated ginger, and let them fizz for 20 seconds.
Add the ground dal with the fennel powder, dry ginger, cumin, chilli powder, sugar and salt, and cook on low for 10 to 12 minutes, breaking up lumps, until it is dry and sandy.
steps.tip: It is ready when a pinch of it holds together but leaves no smear on your fingers.

steps.text: Spread the filling on a plate to cool completely, then divide it into 12 balls.
Knead the rested dough for a minute and divide it into 12 equal balls.
Flatten each dough ball into a 7cm disc with a thicker centre, place a ball of filling in the middle and gather the edges over the top, pinching them shut.
steps.tip: Thicker in the centre, thinner at the rim: that is what lets you roll it out without the filling breaking through.

steps.text: Rest the stuffed balls seam-side down for 10 minutes, then roll each gently into a 10cm disc using oil, not flour, on the board.
steps.tip: Dry flour on the surface burns and darkens the frying oil within two batches.

steps.text: Heat the remaining oil in a kadhai to 180C. A scrap of dough should rise to the surface in about 3 seconds.
Slide in one radhaballavi, press it lightly under the oil with a slotted spoon for 5 seconds, and it will balloon.
steps.tip: That gentle press is what makes it puff. Without it you get a flat, greasy bread.

steps.text: Fry 40 seconds a side, until pale gold rather than brown, and lift onto a rack.
steps.tip: Radhaballavi should stay white and soft. Deep brown means the oil is too hot.

steps.text: Repeat with the rest, keeping the oil steady between batches, and serve hot with alur dom.

recipes.storage: Best within an hour of frying. The filling keeps 3 days refrigerated and the dough 24 hours; assemble and fry fresh rather than reheating fried bread.

recipes.name: Rasgulla
recipes.subtitle: Chhena dumplings boiled in light syrup until they double and turn spongy

ingredients.note: not UHT. It will not curdle cleanly
or 3 tbsp vinegar
omit to keep it gluten-free; handle the balls gently

prepNotes: Everything depends on the chhena: drained enough to hold, moist enough to knead smooth. Squeeze it dry and the rasgulla turns rubbery.
The syrup must be thin. A thick syrup cannot penetrate the dumpling and it stays raw in the middle.

steps.text: Bring the milk to a boil, take it off the heat, and add lemon juice a little at a time until the curds separate cleanly from greenish whey.
Strain through muslin and rinse under cold water to wash out the acid. Hang 30 minutes, no longer.
steps.tip: Rinsing matters; unrinsed chhena tastes of lemon.

steps.text: Knead the chhena on a plate with the heel of your hand for 8-10 minutes, until it goes from grainy to smooth and slightly greasy. Work in the maida if using.
steps.tip: This is the step people cut short, and it is why rasgullas crack.

steps.text: Roll into 12 crack-free balls, smaller than you want them finished, they double.
Bring the sugar and water to a rolling boil with the cardamom. Slide the balls in, cover, and boil hard for 15 minutes.
steps.tip: Hard boil, lid on. A gentle simmer will not inflate them.

steps.text: Cool in the syrup, add rose water, and chill at least 4 hours before serving.

recipes.storage: Keeps 4 days refrigerated in its syrup, and the texture is best from the second day. Do not freeze.

recipes.name: Rasmalai
recipes.subtitle: flattened chhena discs simmered in syrup then steeped in thickened saffron milk

ingredients.qty: 2 litres, plus 1 litre for the rabri

ingredients.note: to split the milk

prepNotes: Chhena for rasmalai must be kneaded until it is genuinely smooth and slightly greasy to the touch. Grainy chhena gives grainy discs.
The discs double in the syrup, so leave room in the pan and do not crowd them.

steps.text: Bring 2 litres of milk to the boil, take it off the heat, and add lemon juice a little at a time until it splits cleanly.
steps.tip: Stop as soon as the whey runs clear green. Extra acid makes the chhena tough.

steps.text: Strain through muslin, rinse under cold water to wash off the lemon, and hang 30 minutes.
Knead the chhena on a board for 8 minutes until completely smooth and it leaves a slight film on your palm.
steps.tip: Eight minutes is not an exaggeration. This is the whole dish.

steps.text: Shape into 12 balls, flatten each into a disc, and rest 10 minutes.
Simmer them in a light syrup of 300g sugar to 1 litre water, covered, for 15 minutes. They will swell.
Separately reduce 1 litre of milk by half with saffron, cardamom and sugar to make the rabri.
Squeeze the discs gently to remove the syrup and slip them into the warm rabri.
steps.tip: Squeeze gently or they tear. This is what lets them drink the milk.

steps.text: Chill 4 hours and serve cold, scattered with pistachios.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and improves overnight as the discs absorb the milk. Does not freeze.

recipes.name: Rui Macher Kalia
recipes.subtitle: fried rohu steaks in a deep onion and ginger gravy, the wedding-lunch fish curry

ingredients.note: 1/2 tsp of it for rubbing the fish

prepNotes: Rub the fish steaks with 1/2 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp salt and leave them 15 minutes, then pat the surface dry before frying.
The oil must be at smoking point before the fish goes in, and the pan must not be moved for the first 2 minutes. That is the only way fish skin does not stick.
Whisk the yogurt and leave it at room temperature; straight from the fridge it will curdle in the gravy.

steps.text: Heat 5 tbsp mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes.
Slide in the fish steaks, two or three at a time, and fry 3 minutes on the first side without touching them, then 2 minutes on the second. Lift out onto a plate.
steps.tip: Move a piece before it has set and you will leave the skin behind in the pan.

steps.text: Fry the potato quarters in the same oil for 6 minutes until golden, then set aside with the fish.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil, then the bay leaves, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves, and let them crackle for 20 seconds.
Add the onion paste and cook on medium for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring often, until it is deep gold and no longer smells raw.
steps.tip: This long fry is the difference between a kalia and a weeknight jhol. Do not rush it.

steps.text: Stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and cook 2 minutes more.
Add the pureed tomato with the turmeric, kashmiri chilli, chilli, cumin and coriander powders and cook 6 to 7 minutes, until the oil pulls away to the sides of the pan.
Take the pan off the heat, beat in the yogurt, then cook on the lowest flame for 3 minutes without boiling.
Add the water, sugar, salt, slit chillies and the fried potatoes, and simmer covered for 12 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Slide the fish back in, spoon gravy over each piece, and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes. Do not stir.
steps.tip: Tilt and swirl the pan instead of stirring, or the steaks will break up.

steps.text: Finish with the ghee and garam masala, cover and rest 10 minutes before serving with rice.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat on low in a wide pan, swirling rather than stirring, and add 2 tbsp water to loosen the gravy.

recipes.name: Sandesh
recipes.subtitle: fresh chhena kneaded with sugar into a soft barely-cooked milk sweet

ingredients.qty: 3 tbsp juice, mixed with 3 tbsp water
ingredients.note: for curdling

ingredients.qty: a few strands, for pressing on top
2 litres cold, for rinsing the chhena

prepNotes: Have a colander lined with a double layer of muslin ready over a bowl before you start heating the milk.
Use diluted lemon juice, not neat. Neat acid makes tough, rubbery chhena.
The chhena must hang 30 minutes and no longer. Over-drained chhena will not knead smooth.
Powder the sugar in advance; granulated sugar leaves a gritty sandesh.

steps.text: Bring the milk to a full boil in a heavy pan, then turn the heat off completely.
Wait 60 seconds, then add the diluted lemon juice a spoonful at a time, stirring slowly, until the curds separate and the whey runs pale green.
steps.tip: Add the acid only as far as you need. The instant the whey turns clear, stop.

steps.text: Pour into the muslin-lined colander and rinse the curds under cold water for 30 seconds to wash off the lemon and stop the cooking.
steps.tip: Skipping the cold rinse leaves the sandesh tasting sour.

steps.text: Gather the muslin, squeeze gently, and hang for 30 minutes.
Tip the chhena onto a clean surface and knead with the heel of your hand for 8-10 minutes until it goes from grainy to completely smooth and slightly greasy.
steps.tip: This kneading is the entire recipe. Under-knead and you get crumbs, not sandesh.

steps.text: Work in the powdered sugar and cardamom and knead 2 minutes more.
Transfer to a non-stick pan and cook on the lowest heat for 6-8 minutes, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens and pulls away from the sides in a mass.
steps.tip: Stop while it still looks slightly wet. Cooked a minute too long, sandesh turns dry and chalky.

steps.text: Spread on a plate and cool 15 minutes until it is comfortable to handle but still warm.
Divide into 12 while still warm, roll each into a ball and flatten slightly, pressing a strand of saffron or a thumbprint into the top.
Cool completely before serving.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated in an airtight box. Bring back to room temperature for 20 minutes before eating; fridge-cold sandesh tastes of nothing.

recipes.name: Shorshe Ilish
recipes.subtitle: Hilsa poached in a raw mustard paste, the dish Bengal argues about most

ingredients.note: any oily river fish; do not skin it
not negotiable here

prepNotes: Mustard turns bitter if the paste is ground hot or too long. Soak the seeds, add a green chilli and a pinch of salt, and grind in short bursts.
Hilsa is full of fine bones and is eaten carefully rather than filleted. Do not substitute a boneless fillet and expect the same dish.

steps.text: Soak the mustard seeds 20 minutes in warm water, then grind with 2 green chillies and a pinch of salt to a smooth paste. Strain if you want it silky.
steps.tip: Short bursts. Overgrinding is what makes mustard bitter.

steps.text: Rub the fish with turmeric and salt and rest 10 minutes.
Heat the mustard oil until it just smokes, then take it off the heat for a moment. This removes the raw pungency.
Return to low heat, add the nigella, then the mustard paste thinned with half a cup of water, the remaining chillies and salt. Simmer 3 minutes.
steps.tip: Do not brown the paste; this is a raw mustard sauce, not a bhuna.

steps.text: Slide in the fish in a single layer, spoon the sauce over, cover and cook 8 minutes. Do not stir, shake the pan.
Finish with a tablespoon of raw mustard oil poured over, and rest 5 minutes before serving with plain rice.

recipes.storage: Eat the same day. Hilsa firms unpleasantly on reheating and mustard sauces turn bitter overnight. Do not freeze.

recipes.name: Shukto
recipes.subtitle: a gently bitter mixed vegetable stew in milk, eaten first with rice

ingredients.note: the shukto in shukto. Do not leave it out

ingredients.qty: 1, peeled and cut into thick batons
1 tsp, ground to a paste with 2 tbsp water

ingredients.note: adds body to the gravy

prepNotes: Soak the poppy seeds in hot water 30 minutes, then grind with the mustard seeds and 2 tbsp water.
Cut all the vegetables to roughly the same length so they finish together.
Have the milk out of the fridge. Cold milk added to a hot pan is more likely to split.

steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp mustard oil to smoking, cool slightly, then fry the bitter gourd rounds 3-4 minutes until browned at the edges. Lift out and set aside.
steps.tip: Frying the bitter gourd separately keeps its bitterness pleasant rather than dominating.

steps.text: In the same oil, fry the eggplant and raw banana for 3 minutes until just coloured. Set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil, the bay leaf and the panch phoron, and let it crackle for 15 seconds.
steps.tip: Panch phoron burns fast, count the seconds.

steps.text: Add the ginger paste and cook 30 seconds until it smells sweet rather than raw.
Add the drumstick, radish and sweet potato with the salt and 300ml water. Cover and simmer 12 minutes.
Return the fried vegetables to the pan and simmer uncovered 5 minutes more.
Stir the mustard and poppy paste into the milk, then pour it in and bring to the barest simmer.
steps.tip: Never let it boil once the mustard paste is in. Boiling turns mustard sharply bitter.

steps.text: Cook 4-5 minutes until the gravy is the thickness of single cream.
Add the sugar and crushed fennel, taste for salt, and finish with the ghee off the heat.
Rest 10 minutes. Shukto is served slightly warm, not piping hot, at the start of the meal.

recipes.storage: Best eaten the day it is made. It will keep 1 day refrigerated; reheat over low heat without boiling.

recipes.name: Aloo Parwal ki Tarkari
recipes.subtitle: dry pointed gourd and potato sabzi tempered with panch phoron and mustard oil

ingredients.note: added at the end

prepNotes: Scrape the parwal skin lightly with a knife rather than peeling it; the ridged skin holds the sabzi together.
Cut the potato fingers the same length as the parwal halves so they cook in step.
Keep the panch phoron measured out by the stove. It goes in and burns fast.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes lightly, then drop the flame to medium.
Add the panch phoron and wait 20 seconds for the fenugreek to darken and the fennel to smell sweet.
steps.tip: Fenugreek in panch phoron turns bitter if it goes past brown. Move fast.

steps.text: Throw in the crushed garlic and green chillies and fry 40 seconds until the garlic is pale gold.
Add the potato fingers and fry 5 minutes, turning, until the edges are translucent and starting to colour.
Add the parwal and fry a further 5 minutes until the cut faces are blistered and browned in patches.
steps.tip: Those browned faces are the flavour. Do not stir constantly or nothing colours.

steps.text: Sprinkle over the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt and toss for 1 minute.
Add the 4 tbsp water, cover and cook on low for 10 minutes, shaking the pan twice.
steps.tip: Cover but do not add more water. This is a dry sabzi and steam from the vegetables is enough.

steps.text: Uncover, check that a knife slides through the potato, and cook off any remaining moisture for 2 minutes.
Stir through the amchur and coriander leaves, rest 2 minutes and serve with roti or dal-bhaat.

recipes.name: Aloo ki Bhujia
recipes.subtitle: dry potato fingers tempered with panch phoron and mustard oil, crisp at the edges and no onion in sight

ingredients.note: the Bihari five-spice temper of fenugreek, nigella, cumin, fennel and mustard seed
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free
for a sour finish

prepNotes: Cut the potatoes into even 5mm fingers and rinse off the surface starch, then dry them thoroughly on a cloth. Wet potato steams instead of frying.
Have the panch phoron measured out by the pan. It burns within seconds of going into hot mustard oil.
Peeling is optional; thin-skinned new potatoes are better left unpeeled here.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes faintly, then drop the heat to medium.
steps.tip: Take mustard oil to smoking point every time. Unheated, it leaves a raw bitterness through the whole dish.

steps.text: Crackle the panch phoron and broken red chillies for 15-20 seconds, until the fenugreek seeds darken and the mustard seeds start popping.
steps.tip: The moment the fenugreek goes past brown it turns bitter; pull the pan off the heat if it is moving too fast.

steps.text: Add the asafoetida, swirl once, then tip in the potato fingers and 3/4 tsp salt.
Toss to coat and spread the potatoes in one layer. Fry undisturbed 4 minutes, then turn and fry 4 minutes more.
Sprinkle over the turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder and toss gently to coat every piece.
Cover and cook on low for 8 minutes, shaking the pan twice, until a potato finger crushes easily against the side.
steps.tip: Shake the pan rather than stirring with a spoon, or the fingers break into mash.

steps.text: Uncover, raise the heat and fry a final 3-4 minutes until the edges are golden and crisped.
Add the slit green chillies and amchur, toss, and finish off the heat with coriander leaves. Serve with dal and rice or with hot puris.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat in a dry pan over high heat for 3-4 minutes to bring the crisp edges back. A microwave leaves it limp.

recipes.name: Anarsa
recipes.subtitle: ghee-fried discs of soaked ground rice and jaggery, crusted with sesame

ingredients.qty: 600 ml, for deep-frying, plus 2 tbsp for the dough

ingredients.note: for coating
only if the dough will not come together
traditional in some households in place of half the sesame

prepNotes: Soak the rice in cold water for 3 days, changing the water every morning and evening, then drain it and spread it on a cloth in the shade for 2 hours until damp-dry, not crisp.
Grind the damp rice to a fine flour and sieve it; any coarse grit will tear the discs in the oil.
Mix the dough and rest it covered for at least 24 hours, and up to 4 days. This rest is what gives anarsa its honeycomb inside, and it cannot be skipped.
Have the sesame in a wide plate and your hands greased before you shape.

steps.text: Rub the grated jaggery into the ground rice flour with your fingertips until it looks like damp sand, 5 minutes.
steps.tip: No water. The moisture in the jaggery and the damp flour is all the dough gets.

steps.text: Work in 2 tbsp ghee and the crushed cardamom and knead to a stiff dough that just holds when squeezed; add the milk a teaspoon at a time only if it crumbles.
Cover and rest the dough at room temperature for 24 hours, by which time it will have softened and smell faintly fermented.
Pinch off lime-sized balls, press each one into the plate of sesame, and flatten to a 7cm disc about 6mm thick, sesame side up.
steps.tip: Keep them thick. Thin anarsa disintegrates the moment it hits the ghee.

steps.text: Heat the ghee in a kadhai to a gentle 160C. A crumb of dough should rise slowly with fine bubbles, not fizz.
steps.tip: Anarsa is fried low and slow. Hot ghee browns the jaggery before the middle cooks.

steps.text: Slide in one disc, sesame side down, and fry undisturbed for 90 seconds until it lifts and floats.
Spoon hot ghee over the top rather than turning it, and fry a further 3 to 4 minutes until deep reddish-brown and the bubbling slows.
steps.tip: Fry two at a time at most. Crowding drops the temperature and they break apart.

steps.text: Lift each anarsa out with a slotted spoon and stand it on edge against the side of a colander to drain for 5 minutes.
Cool completely before eating. They crisp as they cool and are fragile while hot.

recipes.storage: Stores 2 weeks in an airtight tin at room temperature. Do not refrigerate; the jaggery weeps and the discs go soft.

recipes.name: Bafauri
recipes.subtitle: steamed chana dal dumplings, the light cousin of the fried snack
prepNotes: Steamed, not fried, which makes it the rare Bihari snack you can eat a lot of.
Grind the dal coarse. A smooth paste steams into something rubbery.

steps.text: Drain the dal and grind coarse with almost no water. It should still have grit to it.
Mix in the onion, green chilli, ginger, coriander, ajwain, turmeric, asafoetida, oil and salt.
Shape into balls the size of a lime with wet hands.
Steam 20 minutes until firm and a skewer comes out clean.
steps.tip: Steam, do not boil. Boiled bafauri falls apart.

steps.text: Rest 5 minutes before lifting them off, and serve with a sharp chutney.

recipes.name: Baingan Chokha
recipes.subtitle: fire-roasted aubergine mashed with raw mustard oil, garlic and green chilli

ingredients.note: the fat purple kind, not the slim ones
4 pushed into the aubergine, 4 crushed raw
adds sweetness and body

prepNotes: Take the mustard oil out and leave it at room temperature. It goes in raw, so it should not be fridge-cold.
Cut four deep slits in each aubergine and push a garlic clove into each one before roasting.
Chop the onion, chilli and coriander while the aubergines roast; the chokha is mashed and eaten within minutes.

steps.text: Rub the aubergines with a few drops of oil and set them straight on a medium gas flame.
Roast 18 to 22 minutes, turning every few minutes, until the skin is blistered black all over and the flesh has collapsed inward.
steps.tip: It is ready when the aubergine sags and a skewer meets no resistance at the stem end. Underdone chokha tastes soapy.

steps.text: Roast the tomato on the flame alongside for the last 6 minutes until its skin splits and blackens.
Rest the aubergines 5 minutes, then peel off every scrap of charred skin. Do not rinse them under the tap or you wash the smoke away.
steps.tip: Peel with your fingers over a plate, not under running water.

steps.text: Mash the flesh coarsely with a fork along with the roasted tomato; leave some texture rather than making a puree.
Crush the 4 raw garlic cloves to a rough paste with a pinch of salt and stir them through.
Fold in the onion, green chilli, coriander leaves, salt and the raw mustard oil.
steps.tip: Add the mustard oil last and do not heat it. The raw pungency is the whole point of chokha.

steps.text: Squeeze over the lemon, taste for salt and serve at room temperature with litti, roti or rice and dal.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated in a covered box. Bring back to room temperature before serving and refresh with a teaspoon of raw mustard oil; it does not reheat well.

recipes.name: Bihari Khichdi
recipes.subtitle: loose moong dal and rice khichdi eaten with ghee, chokha and pickle

ingredients.note: 2 tbsp for the tadka, 2 tbsp spooned over at the table
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free
the winter version; skip in summer

prepNotes: Rinse the rice and dal together until the water runs almost clear, then leave them to soak 20 minutes. It makes the khichdi break down properly.
Dry-roast the moong dal in a pan for 2 minutes before rinsing if you want the nuttier Mithila version.
Have the chokha and pickle on the table first; khichdi is served the moment it comes off the heat.

steps.text: Drain the soaked rice and dal well.
Heat 2 tbsp ghee in the pressure cooker and crackle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds until they darken a shade.
Add the asafoetida, broken red chillies and bay leaf and fry 10 seconds. The hing should foam and smell sharp.
Stir in the ginger and green chilli and fry 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the cauliflower and peas if using and fry 3 minutes until the florets pick up a little colour.
Tip in the drained rice and dal with the turmeric and fry 2 minutes, stirring, until every grain is coated in ghee.
steps.tip: This short fry stops the khichdi turning gluey.

steps.text: Pour in the water, add salt, close the cooker and cook on high for 3 whistles, then off the heat for 10 minutes.
steps.tip: Do not force the pressure down. The khichdi finishes softening in the residual steam.

steps.text: Open the cooker and stir hard for 30 seconds; it should be loose enough to pour off a spoon. Add hot water a splash at a time if it has set.
steps.tip: Bihari khichdi is deliberately sloppy, not fluffy. Err on the wet side.

steps.text: Serve into bowls and spoon the remaining ghee over each portion at the table, with chokha, papad and pickle alongside.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. It sets solid when cold. Reheat on the stovetop with 100 ml hot water per portion, stirring until it pours again.

recipes.name: Bihari Malpua
recipes.subtitle: fennel-scented flour pancakes fried in ghee with lace-crisp edges, steeped in light sugar syrup

ingredients.note: gives a richer, softer malpua

ingredients.qty: 300g for the syrup, plus 2 tbsp for the batter

ingredients.note: the defining flavour. Do not leave it out

ingredients.qty: a pinch, soaked in 1 tbsp warm milk

prepNotes: Rest the batter at least 30 minutes, and up to 2 hours. Unrested batter spreads thin and the malpua turn leathery.
Make the syrup first and keep it warm on the lowest flame. Malpua must go from the frying pan into warm syrup, not cold.
Bring the milk to room temperature before mixing, so the batter comes together without lumps.

steps.text: Boil the 300g sugar with 150ml water for 5-6 minutes to a thin one-string syrup, stir in the saffron milk, and keep it warm over the lowest heat.
steps.tip: Stop well short of thick. A heavy syrup coats the malpua in a hard crust instead of soaking in.

steps.text: Whisk the maida with the grated khoya, 2 tbsp sugar, crushed fennel and ground cardamom.
Add the milk in three additions, whisking to a smooth, lump-free batter the consistency of thick pouring cream.
Cover and rest the batter 30 minutes, then check it. It should ribbon off the spoon and settle back in about 3 seconds.
steps.tip: If it is too thick the malpua will be doughy in the middle; loosen with a tablespoon of milk at a time.

steps.text: Heat 2cm of ghee in a small kadhai over medium heat until a drop of batter rises at once with a fizz.
Pour in a ladleful of batter from a height of about 10cm so it spreads into a 10cm round with frilled edges. Fry two at a time at most.
steps.tip: Pouring from a height is what makes the lace edge; dropping the batter close gives a flat thick pancake.

steps.text: Fry for 2 minutes without touching it, until the edges turn golden and lift on their own.
Turn once with a slotted spoon and fry the second side 90 seconds, spooning hot ghee over the centre.
Lift out, drain for a few seconds, then slide straight into the warm syrup and soak 4-5 minutes a side.
steps.tip: Hot malpua into warm syrup. Either one cold and it will not absorb.

steps.text: Lift out of the syrup and serve warm, with rabri or on their own.

recipes.storage: Best the day they are made. They keep 2 days refrigerated in a little of the syrup; warm them 20 seconds in a pan over low heat before serving, as cold malpua are dense.

recipes.name: Bihari Murgh Jhor
recipes.subtitle: thin, fiery home-style chicken curry cooked down in mustard oil with potatoes

ingredients.note: the standard Bihari addition; leave out for a leaner curry

prepNotes: Rub the chicken with the turmeric, half the salt and 1 tbsp of the mustard oil then cover and refrigerate it 30 minutes.
Have the hot water standing by. This curry is built by adding hot, never cold, water.
Chop the onions fine rather than slicing; they need to melt into the gravy.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil until it smokes lightly, then take it off the flame for 30 seconds to settle.
steps.tip: Smoking kills the pungency and leaves the nutty note you want.

steps.text: Fry the potato halves for 5 minutes until golden on the cut faces, then lift them out and set aside.
Crackle the cumin seeds, bay leaves and black cardamom in the same oil for 30 seconds.
Add the onion and fry on medium for 12 minutes until it is properly brown and pulling away from the pan.
steps.tip: Undercooked onion is why home chicken curry tastes flat. Wait for the colour.

steps.text: Stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and fry 2 minutes until the raw smell goes.
Add the tomato, chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder and cook 6 minutes until the tomato collapses and oil beads at the edge.
Tip in the chicken and fry on high for 8 minutes, turning the pieces, until they are sealed and coated in dark masala.
steps.tip: Do not add water at this stage. The chicken has to sear, not steam.

steps.text: Return the potatoes, pour in the hot water, add the green chillies and salt, and bring to a boil.
Simmer uncovered for 18 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the gravy has reduced by about a third. It should stay thin and pourable.
Stir in the garam masala, scatter the coriander leaves and rest 5 minutes before serving with rice or roti.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. Reheat on the stovetop with a little hot water; it thickens overnight and needs loosening.

recipes.name: Champaran Ahuna Mutton
recipes.subtitle: handi mutton sealed with dough and slow-cooked in mustard oil with whole garlic

image.alt: Champaran-style mutton in a dark garlic gravy

ingredients.qty: 1 kg, bone-in shoulder and leg, cut into 4cm pieces
ingredients.note: ask for a mix of meat and bone

ingredients.qty: 2 whole bulbs: 1 broken into peeled cloves, 1 crushed to a paste

ingredients.note: the local ones are mild; use 4 if yours are hot

ingredients.qty: 1 cup, made into a stiff dough with water
ingredients.note: for sealing the lid; discard after cooking
to finish

prepNotes: Marinate the mutton with the yogurt, both pastes, turmeric, chilli powder and salt for at least 2 hours, or overnight in the fridge.
Take the meat out 30 minutes before cooking so it is not fridge-cold going into the pot.
Knead the atta into a firm rope of dough while the marinade sits. You need it ready the moment the pot goes on dum.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a heavy pot until it thins and stops smelling sharp, about 3 minutes, then cool it slightly.
steps.tip: Raw mustard oil tastes bitter. Smoking it first is not optional here.

steps.text: Fry the bay leaves, cinnamon, cloves, black cardamom and whole dried chillies for 40 seconds until they swell and smell toasty.
Add the sliced onion and cook on medium until deep brown at the edges, 15 to 18 minutes.
steps.tip: Brown, not black. Pull it off the moment the edges darken.

steps.text: Tip in the whole peeled garlic cloves and fry 3 minutes until they turn pale gold and lose their raw bite.
Add the marinated mutton and fry hard on high heat for 12 minutes, stirring, until the yogurt dries off and the oil separates at the sides.
steps.tip: This is the stage that builds the colour. If it looks pale, keep going.

steps.text: Stir in the coriander powder and cook 2 minutes more, splashing in a tablespoon of water if it catches.
Pour in the 100 ml water, taste for salt, and bring to a hard boil for 2 minutes.
Press the rope of dough around the rim, clamp the lid on and cook on the lowest heat for 75 minutes without opening it.
steps.tip: Put a tawa under the pot if your smallest flame still runs hot.

steps.text: Crack the seal, discard the dough, and check the meat. It should slide off the bone under a spoon. If not, reseal and give it 15 minutes more.
Scatter over the garam masala and coriander leaves, stir once, and rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and tastes better on day two. Reheat gently on the stovetop with a splash of hot water; do not microwave on high or the meat tightens.

recipes.name: Dahi Chura Gud
recipes.subtitle: beaten rice softened in cold yogurt with jaggery, the Makar Sankranti breakfast

ingredients.note: thin poha dissolves; you need the thick flakes
sweet-set dahi, not sour
loosens it if your yogurt is very thick
only if the jaggery is mild

prepNotes: Rinse the poha in a colander under cold running water for 15 seconds, then leave it to drain for 10 minutes. That soak is all the softening it gets.
Chill the yogurt properly; this dish is eaten cold and lukewarm dahi makes it heavy.
Break the jaggery into small shards rather than one lump so every mouthful gets some.

steps.text: Rinse the thick poha in a colander under cold water and shake it dry.
steps.tip: Fifteen seconds under the tap, no longer. Poha left sitting in water turns to paste.

steps.text: Let it drain and swell for 10 minutes; the flakes should be soft enough to crush between two fingers but still separate.
Whisk the chilled yogurt smooth in a large bowl with a pinch of salt.
Loosen it with the cold milk if it is stiff. You want the consistency of thin cream.
Fold the drained poha into the yogurt and leave it 5 minutes to absorb.
steps.tip: Fold, do not beat. The flakes should stay recognisable.

steps.text: Taste and stir in the sugar only if the mixture is flat.
Serve into bowls with a generous pile of jaggery shards on the side of each portion, to be broken off and eaten with each spoonful.
steps.tip: The jaggery goes alongside, not stirred in. The contrast of cold sour dahi and sharp sweet gud is the dish.

recipes.storage: Assemble and eat within an hour; the poha keeps swelling and the yogurt turns sour. Soaked poha can be drained and refrigerated for a few hours ahead, but mix in the yogurt only at the table.

recipes.name: Dal Pitha
recipes.subtitle: steamed rice-flour dumplings filled with coarse spiced chana dal, tempered in mustard oil

ingredients.note: the filling; soaked and ground coarse, never smooth
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free. Most brands are cut with wheat flour
for the finishing temper

ingredients.qty: 450ml for the dough, plus water for the steamer

prepNotes: Soak the chana dal in cold water for 4 hours, then drain it well. Wet dal grinds to a paste and the filling turns sticky instead of crumbly.
Make the rice dough while it is hot and keep it covered under a damp cloth at all times. Rice flour dough cracks the moment it dries.
Have the steamer water already boiling before you start shaping, so the pithas go in as soon as they are made.

steps.text: Grind the drained chana dal with the garlic, ginger, green chilli, 1 tsp cumin seeds and 1 tsp salt to a coarse, sandy mixture with no added water.
steps.tip: Pulse rather than run the grinder. You want the texture of wet semolina, not hummus.

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp mustard oil, add the asafoetida and turmeric, then the ground dal, and fry over medium heat for 6-8 minutes until it dries out and smells cooked.
steps.tip: It is done when the mixture stops clinging together and moves loose in the pan.

steps.text: Bring 450ml water to a rolling boil with 1 tsp salt and 1 tsp mustard oil.
Take the pan off the heat, tip in the rice flour all at once and stir hard with a wooden spoon until it comes together into a shaggy mass. Cover and leave 5 minutes.
Knead the warm dough with oiled palms for 4-5 minutes until it is completely smooth and takes a fingerprint without cracking.
steps.tip: Knead it as hot as you can bear; cooled rice dough will not come smooth and the pithas split while steaming.

steps.text: Pinch off walnut-sized pieces, roll each into a ball and press into a 8cm disc between oiled palms.
Place a heaped teaspoon of the dal filling in the centre, fold into a half-moon and press the edge shut, crimping it with your fingers.
Steam the pithas in a single layer over boiling water for 12-15 minutes, until the surface turns glossy and no longer looks chalky.
steps.tip: Do not crowd the steamer. Pithas that touch stick together and tear when you separate them.

steps.text: Heat the remaining mustard oil until it smokes faintly, then crackle the panch phoron, remaining cumin seeds and broken red chillies for 20 seconds.
Toss the steamed pithas in the temper for 2 minutes so they take on a light crust, scatter over the coriander leaves and serve hot with chutney.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Re-steam 5 minutes to soften, or shallow fry the cold pithas in mustard oil until crisp at the edges, which many households prefer to the fresh version.

recipes.name: Dhuska
recipes.subtitle: jharkhandi deep-fried rice and chana dal discs, crisp outside and soft within

ingredients.note: gives dhuska its yellow

prepNotes: Soak the rice and chana dal together in plenty of water for at least 5 hours or overnight; they must crush easily between your nails before you grind.
Grind the batter at least 2 hours before frying and leave it at room temperature. It does not ferment, but resting makes the dhuska lighter.
Do not add extra water to the batter at the last minute; a slack batter drinks oil.

steps.text: Drain the soaked rice and dal thoroughly, shaking the colander dry.
Grind them with the ginger, green chillies and 150 ml water into a thick, slightly grainy batter. The texture of idli batter, not smooth.
steps.tip: Add the water in stages. Too thin and the dhuska will not hold its shape in the oil.

steps.text: Beat in the turmeric, chilli powder, cumin seeds and salt, then rest the batter 2 hours covered.
Stir in the coriander leaves and whisk the batter hard for 30 seconds to aerate it.
Heat the oil in a kadhai to 180C. A drop of batter should rise and sizzle within 3 seconds.
steps.tip: Too cool and they turn greasy; too hot and the centres stay raw.

steps.text: Slide in ladlefuls of batter, 3 at a time, easing each one into a rough 10cm disc as it hits the oil.
Fry 2 minutes until they puff and float, then turn and fry another 2 to 3 minutes until deep gold and crisp at the edges.
steps.tip: Wait for them to float before turning, or they collapse.

steps.text: Lift onto a rack, not paper, so the undersides stay crisp, and repeat with the rest of the batter.
Serve hot with ghugni or aloo chokha.

recipes.storage: Best eaten within the hour. Leftovers keep 1 day refrigerated; crisp them up in a hot oven or a dry pan for 4 minutes rather than the microwave.

recipes.name: Ghugni
recipes.subtitle: dried white peas stewed soft with mustard oil, ginger and cumin, finished with lemon and black salt

ingredients.qty: 1 tbsp, grated, plus 1 tbsp julienned to finish

prepNotes: Soak the dried peas in plenty of cold water overnight, or at least 8 hours. Under-soaked peas take much longer and cook unevenly.
Heat the mustard oil to smoking and let it cool a little before you start cooking. Raw mustard oil is bitter.
Chop the onion fine; it has to disappear into the gravy rather than sit in it.

steps.text: Drain the soaked peas and pressure cook them with 600ml water, the turmeric and 1 tsp salt for 3 whistles, then 10 minutes on low. They should crush easily between finger and thumb but still hold their shape.
steps.tip: Salt the peas at this stage. Added later it sits on the surface and never gets inside.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes faintly, then lower the heat and let it settle for 30 seconds.
Crackle the cumin seeds and bay leaf for 20 seconds until the cumin darkens and smells toasted.
Add the chopped onion and fry over medium heat for 10-12 minutes until deep golden brown at the edges.
steps.tip: This browning is where ghugni gets its sweetness; pulling the onion out pale leaves the dish flat.

steps.text: Stir in the garlic and grated ginger and cook 90 seconds, until the raw smell goes.
Add the tomato and cook 6-8 minutes, pressing it down, until it breaks up and the oil separates at the edges of the pan.
Add the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder with a splash of water and fry 1 minute so the spices do not burn.
Tip in the diced potato with 200ml water and cook covered 10 minutes, until the potato is just tender.
Add the cooked peas with their liquid and the slit green chillies. Simmer uncovered 12-15 minutes, mashing a ladleful of peas against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy.
steps.tip: Mashing part of the peas is what gives ghugni body. Do not add flour or let it stay watery.

steps.text: Stir in the garam masala, taste for salt, and finish off the heat with lemon juice, black salt, julienned ginger and coriander leaves.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and thickens as it sits. Reheat with a splash of hot water and add fresh lemon and ginger at the table, since both fade overnight.
