recipes.name: Khatti Dal
recipes.subtitle: everyday toor dal made unapologetically sour with tamarind

ingredients.qty: 200g, rinsed until the water runs clear

ingredients.note: use a compounded-free asafoetida to keep the dish gluten-free

prepNotes: Soak the toor dal 20 minutes if you have the time. It cooks softer and faster.
Soak the tamarind in hot water for 20 minutes, squeeze it out with your fingers and strain; the dal should be assertively sour, not merely tangy.
Most block asafoetida is cut with wheat flour, so buy a compounded-free one if gluten matters to you.

steps.text: Pressure cook the dal with the turmeric, chopped tomato, green chillies and 700ml water for 4 whistles, about 12 minutes.
Let the pressure fall on its own, then whisk the dal hard for 30 seconds until it is smooth and creamy with no whole lentils left.
steps.tip: Whisking, not blending. A blender makes it gluey.

steps.text: Return the pan to a low flame, add the remaining water and salt, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Stir in the tamarind water and simmer 8 minutes, until the raw sour smell has cooked off and the dal has thickened slightly.
steps.tip: Taste after these 8 minutes, not before. Tamarind mellows as it cooks.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a small pan for the tempering. Crackle the mustard seeds, then the cumin and fenugreek.
Add the crushed garlic and fry until it turns golden, about 1 minute, then the dried red chillies, curry leaves and asafoetida. It will spit hard.
steps.tip: Take the pan off the heat before the asafoetida goes in. It scorches in seconds.

steps.text: If using onion, add it to the tempering and fry 3 minutes until soft and translucent.
Pour the tempering into the dal, cover immediately for a minute to trap the aroma, then stir through.
Finish with coriander leaves and serve with plain rice and a wedge of lime.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. It sets firm when cold. Reheat with 100ml water per portion, stirring until it flows again, and refresh with a small second tempering if it tastes flat.

recipes.name: Khichdi Ka Khatta
recipes.subtitle: thin, sharp tamarind sauce poured over khichdi, sour first and sweet after

ingredients.note: a scant quarter; more turns it bitter
use compounded-free hing to keep the dish gluten-free
balances the sourness; the khatta should still lead with tamarind

prepNotes: Soak the tamarind in hot water for 20 minutes, then squeeze it out thoroughly with your fingers and strain. Do this before anything else.
Khatta is meant to be pourable, closer to rasam than to chutney. Have extra hot water ready in case it tightens too much.
Grate the jaggery before you start; a solid lump will not dissolve evenly in a thin sauce.

steps.text: Squeeze the soaked tamarind hard in its water, strain through a sieve, and press the pulp to get everything out. Discard the fibres.
Heat the oil in a pan and pop the mustard seeds, 20 seconds, until they stop jumping.
Add the cumin, fenugreek seeds and dried red chillies and fry 15 seconds, no longer.
steps.tip: Fenugreek burns in seconds and takes the whole pot bitter with it. Count it out.

steps.text: Add the asafoetida, curry leaves, crushed garlic and green chillies and fry 1 minute, until the garlic is pale gold and the leaves are crisp.
Stir in the turmeric and chilli powder off the heat for 10 seconds so they bloom without scorching.
Pour in the strained tamarind water and 200ml plain water, add the salt, and bring to a boil.
Simmer uncovered 12 minutes, until the raw edge of the tamarind has gone and the sauce smells rounded rather than sharp.
steps.tip: Undercooked tamarind tastes metallic. Twelve minutes is the minimum, and it is the difference between good khatta and puckering acid.

steps.text: Stir in the jaggery and simmer 3 minutes more, until dissolved. Taste: sour should lead, sweet should follow.
Slacken with hot water if it has thickened past pouring consistency, scatter the coriander, and serve hot over khichdi.

recipes.storage: Keeps 5 days refrigerated and the flavour improves after a day. Reheat on the stovetop, thinning with a little hot water as it will have thickened.

recipes.name: Lukhmi
recipes.subtitle: square flaky pastries filled with spiced mutton mince, the classic wedding starter

ingredients.note: the shortening that gives the flaky layers

prepNotes: Rest the dough at least 30 minutes under a damp cloth; unrested dough springs back and will not roll thin.
Cook the mince filling ahead and cool it completely. Warm filling steams inside the pastry and bursts the seams in the fryer.
The filling must be dry. Any liquid left in it will make the lukhmi split open in the oil.

steps.text: Rub the melted ghee into the maida with your fingertips for 3 minutes until the flour holds its shape when squeezed in a fist.
steps.tip: This step is the flakiness. Skimp on it and you get a bread, not a pastry.

steps.text: Add the salt and cold water a little at a time and bring together into a firm, tight dough. Firmer than a chapati dough. Knead 5 minutes, cover and rest 30 minutes.
For the filling, heat 2 tbsp oil and fry the chopped onion for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the ginger and garlic pastes and green chillies, cook 1 minute, then the mince. Break it up with the back of a spoon and fry on high for 5 minutes until it loses its pink.
Add the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt and cook on medium for 12 minutes, stirring, until the mince is dry and the fat has separated out.
steps.tip: Keep going until the pan base stays clear when you drag a spoon through.

steps.text: Stir in the garam masala, black pepper, lemon juice, mint and coriander. Spread on a plate and cool completely.
Divide the dough into 12. Roll each into a 12cm square about 2mm thick, keeping the rest covered.
Put 1.5 tbsp of filling on one half of each square, brush the edges with water, fold into a rectangle and press the edges firmly, then crimp with a fork.
steps.tip: Press out every air pocket. Trapped air expands and splits the pastry in the oil.

steps.text: Heat the frying oil to 160C. It should be moderate, not fierce: a scrap of dough should rise slowly over 4-5 seconds.
Fry 4 at a time for 6-7 minutes, turning once, until pale biscuit-gold and blistered. Drain on a rack.
steps.tip: Low and slow is what makes them flaky; hot oil browns the outside while the layers inside stay doughy.

steps.text: Serve hot with sliced onion and lemon.

recipes.storage: Best eaten within a couple of hours. They keep 2 days in an airtight tin and crisp up again in a 180C oven for 8 minutes. Uncooked assembled lukhmi freeze well for a month and fry from frozen at 150C.

recipes.name: Marag
recipes.subtitle: thin white mutton soup enriched with cashew and yogurt, drunk before a biryani

ingredients.note: the bones make the broth
marag is white and chilli-hot, not red
for a richer finish

prepNotes: Soak the cashews, almonds and poppy seeds in warm water for 20 minutes, then grind to a completely smooth paste with a little of the soaking water.
Whisk the yogurt until it is perfectly smooth and leave it at room temperature. Cold yogurt splits the moment it hits the pot.
Ask for mutton with marrow bones included; marag without them is just a thin curry.

steps.text: Heat the ghee in a pressure cooker and add the cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, bay leaf and mace. Let them puff for 30 seconds.
Add the sliced onion and cook 8 minutes until soft and pale gold. Stop before it browns, or the broth loses its whiteness.
steps.tip: Colour in the onion means colour in the soup. Pale gold is the target.

steps.text: Stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and the slit green chillies and cook 1 minute.
Add the mutton and sear on high for 5 minutes until the outside is sealed and no pink shows.
Take the pot off the heat, wait a minute, then fold in the whisked yogurt in three additions, stirring continuously.
steps.tip: Off the heat and in stages. This is the one step where marag most often curdles.

steps.text: Return to a low flame and cook 5 minutes until the yogurt tightens around the meat and no longer smells raw.
Add the water, salt and half the mint. Pressure cook for 5 whistles, about 25 minutes, and let the pressure fall on its own.
Open, and stir in the ground cashew and almond paste. Simmer uncovered 12 minutes until the broth thickens just enough to coat a spoon.
steps.tip: Stir the base often here. Nut paste sinks and catches.

steps.text: Add the crushed black pepper and the cream, if using, and simmer 3 minutes more. Marag should stay drinkable, not stew-thick; loosen with hot water if needed.
Finish with the remaining mint and the coriander leaves, and serve in cups with lemon wedges to squeeze in.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. Reheat gently over low heat without letting it boil, since a hard boil splits the yogurt; thin with hot water and re-check the salt and pepper before serving.

recipes.name: Methi Murgh
recipes.subtitle: chicken braised with fresh fenugreek, bitter-sweet and thick rather than soupy

ingredients.note: thigh and drumstick hold up better than breast
deepens the fenugreek note at the end

prepNotes: Toss the picked methi leaves with 1 tsp salt, leave 20 minutes, then squeeze out the dark liquid hard. This is what stops the dish turning harshly bitter.
Take the yogurt out of the fridge 30 minutes ahead. Cold yogurt splits the moment it hits a hot pan.
Pat the chicken dry so it browns instead of steaming.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadhai and fry the sliced onion over medium heat until evenly golden brown, 12-14 minutes.
steps.tip: Stir every couple of minutes and take it to gold, not mahogany. Burnt onion turns the gravy bitter and there is no rescuing it.

steps.text: Add the ginger and garlic pastes and fry 2 minutes, until the raw smell goes and the oil looks clear at the edges.
Add the chicken and green chillies and sear over high heat 5 minutes, until the pieces are opaque all over.
Lower the heat, stir in the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander and cumin powders with 2 tbsp water, and fry 3 minutes until the oil separates.
steps.tip: The splash of water keeps the ground spices from scorching in the few seconds before the chicken juices come out.

steps.text: Take the pan off the heat for 30 seconds, whisk in the yogurt a spoonful at a time, then return to low heat and cook 5 minutes.
steps.tip: Off the heat and a spoon at a time. This is the only reliable way to keep yogurt from curdling into grains.

steps.text: Fold in the squeezed methi leaves and salt, and cook uncovered 8 minutes, until the leaves collapse and darken.
Cover and simmer on low 12 minutes, stirring twice, until the chicken is tender and the gravy clings to the pieces.
Uncover and cook off any watery liquid over medium heat, 3-4 minutes. Methi murgh should be thick enough to scoop, not ladle.
Sprinkle over the garam masala and crushed kasuri methi, spoon on the ghee, and rest covered 5 minutes off the heat.
Finish with coriander leaves and lemon juice, and serve with rumali roti or plain rice.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and tastes better on day two. Reheat gently on the stovetop with 2 tbsp water; the microwave dries the chicken out.

recipes.name: Mirchi ka Salan
recipes.subtitle: long green chillies in a thick peanut, sesame and tamarind gravy

ingredients.qty: 10 large mild bhavnagri, slit lengthways, seeds scraped out
ingredients.note: the fat pale ones, not the thin hot ones
the backbone of the gravy
any more turns the gravy bitter
to round off the sourness
salan is meant to be an oily gravy

prepNotes: Soak the tamarind in hot water for 20 minutes and squeeze out a thick pulp; strain and keep the liquid.
Slit the chillies down one side and scrape out the seeds and ribs with a teaspoon handle. That is where nearly all the heat sits.
Dry-roast the peanuts, sesame and coconut ahead and let them cool fully before grinding, or the paste turns oily and grainy.

steps.text: Dry-roast the peanuts in a kadhai over medium heat for 5 minutes until the skins blister and loosen, then rub off the skins in a cloth.
Roast the sesame in the same pan for 1 minute until it pops, then the dried coconut for 1 minute until it smells nutty and turns pale gold. Cool completely.
Grind the peanuts, sesame and coconut with 150ml water to a fine, smooth paste. Set aside.
steps.tip: Grind for longer than you think. Any grit here stays gritty in the finished dish.

steps.text: Heat 3 tbsp of the oil and fry the slit chillies for 2-3 minutes, turning, until the skins blister and go khaki. Lift them out and reserve.
In the same oil, fry the chopped onion until soft and light brown, about 8 minutes, then cool and grind to a paste.
Add the rest of the oil to the pan and crackle the cumin, mustard, fenugreek and nigella, then throw in the curry leaves.
steps.tip: The fenugreek should barely change colour. Dark fenugreek is bitter.

steps.text: Add the ginger and garlic pastes and fry 1 minute until the raw smell goes, then the onion paste, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder. Cook 3 minutes.
Stir in the ground peanut-sesame paste and fry on medium-low for 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until the mixture darkens and oil rises around the edges.
steps.tip: This is the step that decides the dish. Undercooked paste tastes raw and chalky.

steps.text: Pour in the tamarind water and the remaining water, add salt and the jaggery, and simmer uncovered 12 minutes until glossy and the thickness of pouring cream.
Slide the fried chillies back in, cover and simmer 5 minutes more, then rest off the heat 10 minutes and scatter with coriander leaves.
steps.tip: The chillies should stay whole. Stir gently or not at all once they are back in.

recipes.storage: Keeps 4 days refrigerated and tastes better on day two. The oil sets on top when cold; warm it gently on the stove and stir it back in, adding a splash of water if it has tightened.

recipes.name: Murgh do Pyaza
recipes.subtitle: chicken cooked with onions twice over, once browned to a paste and once in chunks

ingredients.qty: 600g total: 3 sliced for browning, 2 quartered into petals

prepNotes: Marinate the chicken in the yogurt with half the ginger-garlic paste, the turmeric and salt for at least 1 hour, refrigerated.
Take the marinated chicken out 20 minutes before cooking so it is not fridge-cold when it hits the pan.
Cut the second lot of onions into petals rather than slices. They need to keep their shape to the end.

steps.text: Heat 3 tbsp oil and fry the sliced onions over medium heat for 12-14 minutes until evenly deep brown. Lift out half and reserve for the finish.

steps.text: Cool the remaining browned onions and grind to a paste with a splash of water.
In the same pan, add the whole spices (cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, bay leaf) and let them puff for 30 seconds.
Add the remaining ginger and garlic pastes and cook 1 minute until the raw edge disappears.
Add the marinated chicken and sear on high for 6 minutes, turning, until the yogurt has tightened around the pieces and the base looks dry.
steps.tip: Keep the flame high here so the yogurt reduces rather than boils and splits.

steps.text: Stir in the browned onion paste, chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder. Fry on medium for 6-8 minutes until oil separates at the sides.
Pour in the water, add the green chillies, cover and simmer 15 minutes until the chicken is tender and pulling from the bone.
Heat the last 2 tbsp oil in a separate pan and sear the onion petals on high for 3 minutes until charred at the edges but still crunchy inside.
steps.tip: This second onion should have bite. That contrast is the whole point of do pyaza.

steps.text: Fold the seared petals, the reserved browned onions, garam masala and black pepper into the curry and cook uncovered 3 minutes to thicken.
Take off the heat, stir in the lemon juice, mint and coriander, and rest 5 minutes before serving with roti.

recipes.name: Mutton Do Pyaza
recipes.subtitle: mutton with onion twice over, once melted into the gravy and once in soft wedges

ingredients.qty: 5 medium, three finely sliced and two quartered into petals

prepNotes: Marinate the mutton in the yogurt, ginger and garlic pastes, turmeric and salt for 1 hour in the refrigerator, or up to 4 hours.
Cut the second lot of onion into quarters and separate the layers into petals. These go in late and must stay in recognisable pieces.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pressure cooker and crackle the cardamoms, cloves, cinnamon and bay leaf for 30 seconds, until fragrant.

steps.text: Tip in the marinated mutton and sear over high heat 6 minutes, until the pieces have coloured and the yogurt has dried onto them.

steps.text: Open up, taste for salt, and boil uncovered 5 minutes to reduce the gravy to a coating consistency.

Fold the petals into the curry, sprinkle over the garam masala, cover and rest off the heat 5 minutes.
Scatter with coriander leaves and serve with roti or khatti dal and rice.

recipes.name: Patthar Ka Gosht
recipes.subtitle: thin mutton slices seared hard and fast, smoky at the edges and still juicy

ingredients.qty: 600g leg, sliced into 5mm escalopes and flattened
ingredients.note: ask the butcher for boneless leg cut thin
the tenderiser; skip only if using very young meat

ingredients.qty: 1, half in the marinade and half to serve

prepNotes: Marinate 2 hours refrigerated, and no longer than 3. Papaya keeps working, and overnight it turns the meat pasty.
Flatten each slice between two sheets of cling film with a rolling pin until about 4mm thick. Even thickness matters more than any spice here.
Bring the meat to room temperature 20 minutes before cooking, or the outside chars before the centre is done.

steps.text: Grind the green chillies, coriander leaves and mint with 1 tbsp water to a coarse green paste.
Mix the papaya paste, yogurt, ginger and garlic pastes, green paste, pepper, garam masala, cumin, chilli powder, juice of half a lemon and salt.

Heat a heavy tawa or cast-iron griddle over high heat for a full 5 minutes, until a drop of water skitters and vanishes.

Move the cooked slices to a warm plate and repeat with the rest, wiping the griddle between batches.
Rest 3 minutes, then squeeze over the remaining lemon and serve hot with sliced onion and mint chutney.

omit for a nut-free version

recipes.name: Sheer Khurma
recipes.subtitle: eid morning milk pudding heavy with dates, roasted vermicelli and nuts

ingredients.note: the khurma in the name
for the thick, milky finish

ingredients.qty: a large pinch, soaked in 2 tbsp warm milk

prepNotes: Soak the saffron in warm milk for 15 minutes so it gives up its colour.
Soak the sliced dates in 100ml warm milk for 20 minutes; they plump up and stop drinking the pudding dry later.
Use a heavy-bottomed pan. Milk reduced for 30 minutes will scorch in a thin one.

steps.text: Melt the ghee in a heavy pan and fry the almonds, pistachios and cashews for 2 minutes until golden. Lift them out with a slotted spoon.

steps.tip: They puff and burn within seconds, stand over them.

steps.text: Add the broken vermicelli to the remaining ghee and roast on low for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly, until evenly reddish-brown and fragrant.

steps.text: Pour in the milk and bring to a gentle boil, stirring to keep the vermicelli from clumping on the base.

Add the sugar and stir until fully dissolved, about 2 minutes.

steps.text: Take off the heat, stir in the rose water, and fold through most of the fried nuts and raisins.
Rest 10 minutes and serve warm in small bowls, scattered with the remaining nuts. It is equally good chilled.

recipes.name: Shikampuri Kebab
recipes.subtitle: soft mince patties with a cool hung-curd filling hidden inside

ingredients.note: binds the mince; nothing else does this job as cleanly
for the filling

ingredients.qty: 1 large, half finely chopped raw for the filling and half sliced

prepNotes: Hang the yogurt in muslin for at least 4 hours, or overnight in the fridge. The filling must be dry and crumbly; wet curd will burst the kebab in the pan.
The cooked mince has to be bone dry before grinding. Any moisture left in the pan becomes a kebab that falls apart.
Chill the shaped kebabs 30 minutes before frying. Cold kebabs hold their shape.
Soak the chana dal 30 minutes so it cooks in the same time as the mince.

steps.text: Put the mince, drained chana dal, sliced onion, ginger and garlic pastes, dried red chillies, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, cumin seeds, salt and 250ml water in a pan.
Bring to a boil, then simmer covered 30 minutes, until the dal is soft and the mince is cooked through.
Uncover and cook over medium heat, stirring, until every trace of liquid has gone and the mixture squeaks against the pan, about 8 minutes. Cool completely.
steps.tip: Do not shortcut this. Damp mince is the single reason shikampuri kebabs disintegrate in the ghee.

steps.text: Grind the cooled mixture to a smooth, stiff paste with no added water. Mix in the black pepper, garam masala and lemon juice, and check the salt.
Make the filling: mash the hung curd with the finely chopped raw onion, green chillies, mint, coriander and a pinch of salt.
Divide the mince into 12. Flatten a portion in your palm, place a teaspoon of filling in the centre, and draw the edges over to seal completely.
steps.tip: Seal with wet fingertips and check for cracks before flattening. An open seam leaks curd and the kebab collapses.

steps.text: Press gently into a disc 6cm across and 1.5cm thick. Repeat with the rest and chill 30 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp ghee on a tawa over medium-low heat and fry the kebabs in batches, 3 minutes a side, until deep brown and crusted.
steps.tip: Medium-low, and turn only once. High heat browns the outside before the crust is strong enough to survive the flip.

steps.text: Drain briefly on paper and serve hot with onion rings and lemon.

recipes.storage: The shaped raw kebabs keep 24 hours refrigerated and fry better cold; they also freeze 1 month between sheets of paper. Fried kebabs keep 2 days and reheat on a tawa with a little ghee, 2 minutes a side.

recipes.name: Tala Hua Gosht
recipes.subtitle: mutton boiled tender then fried dry with black pepper until the masala clings

ingredients.note: the dominant note of the dish

prepNotes: Marinate the mutton with the ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chilli powder and salt for 1 hour in the refrigerator, or up to overnight.
Crush the peppercorns coarsely in a mortar just before cooking; pre-ground pepper tastes flat and dusty here.
Use a wide pan for the frying stage. The meat needs room to sit in one layer and colour.

steps.text: Pressure cook the marinated mutton with 1 sliced onion, the whole spices and 400ml water for 5 whistles, about 25 minutes.
Let the pressure fall naturally, then check: the meat should give completely to a fork. If not, cook 5 minutes more.
steps.tip: Undercooked mutton will not tenderise once you start frying it. Get it right here.

steps.text: Strain, keeping the stock. Boil the stock down separately to about 100ml of concentrated liquid.
Heat the oil in a wide kadhai and fry the remaining sliced onions for 10 minutes until deep golden brown.
Add the green chillies and curry leaves and let them crackle for 20 seconds.
Add the coriander powder and cumin powder and fry 30 seconds, then tip in the drained mutton pieces.
Fry on medium-high for 12-15 minutes, turning the pieces every couple of minutes, until they are browned on all sides and the masala has dried onto them.
steps.tip: This is the whole dish. Turn, do not stir. You want colour on the meat, not a mash.

steps.text: Pour in the reduced stock a spoon at a time, letting each addition dry off before adding the next, until the pan is dry and glossy.
Add the crushed black pepper and garam masala and toss for 2 minutes off the direct heat.
steps.tip: Pepper goes in at the end; cooked long it loses its top notes.

steps.text: Finish with lemon juice and coriander leaves and serve with roti or bagara khana.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. Reheat in a dry pan over medium heat with 1 tbsp water so it steams loose without going soggy; it is meant to be a dry dish, so avoid adding oil.

recipes.name: Til Ki Chutney
recipes.subtitle: toasted sesame and coconut ground with tamarind into a thick, nutty relish

ingredients.qty: walnut-sized lump, soaked in 3 tbsp hot water

prepNotes: Soak the tamarind in hot water for 10 minutes while you toast the sesame.
Toast the sesame in a dry pan and keep it moving. It goes from pale to burnt in about fifteen seconds and burnt sesame is unusable.
Cool everything to room temperature before grinding, or the chutney sweats and sours within a day.

steps.text: Dry-toast the sesame over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, 3-4 minutes, until the seeds turn one shade darker and start popping.
steps.tip: Tip them onto a cold plate the moment they pop, or the residual pan heat keeps toasting them.

steps.text: In the same pan, toast the grated dried coconut 1 minute, until fragrant and just golden. Set aside.
Add 1 tsp of the oil and fry the dried red chillies, garlic and cumin over medium heat 1 minute, until the chillies darken slightly.
Cool all the toasted ingredients completely, about 10 minutes.
Grind the sesame alone first to a coarse powder, then add the coconut, chillies, garlic, cumin, soaked tamarind with its water and salt.
Grind to a thick paste, adding the water 1 tbsp at a time. Stop while it still has a little grain. This is a chutney, not a puree.
steps.tip: Too much water at once makes it loose and it will not tighten again. Add it slowly.

steps.text: Heat the remaining oil, pop the mustard seeds and crisp the curry leaves, 20 seconds, and pour over the chutney.
Fold in the coriander leaves and serve with rice and ghee, or as a side to biryani.

recipes.storage: Keeps 1 week refrigerated in a clean airtight jar, or 3 days at room temperature in cool weather. Always use a dry spoon; the oil separates and can be stirred back in.

recipes.name: Tomato Kut
recipes.subtitle: thick sour-hot tomato gravy thickened with gram flour and eggs poached in it

ingredients.note: the thickener; gluten-free unlike the wheat flour some cooks use

ingredients.qty: 4, poached in the gravy at the end

ingredients.note: compounded-free if you need it gluten-free

prepNotes: Use the ripest tomatoes you can find; underripe ones give a thin, metallic kut that no amount of simmering will fix.
Soak the tamarind in hot water 20 minutes and strain.
Whisk the besan into 150ml cold water until completely lump-free and leave it standing while the tomatoes cook.

steps.text: Simmer the tomatoes with 350ml water and the turmeric for 15 minutes until completely collapsed and pulpy.
Cool slightly, blend smooth, then push through a sieve to leave the skins and seeds behind.
steps.tip: Sieving is what gives kut its velvety body. Do not skip it.

steps.text: Heat 3 tbsp oil in a heavy pan, crackle the mustard, cumin and fenugreek, then add the curry leaves, dried red chillies and green chillies.
Add the crushed garlic and fry 1 minute until it smells sweet and turns pale gold, then take the pan off the heat and stir in the asafoetida.
steps.tip: Asafoetida burns almost instantly on a hot base. Off the heat is the safe way.

steps.text: Return to the heat, add the chilli powder and coriander powder, and fry 20 seconds before pouring in the sieved tomato.
Whisk the standing besan slurry once more and pour it in slowly, stirring constantly. Simmer 12 minutes until the gravy is thick, glossy and no longer tastes of raw flour.
steps.tip: Pour the slurry in a thin stream while stirring, or you will be picking out lumps for the next ten minutes.

steps.text: Add the tamarind water and salt and simmer 5 minutes more; it should be thick enough to hold a channel behind the spoon.
Crack the eggs one at a time onto the surface, spacing them apart. Cover and poach on low for 6 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still soft.
Heat the last 2 tbsp oil, sizzle a few extra curry leaves in it, and pour it over the top. Scatter with coriander leaves and serve with plain rice.

recipes.storage: The gravy keeps 3 days refrigerated, but poach the eggs fresh each time. Reheated poached eggs go rubbery. Warm the kut with a splash of water over low heat, stirring so the besan does not catch.

recipes.name: Vegetable Biryani
recipes.subtitle: layered rice and mixed vegetables sealed and steamed, the meatless dum biryani

ingredients.qty: a pinch in 3 tbsp warm milk

prepNotes: Vegetables release water in a way meat does not, so they are fried hard first. Raw vegetables layered under rice make it soggy.

steps.text: Fry the sliced onion in ghee until deep brown and crisp. Drain and reserve; this birista carries the sweetness of the dish.

steps.text: Fry the potato, cauliflower, carrot and beans in the same ghee over high heat until the edges colour. Do not cook them through.
Fold the vegetables into the whisked yogurt with ginger, garlic, chilli, turmeric, half the herbs, half the birista and salt. Rest 20 minutes.
Boil the rice in heavily salted water with the whole spices until 70 per cent done, about 5 minutes, then drain at once.
steps.tip: Test by crushing a grain: it should still have a hard white core.

steps.text: Spread the vegetable mixture in a heavy pot, layer the rice over it, and top with the remaining birista, herbs, saffron milk, lemon juice and ghee.
Seal with a tight lid or foil. Cook 5 minutes on high to build steam, then 25 minutes on the lowest heat.
Rest 15 minutes before opening. Lift from the bottom to serve so every plate gets both layers.

prepNotes: Boil and dry the noodles at least 30 minutes before frying. Surface moisture is what makes hot oil erupt.
Blend the tomatoes and pass them through a sieve if you want the glassy restaurant gravy; skip the sieve for a homier one.
Fry the noodle nests first and keep them uncovered. Covered, they steam themselves soft.

steps.text: Boil the noodles for 1 minute less than the packet says, drain, rinse cold and spread on a cloth to dry for 30 minutes.
Heat 500ml oil in a kadhai to 180C and fry the noodles in four loose nests for 2 to 3 minutes each, until golden and audibly brittle. Drain on paper.
steps.tip: Lower each nest in with a slotted spoon and hold its shape for the first 20 seconds so it fries as a disc.

steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wide pan, add the garlic, ginger and spring onion whites and fry 40 seconds.
Add the onion, carrot and beans and toss 2 minutes, then the cabbage and capsicum for 2 minutes more. Keep them crisp.
Pour in the tomato puree with the kashmiri chilli and cook 6 minutes on a medium flame until it darkens and stops smelling raw.
steps.tip: Do not shortcut this. Undercooked tomato makes the gravy taste tinny however much sugar goes in.

steps.text: Add 500ml water, the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, pepper and 1 tsp salt and simmer 4 minutes.
Slake the cornflour in 80ml cold water, stir it in and cook 2 minutes to a glossy gravy that pours thickly off a ladle.

steps.tip: This balancing step is the whole dish. Take a minute over it.

steps.text: Set a noodle nest on each plate, ladle the hot gravy over the middle so the edges stay crisp, and scatter the spring onion greens.
steps.tip: Sauce it at the table, not in the kitchen, if there is any delay between the two.

colour without ferocious heat
1 for the marinade, 1 for the glaze

ingredients.note: for the dip
for the dip

recipes.subtitle: fried chicken in a dark garlic and soy gravy, the dish that built Indian Chinese

image.credit: Abhinaba Basu from Redmond, United States

ingredients.note: the dish is built on garlic; do not reduce this

prepNotes: Invented in Kolkata, not Manchuria. Nelson Wang is generally credited with it at a Bombay hotel in the 1970s.

recipes.name: Hakka Noodles

ingredients.qty: 5, whites sliced and greens kept for the end

ingredients.note: the sharper restaurant note
stirred in at the end, not cooked

prepNotes: Cut every vegetable to the same fine matchstick before you light the stove. The stir-fry itself takes 6 minutes and there is no pausing.
Boil the noodles ahead, rinse them cold, and toss with 1 tsp oil. Cold, oiled noodles do not clump in the pan.

steps.text: Boil the noodles in 3 litres of salted water for 1 minute less than the packet says, until just yielding with a firm core.

steps.text: Drain, rinse under cold running water until completely cool, drain hard and toss with a teaspoon of oil.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a kadhai until it shimmers and a shred of cabbage sizzles on contact.
Add the garlic, ginger and spring onion whites and stir for 30 seconds, fragrant, not browned.

steps.tip: Keep them moving constantly and keep the flame at maximum. Vegetables that sit still release water and the dish stews.

steps.text: Push the vegetables to one side, add the remaining 1 tbsp oil and the noodles, and toss to loosen them.

the crunchy raft on top

steps.text: Drain the soaked chillies and grind them with 10 garlic cloves, the ginger and 60ml water to a coarse red paste.

Heat the oil in a deep pan, add the garlic, ginger and spring onion whites and cook 40 seconds without letting them brown.

recipes.name: Baimbale Curry

Drop the cut pieces into salted water as you go so they do not brown.

steps.text: Pressure-cook the jackfruit with 250 ml water, the turmeric and 1 tsp salt for 3 whistles, then let the pressure drop by itself.
steps.tip: Jackfruit should be soft enough to crush against the pot but still hold its shape. Overcooked, it goes to mush in the gravy.

steps.text: Grind the coconut, cumin, green chilli and garlic with 150 ml water to a smooth paste.
Heat the coconut oil in a pan, add the mustard seeds and wait for them to pop, about 30 seconds.
Add the dried red chilli and curry leaves and let them crackle for 10 seconds.
Add the onion and fry until soft and pale gold, about 7 minutes.
Stir in the coriander powder and crushed black pepper and fry 1 minute.
Tip in the cooked jackfruit along with its liquid and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the ground coconut paste, bring to a bare simmer and cook 8 minutes, stirring often.
steps.tip: Do not let it boil hard once the coconut is in. It will curdle and go grainy.

steps.text: Check the salt, take the pan off the heat and stir in the vinegar if using. Rest 5 minutes before serving with rice.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat gently with a splash of water. It does not freeze well. The jackfruit turns stringy.

recipes.name: Dali Thoy
recipes.subtitle: the everyday konkani toor dal, thin and clean, finished with hing and green chilli

ingredients.note: not strictly traditional but common in Mangalore homes
the flavour of this dal is really coconut oil and hing, so use both properly
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Rinse the toor dal until the water runs clear. Cloudy dal makes a muddy thoy.
No soaking needed, but 20 minutes in warm water shaves cooking time if you are in a hurry.
Have the tempering ingredients within reach of the stove; the whole tadka takes under a minute.

steps.text: Pressure cook the dal with 2 1/2 cups water and the turmeric for 4 whistles, then let the pressure fall on its own.
Open the cooker and whisk the dal smooth, adding up to 1/2 cup hot water. Thoy should pour like thin cream, not sit in a mound.
steps.tip: This is the single thing people get wrong. Thoy is meant to be thin enough to drink from the bowl.

steps.text: Add the green chillies, crushed ginger and salt and simmer 5 minutes on low.
Taste and check the salt now, while there is still time for it to dissolve evenly.
Heat the coconut oil in a small pan until it shimmers, then add the mustard seeds and let them pop fully, about 20 seconds.
steps.tip: Wait for the popping to actually stop. Half-popped mustard tastes raw and slightly bitter.

steps.text: Take the pan off the flame, add the broken red chilli, curry leaves and hing, and let them foam in the residual heat for 5 seconds.
steps.tip: Hing burns almost instantly on a live flame. Off the heat is the only safe way.

steps.text: Pour the tempering into the dal, cover immediately and leave it 2 minutes to trap the aroma.
Stir through the coriander leaves and serve hot over rice with a spoon of coconut oil and a piece of pickle.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. It thickens in the fridge, so whisk in hot water and re-warm gently; the tempering flattens after a day, so a fresh 20-second tadka on top is worth it.

recipes.name: Goli Baje
recipes.subtitle: soft, tangy gram flour dumplings from the Mangalore coast

ingredients.note: sour curd is what gives goli baje its tang and its lift

prepNotes: Also sold as Mangalore bajji. The batter must be thick enough to hold a rough ball dropped from the fingers.

steps.text: Whisk the yogurt smooth and mix in both flours, salt and the soda into a thick batter.
Rest, covered, 2 to 3 hours at room temperature until it looks aerated.
Fold in the green chilli, ginger, curry leaves and coconut slivers.
Drop rough balls into medium-hot oil using wet fingers.
steps.tip: Medium heat. Too hot and they brown before the middle sets.

steps.text: Fry 5 minutes, turning, until deep gold all over. Drain and serve hot with coconut chutney.

recipes.name: Halbai
recipes.subtitle: set rice and coconut milk pudding sweetened with jaggery and cut into soft diamonds

ingredients.note: first-press if you are extracting it fresh
dark jaggery gives the proper deep colour
scattered over the tray before setting
makes the jaggery taste like more than just sweet

prepNotes: Soak the rice at least 4 hours so it grinds completely smooth. Any grit will still be there in the set pudding.
Melt the jaggery in 1 cup water, then strain it through a fine sieve to catch the grit that jaggery always carries.
Grease a shallow tray or thali with ghee and keep it beside the stove; the mixture sets fast once it comes off the heat.

steps.text: Drain the rice and grind it with 1 cup of the coconut milk to a completely smooth, pourable batter.
steps.tip: Run a little between your fingers. If it feels at all sandy, grind another 2 minutes.

steps.text: Strain the batter through a fine sieve into a heavy-bottomed pan, pushing through with the back of a ladle.
Stir in the strained jaggery syrup, the remaining coconut milk and the salt.
Cook over low heat, stirring continuously with a flat wooden spoon, for about 20 minutes.
steps.tip: Continuously means continuously. The moment you stop, the base catches and the whole batch tastes burnt.

steps.text: The mixture will thin first, then thicken and start to gloss and pull away from the sides of the pan.
Add the ghee a tablespoon at a time, letting each one be absorbed before the next goes in, about 8 minutes more.
steps.tip: When the last of the ghee starts to weep back out at the edges, it is done.

steps.text: Stir in the crushed cardamom and cook 1 minute more.
Pour into the greased tray, level the top with a ghee-smeared spatula and scatter the grated coconut over.
steps.tip: Work fast. It stiffens as it cools and will not level cleanly once it starts to set.

steps.text: Cool at room temperature for 3 to 4 hours until firm, then cut into diamonds with a greased knife.
steps.tip: Do not put it in the fridge to speed this up; chilled halbai sets hard and loses its softness.

recipes.storage: Keeps 4 days in a covered box at room temperature in cool weather, or 1 week refrigerated. Bring refrigerated pieces back to room temperature before eating, or warm them 10 seconds so the ghee softens.

recipes.name: Hesarubele Payasa
recipes.subtitle: soft moong dal pudding sweetened with jaggery and finished in coconut milk

ingredients.note: split yellow
dark, for colour and depth
thick, first extract
the chips Kannadiga households fry with the cashews

prepNotes: Dry-roast the moong dal before cooking, 4 minutes in a dry pan is what gives this payasa its nutty backbone.
Melt the jaggery separately in 1/4 cup water and strain it; unstrained jaggery carries grit and sand.
Have the coconut milk at room temperature and add it only off the boil, or it will separate.

steps.text: Dry-roast the moong dal over medium heat 4 minutes, stirring, until it is a shade darker and smells like roasted nuts.
steps.tip: Stop while it is still pale gold. Dark dal makes a bitter payasa.

steps.text: Rinse the roasted dal, then pressure-cook it with 2 cups water for 3 whistles, or simmer covered 25 minutes, until completely soft and mashable.
Mash the cooked dal lightly against the side of the pot, leaving some texture, and keep it on low heat.
Melt the grated jaggery with 1/4 cup water in a separate pan over low heat, then strain it through a fine sieve into the dal.
Simmer the dal and jaggery together 8 minutes, stirring, until the mixture thickens and takes on a glossy amber colour.
steps.tip: Jaggery must go in after the dal is fully cooked. Added early it stops the dal softening.

steps.text: Take the pot off the heat and stir in the coconut milk, crushed cardamom and the pinch of salt.
steps.tip: Off the heat. Boiling coconut milk after this point will make it curdle and grainy.

steps.text: Return to the very lowest heat for 2 minutes to warm through, without letting it bubble.
Heat the ghee in a small pan and fry the cashews 1 minute until golden, then the coconut slices 30 seconds, then the raisins until they swell.
Pour the ghee and its fried garnish over the payasa, stir once and serve warm.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated and thickens considerably as it cools. Loosen with 2 tbsp warm water or coconut milk and reheat on low without boiling.

recipes.name: Jolada Rotti
recipes.subtitle: thin unleavened jowar bread from north Karnataka, dry-toasted until it puffs

ingredients.note: plus 1/2 cup extra for dusting and patting
boiling hot

prepNotes: Jowar has no gluten, so the dough is held together by hot water and kneading alone. The water must be at a full boil when it goes in.
Set out a clean damp cloth or a sheet of parchment; north Karnataka cooks pat the rotti out by hand on it rather than rolling.
Knead and rest the dough 10 minutes under a damp cloth before shaping, and keep it covered between rottis so it never dries.

steps.text: Boil the water with the salt. Tip in the jowar flour all at once and stir with a wooden spoon until no dry flour remains.
Cover and rest 5 minutes off the heat so the flour drinks the water.
Turn out while still warm and knead 6 to 8 minutes with the heel of your hand until the dough is smooth, warm and slightly tacky, not crumbly.
steps.tip: If it cracks when you press it, wet your palm and knead again. Underkneaded jowar dough will never hold a round.

steps.text: Divide into 8 balls and keep them under a damp cloth.
Dust the work surface generously with dry jowar flour. Flatten one ball and pat it outward with flat fingertips, rotating as you go, into a 7-inch round about 2mm thick.
steps.tip: Pat from the centre outward and rotate a quarter turn each time. That is what keeps it circular.

steps.text: Brush the excess flour off the round and lift it onto a hot tawa over medium heat.
Cook 40 seconds until the surface dulls, then flip. Wipe a wet hand lightly over the top surface.
steps.tip: The film of water is what makes it steam and balloon.

steps.text: Cook the second side 1 minute, then lift the rotti onto a direct flame or press it with a cloth on the tawa until it puffs into a dome, about 20 seconds.
Stack the finished rottis in a cloth-lined basket and repeat with the rest.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days wrapped in a cloth at room temperature and stiffens as it sits, which is intended. North Karnataka households eat day-old rotti with ennegayi and chutney pudi. Warm briefly on a tawa before serving.

recipes.name: Kadambuttu
recipes.subtitle: soft steamed rice dumplings, the standing partner to pandi curry

ingredients.note: coarse rice rava is traditional; fine rice flour gives a smoother, slightly softer dumpling
for fragrance and a little bite

prepNotes: Boil the water in a wide, heavy pan. A thin pan scorches the flour the moment it hits the base.
Shape the dumplings while the dough is still hot enough to be uncomfortable to hold. Cooled dough cracks and will not seal.
Keep a bowl of cold water beside you for dipping your palms between dumplings.
Have the steamer already at a rolling boil before the first dumpling is rolled.

steps.text: Bring the water to a full boil with the salt and coconut oil in a wide heavy pan.
Lower the heat to minimum and add the rice flour all at once, stirring hard with a wooden spoon.
steps.tip: Add it in one go, not in stages. Sprinkling flour in slowly is how you get lumps.

steps.text: Keep stirring 2 to 3 minutes until the mixture pulls away from the sides in a single rough mass with no dry flour left.
Cover the pan and leave it on the lowest heat for 5 minutes so the flour steams through.
Tip the dough onto a plate, scatter over the grated coconut and let it cool just enough to handle, about 3 minutes.
Knead the hot dough with wet hands for 3 minutes until it is completely smooth and slightly shiny.
steps.tip: This kneading is the whole recipe. Under-kneaded dough gives dumplings that crack open in the steamer.

steps.text: Break off lime-sized pieces and roll each between wet palms into a smooth ball with no seams or cracks.
Arrange the balls in a greased steamer plate, leaving a finger's gap between them.
Steam over rapidly boiling water for 12 minutes, until the surfaces look matt and set rather than wet.
Turn off the heat and leave them in the covered steamer 5 minutes before lifting them out.
steps.tip: Straight out of the steam they are sticky; the short rest firms them up.

recipes.storage: Best within a few hours. Keeps 2 days refrigerated in a covered box; re-steam 5 minutes to soften. They go hard and chalky in the fridge if left uncovered.

recipes.name: Kane Rava Fry
recipes.subtitle: ladyfish rubbed in red chilli paste and shallow fried in a sandy semolina crust

ingredients.qty: 8 whole ladyfish, cleaned and slit down both sides
ingredients.note: kane is the local name; small pomfret or mackerel fillets fry the same way

ingredients.qty: 8 dried, soaked 20 minutes in warm water

ingredients.note: this is wheat semolina, so the dish is not gluten-free
mixed into the rava, it keeps the crust crisp as the fish cools
fried in the last of the oil and scattered over

prepNotes: Rinse the fish, pat it thoroughly dry inside and out, and score the thicker fish twice on each side.
Grind the masala first, then marinate the fish for 30 minutes in the fridge. Much longer and the lemon starts cooking the flesh.
Spread the rava on a wide plate so you can press the fish into it in one motion.

steps.text: Grind the soaked chillies, garlic, ginger, tamarind, turmeric and pepper with 2 tbsp of the soaking water to a thick paste.
Mix in the lemon juice and 1 tsp salt, then rub the paste into the fish, working it into the slits.
Marinate 30 minutes in the fridge while you get the pan and the rava plate ready.
Stir the rice flour into the rava on a wide plate.
Heat 3 tbsp coconut oil in a flat tawa until a pinch of rava dropped in sizzles immediately.
steps.tip: If the oil is not hot enough the crust drinks it and goes soggy instead of crisping.

steps.text: Press each fish into the rava on both sides, shake off the loose grains and lay it straight into the pan.
steps.tip: Coat one fish at a time. Rava left sitting on a wet marinade turns to paste.

steps.text: Fry 4 minutes on the first side without touching it, until the crust is set and deep red-gold at the edges.
steps.tip: Moving it early is what tears the crust off. Wait until it releases from the pan on its own.

steps.text: Flip once and fry 3 minutes on the second side, adding the remaining oil around the edge of the pan as needed.
Fry the curry leaves in the last of the hot oil for 15 seconds and scatter them over the fish.
Drain on a rack, not on paper, and serve hot with raw onion and lemon.
steps.tip: A rack keeps the underside crisp; paper traps steam and softens it.

recipes.storage: Eat within the hour. This is a dish that does not keep. Leftovers will sit 1 day refrigerated and are best crisped up in a dry pan, never in a microwave.

recipes.name: Kesari Bath
recipes.subtitle: glossy saffron semolina pudding set soft with ghee, cashew and cardamom

image.credit: Harsha K R from Bangalore, India

ingredients.note: bombay rava, not the coarse idli variety

ingredients.qty: a generous pinch, soaked in 2 tbsp warm milk

ingredients.note: lifts the sweetness

prepNotes: Soak the saffron in warm milk for 15 minutes so the colour and scent are fully drawn out.
Measure the liquid at three times the volume of rava and have it simmering in a second pan before the rava is roasted. Cold liquid on hot rava lumps instantly.
Warm the sugar so it dissolves without dropping the temperature of the pan.

steps.text: Fry the cashews and raisins in 2 tbsp ghee until the nuts are golden and the raisins swell. Lift them out and set aside.
Add 2 tbsp more ghee to the kadhai and roast the rava over low-medium heat for 6 to 7 minutes until it smells nutty and each grain is separate and pale gold.
steps.tip: Roast on low. Rava browned too fast tastes toasted but is still raw inside, and the kesari turns gritty.

steps.text: In another pan bring the water, milk and pinch of salt to a rolling boil.
Pour the boiling liquid into the roasted rava in a steady stream while stirring hard and continuously with the other hand.
steps.tip: It will splutter violently. Keep stirring through it. This ten seconds decides whether you get lumps.

steps.text: Stir in the saffron milk, then cover and cook on low for 4 minutes until the rava has absorbed everything and looks fluffy.
Add the sugar all at once. The mixture will loosen and turn liquid again; do not panic.
steps.tip: Sugar always melts the mixture back down. Keep stirring and it firms up within four minutes.

steps.text: Stir over low heat for 5 minutes until it thickens and starts leaving the sides of the pan.
Drizzle in the remaining ghee a tablespoon at a time, stirring, until the kesari is glossy and no longer sticks to the pan.
Fold in the crushed cardamom and the fried cashews and raisins, and take it off the heat.
Serve warm, either spooned into bowls or pressed into a greased tray and cut into squares once cool.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. It sets firm when cold; reheat portions with a teaspoon of milk in a pan over low heat, or steam for 5 minutes, until soft and glossy again.

recipes.name: Koli Curry
recipes.subtitle: Kodava chicken curry in a roasted coconut and pepper gravy

ingredients.note: any more turns the gravy bitter
stands in for kachampuli, the dark Coorg sour vinegar; a spoon is enough. It is added off the heat at the very end
to finish

prepNotes: Rub the chicken with the turmeric and 1 tsp salt then cover and refrigerate it 30 minutes before cooking.
Grate the coconut fresh if you can; frozen grated coconut, thawed, is the next best thing.

steps.text: Dry-roast the coriander powder, cumin, dried red chilli, fenugreek and mustard seeds in a small pan over low heat for 2 minutes, until they smell nutty and the mustard begins to pop.
steps.tip: Low heat only. Fenugreek scorches first and its bitterness carries through the whole pot.

steps.text: Add the grated coconut to the same pan and roast, stirring constantly, 6 to 8 minutes until it is an even reddish brown.

Heat the coconut oil in a heavy pan and fry the onion until soft and gold, about 8 minutes.

Add the chicken and fry on medium-high for 6 minutes, turning the pieces, until the flesh is opaque and lightly coloured.
Stir in the ground coconut masala and fry 4 minutes until the oil separates at the edges and the paste darkens a shade.
steps.tip: This frying step is what stops the gravy tasting raw and chalky. Wait for the oil.

steps.text: Pour in the remaining 150 ml water and the crushed black pepper, cover and simmer on low 20 minutes until the chicken is tender at the bone.
Uncover and simmer 5 minutes more to thicken, then check the salt.
Off the heat, stir in the vinegar and the coriander leaves and rest 5 minutes before serving.
steps.tip: Kachampuli is potent and this curry needs only a hint of it. Taste before adding a second spoon.

recipes.name: Koli Saaru
recipes.subtitle: peppery kannadiga chicken curry in a roasted coconut and poppy seed gravy

ingredients.note: bone-in matters for the saaru
to finish

prepNotes: Rub the chicken with 1/2 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp salt then cover and refrigerate it 30 minutes while you make the masala.
Roast and grind the coconut masala before you start cooking. It cannot be rushed once the chicken is in the pan.
Use fresh coconut if you can. Desiccated gives a thinner, sweeter gravy.

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp of the coconut oil and fry the sliced onion 6 minutes until browned at the edges. Set aside.
In the same pan roast the red chillies, black pepper, cumin, cinnamon and cloves 1 minute until they smell sharp, then add the poppy seeds for 30 seconds.
Add the grated coconut and roast 4 minutes over medium-low, stirring constantly, until it turns an even golden brown and smells toasted.
steps.tip: Constant stirring, medium-low heat. Coconut scorches in patches and one burnt patch makes the whole saaru bitter.

steps.text: Cool, then grind the roasted spices, coconut, browned onion, garlic, ginger and coriander powder with 3/4 cup water to a very smooth dark paste.
Heat the remaining 3 tbsp coconut oil in a kadhai, add the curry leaves and the chopped onion and fry 8 minutes until soft and deep gold.
Add the tomato and remaining turmeric and cook 5 minutes until the tomato collapses and oil beads at the edges.
Add the chicken and fry on high 6 minutes, turning the pieces, until they are opaque all over and lightly seared.

steps.text: Stir in the ground masala and cook 6 minutes on medium, scraping the base, until it darkens by a shade and the oil separates.
Pour in 1 1/4 cups hot water and salt to taste, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 20 minutes on low until the chicken is falling off the bone and the gravy is the thickness of pouring cream.

recipes.name: Kori Rotti
recipes.subtitle: bunt chicken curry poured over crisp rice wafers that soften as you eat

ingredients.note: kori rotti wafers are sold ready-made; almost every home buys them
frozen grated coconut, thawed, works
byadgi if you can get it. Same deep red, gentle heat
this is where the actual heat comes from
any more and the gravy turns bitter

ingredients.qty: 2 medium, one sliced and one finely chopped

ingredients.note: loosens and rounds the gravy at the end

prepNotes: Soak the tamarind in 1/2 cup warm water for 20 minutes, then squeeze it out and strain.
Wipe the chicken dry and salt it lightly 30 minutes ahead so the masala has something to grip.
Keep the rotti wafers sealed until the curry is actually on the table. They lose their crackle in humid air.

steps.text: Roast the kashmiri and hot chillies in 1 tsp of the coconut oil over low heat until they darken a shade and smell toasty, about 2 minutes.
steps.tip: Pull them out the second they smell nutty. Scorched chilli makes the whole pot bitter and there is no fixing it.

steps.text: In the same pan roast the coriander powder, cumin, fenugreek and pepper for 1 minute until fragrant, then tip everything onto a plate to cool.

steps.text: Heat the remaining coconut oil in a kadhai, crackle the curry leaves and cook the chopped onion until translucent, about 4 minutes.

Stir in the ground masala and fry it down for 8 minutes, until it darkens and oil beads at the edge of the pan.

steps.text: Pour in 2 cups water and the tamarind extract, salt it, and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes until the chicken is tender and the gravy just coats a spoon.

steps.text: Break the rotti wafers into wide bowls and ladle the hot curry over them at the table.

recipes.subtitle: quick hill mushroom curry heavy with black pepper and coconut

ingredients.note: wild mushrooms after the first rains are the Kodagu version; button or oyster mushrooms stand in well
the defining flavour, crush it fresh
to finish

prepNotes: Wipe the mushrooms with a damp cloth instead of washing them; soaked mushrooms release water into the pan and refuse to brown.

Crush the black pepper coarsely just before cooking.

recipes.name: Kundapur Chicken Ghee Roast
recipes.subtitle: chicken cloaked in a dark tangy byadgi masala fried down in a serious amount of ghee

ingredients.note: thighs and drumsticks hold up best
for the marinade
the dish is named for it, so do not cut it back
byadgi gives the signature colour without the burn
takes the edge off the sourness

prepNotes: Marinate the chicken in the yogurt, lemon juice, turmeric and 1 tsp salt for at least 1 hour, or overnight in the fridge.
Soak the chillies and the tamarind in separate bowls of warm water for 20 minutes.
Bring the marinated chicken back to room temperature before it hits the pan, or it will steam instead of roast.

steps.text: Drain the soaked chillies and grind them with the garlic, coriander powder, cumin, fenugreek, pepper and tamarind pulp to a thick, smooth paste using as little water as possible.
steps.tip: Keep the paste stiff. A watery masala will never fry down into the glossy coat this dish is about.

steps.text: Melt 3 tbsp ghee in a kadhai and fry the marinated chicken over high heat for 6 minutes, until the pieces are sealed and patched with brown.
Lift the chicken out onto a plate, leaving the ghee and any juices behind.
Add the remaining ghee to the same pan and fry the ground masala on a low flame for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring often.
steps.tip: It is ready when the raw chilli smell is gone, the colour has gone from bright red to brick, and ghee pools clearly at the sides.

steps.text: Stir in the jaggery and 1/2 tsp salt and cook another minute.
Return the chicken with its juices, toss to coat every piece, add 1/2 cup water and cover.
Cook on low for 15 minutes, turning the pieces twice, until the chicken is done and the masala clings to it with almost no gravy left.
steps.tip: If it looks wet at the end, take the lid off and raise the heat for 2 minutes to dry it out.

steps.text: Throw in the curry leaves, let them crisp in the hot ghee for 30 seconds, and take it off the heat.
Rest 5 minutes before serving with neer dosa or plain rice.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. The ghee will set solid when cold, so reheat covered on low with 2 tbsp water and it comes back glossy. It does not freeze well.

recipes.name: Maddur Vada
recipes.subtitle: flat, shatteringly crisp onion fritters from the railway platform at maddur

ingredients.note: fine chiroti rava if available
the hot fat is what makes them crisp
for deep frying

prepNotes: Chop the onion as finely as you can. Coarse pieces steam inside the vada and leave it soft.
Melt the ghee until it is smoking-hot before rubbing it into the flours; warm ghee will not give the same short, crumbly bite.
Mix the dough only when the oil is nearly at temperature. Standing dough goes wet as the onion releases water.

steps.text: Combine the rice flour, rava, maida, salt, hing and cumin in a wide bowl.
Pour over the hot ghee and rub it through the flour with your fingertips for a minute, until the mix holds its shape when squeezed in a fist.
steps.tip: This step is the whole recipe. Skimp on it and you get chewy vadas.

steps.text: Add the onion, green chilli, curry leaves and coriander leaves and mix with your hands, crushing the onion slightly.
Add water a tablespoon at a time to a stiff, barely-together dough. It should be firmer than a chapati dough.
steps.tip: Stop early. A wet dough will not hold a thin round in the oil.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadhai to medium. A pinch of dough should rise steadily in about 5 seconds, not shoot to the surface.
Take a lime-sized ball, place it on an oiled sheet of plastic or a wet palm, and press it flat into a thin 9cm disc.
Peel it off and slide it into the oil. Fry 3 to 4 vadas at a time for 4 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and the bubbling has almost stopped.
steps.tip: The sound tells you more than the colour. When the fierce hiss drops to a whisper, the moisture is out and it will be crisp.

steps.text: Lift onto paper and repeat with the rest, letting the oil come back to temperature between batches.
Serve hot with coconut chutney and filter coffee.

recipes.storage: Best within an hour of frying. They keep 2 days in an airtight tin at room temperature and can be re-crisped in a 160C oven for 5 minutes.

recipes.name: Majjige Huli
recipes.subtitle: gentle udupi buttermilk curry with ash gourd in a coconut-cumin paste

ingredients.note: or bottle-gourd
sour but not sharp
for the paste
thickens the gravy
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Soak the toor dal in warm water for 30 minutes before you start; it grinds smooth and thickens the curry without any flour.
Whisk the yogurt with 1/2 cup water until completely lump-free and leave it at room temperature so it does not shock the hot pot.
Grind the coconut paste first and keep it ready. The curry comes together in five minutes once the gourd is cooked.

steps.text: Simmer the ash gourd with the turmeric, 1 tsp salt and 1 cup water for 10 minutes until a knife slides through but the cubes still hold shape.
steps.tip: Overcooked gourd turns to mush and clouds the curry.

steps.text: Meanwhile grind the coconut, green chillies, cumin seeds and drained toor dal with 1/2 cup water to a very smooth, thick paste.
steps.tip: Grind longer than feels necessary. Any grit in the paste stays grit in the curry.

steps.text: Stir the paste into the cooked gourd and simmer 5 minutes on medium, stirring often, until the raw coconut smell is gone and the gravy coats the spoon.
Take the pot off the heat and let it stop bubbling, about 2 minutes.
Pour in the whisked yogurt, stirring continuously, then return to the lowest heat.
steps.tip: Adding yogurt to a boiling pot will split it. Off the heat, then low, always.

steps.text: Warm through 3 minutes without letting it boil. The surface should barely tremble. Check the salt.
Heat the coconut oil in a small pan, crackle the mustard seeds, then add the broken red chillies, curry leaves and hing and fry 10 seconds.
Pour the tempering over the curry, scatter the coriander leaves and serve hot with plain rice.

ingredients.note: the riper and blacker the better

prepNotes: Despite the name they are puris, not bread. The dough must rest 6 hours or overnight, which is where the flavour comes from.

steps.text: Mash the bananas with the sugar until liquid, then mix in the curd, cumin, soda and salt.

recipes.name: Meen Gassi
recipes.subtitle: coastal fish curry in a roasted coconut gravy soured with kokum

ingredients.qty: 600g seer or pomfret, cut into thick steaks
ingredients.note: any firm-fleshed fish that will not fall apart
tamarind will do at a pinch but the colour and the clean sourness change

prepNotes: Rub the fish with 1/4 tsp turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt and leave it 15 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
Soak the kokum in 1/2 cup warm water for 15 minutes.
Grate the coconut before you start. The grinding is the only fiddly part of this curry.

steps.text: Warm 1 tsp coconut oil in a pan and roast the chillies over low heat for 1 minute until they puff slightly and smell toasted.
Add the coriander powder, cumin, fenugreek and pepper and roast 45 seconds more, then take the pan off the heat.
steps.tip: Fenugreek burns faster than anything else here. If it goes dark brown, start the spice roast again.

steps.text: Grind the roasted spices with the grated coconut, garlic and the remaining turmeric and 3/4 cup water into a smooth, thick orange paste.
Heat 2 tbsp coconut oil in a wide pan, pop the mustard seeds and add the curry leaves.
Cook the onion until soft and just turning gold at the edges, about 6 minutes.
Pour in the ground masala and 1 1/4 cups water, add the kokum with its soaking liquid and salt, and bring it to a gentle simmer.
Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until the raw coconut smell is gone and the gravy thickens enough to coat a spoon.
steps.tip: Stir every couple of minutes. Ground coconut catches on the base of the pan very easily.

steps.text: Slide the fish steaks in in a single layer, spoon gravy over them and cook 7 to 8 minutes without stirring.
steps.tip: Never stir fish curry. Tilt and swirl the pan instead, or you will end up with flakes in gravy.

steps.text: Drizzle over the last 1 tsp raw coconut oil, cover and let it stand 10 minutes off the heat before serving with red rice.

recipes.name: Mysore Pak
recipes.subtitle: porous gram flour fudge that dissolves in ghee as you bite it

ingredients.note: sifting is not optional. Lumps do not come out later

ingredients.qty: 1.5 cups, melted and kept hot on a low flame
ingredients.note: hot ghee is absorbed; cool ghee sits on top

prepNotes: Grease a 20cm tray and keep it next to the stove. You will have about 30 seconds to pour.
Melt the whole quantity of ghee in a separate pan and keep it hot throughout; you add it ladle by ladle.
Sift the besan twice and warm it in a dry pan for 2 minutes so it absorbs ghee readily.
Read the whole method first. Once the sugar syrup is at one-string, there is no pausing.

steps.text: Dissolve the sugar in the water and boil until the syrup reaches one-string consistency, about 6 minutes.
steps.tip: Test by pulling a cooled drop between thumb and finger. A single thread that holds is right.

steps.text: Lower the heat and add the sifted besan in a thin stream, whisking hard so no lumps form.
Whisk until the mixture is smooth and glossy, about 1 minute.
Start adding the hot ghee one ladle at a time, stirring constantly and waiting until each ladle is absorbed.
steps.tip: Adding ghee faster than the batter can drink it gives a greasy, dense slab.

steps.text: Keep going for 12 to 15 minutes as the mixture froths, bubbles and rises in the pan.
Watch for the moment it turns porous and foamy and the last ghee refuses to be absorbed and pools at the sides.
steps.tip: That refusal is the signal. Miss it and the sweet sets hard and chewy.

steps.text: Pour it into the greased tray immediately without scraping the pan and level the top with the back of a ladle.
Wait 4 minutes, then score it into diamonds while still hot.
steps.tip: Score too late and it shatters; too early and the lines close up again.

steps.text: Cool completely for an hour before lifting the pieces out.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight tin at room temperature. Do not refrigerate. It goes hard and loses its porous crumb.

recipes.name: Neer Dosa
recipes.subtitle: lacy, paper-thin rice crepes from the coast, soft and faintly sweet

image.alt: Neer dosa, the thin rice crepe of coastal Karnataka

ingredients.note: sona masoori or any short-grain raw rice

prepNotes: Soak the rice 5 hours or overnight. Neer dosa has no fermentation and no leavening, so the soak is what makes the batter grind fine.
Neer means water: the finished batter should be as thin as full-fat milk and run straight off the ladle in a stream.
Season a cast iron tawa properly beforehand. On a poorly seasoned pan these tear every time.

steps.text: Drain the soaked rice and grind it with the grated coconut and 250ml water to a completely smooth batter, 4 to 5 minutes in the blender.
steps.tip: Rub a drop between your fingers. Any grittiness at all means it needs another two minutes.

steps.text: Pour into a bowl, stir in the salt and thin with the remaining water until it is the consistency of thin milk.
steps.tip: This will feel far too thin. It is meant to. A pourable-but-thick batter gives you a chapati, not a neer dosa.

steps.text: Heat the tawa over medium-high until a drop of water skitters across it, then wipe it with a coconut-oil-dipped cloth.
Stir the batter well, then pour a ladleful from a height onto the hot tawa, moving in a spiral from the outside in. Do not spread it with the ladle.
steps.tip: Filling gaps with extra batter is the instinct to resist; a hole or two is the mark of a proper neer dosa.

steps.text: Cover and cook 60 to 90 seconds until the surface loses its wet sheen and the edges lift on their own.
Do not flip. Fold the dosa in half and then in half again with a spatula and slide it onto a plate.
Wipe the tawa with the oiled cloth between each dosa and stir the batter every time, since the rice settles fast.
steps.tip: Stir before every single ladle. The batter separates within a minute.

steps.text: Serve warm with coconut chutney, a jaggery-coconut filling, or a coastal fish curry.

recipes.storage: Best eaten within a couple of hours, stacked and covered with a cloth so they stay pliable. The batter keeps 2 days refrigerated; whisk and re-thin with water before using.

recipes.name: Otti
recipes.subtitle: thin rice flatbread pressed by hand and cooked on a griddle

ingredients.note: optional but common in Kodagu homes
for the griddle and for oiling your palms

prepNotes: Take the dough out in portions and keep the rest covered with a damp cloth; exposed rice dough dries within minutes and will not spread.
Cut two squares of banana leaf or greaseproof paper for patting the rotis out. A plastic sheet works too.
Heat the griddle on medium while you shape the first roti so it is ready when you are.

steps.text: Bring the water to a boil with the salt and 1 tsp of the coconut oil.
Turn the heat to its lowest, add the rice flour all at once and stir hard until no dry flour is visible, about 2 minutes.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat for 4 minutes, then turn the dough out onto a plate.
Add the grated coconut and knead the hot dough with oiled hands for 3 minutes until smooth and pliable, like soft clay.
steps.tip: It must be kneaded hot. Once it cools the starch sets and the roti will crack at every edge.

steps.text: Divide into 8 balls and keep them under a damp cloth.
Place a ball on an oiled sheet and pat it out with your palm and fingertips into a 15 cm round, turning as you go.
steps.tip: Pat from the centre outwards and keep the thickness even; thin patches burn before the thick ones cook.

steps.text: Lift the roti onto a hot griddle and cook 90 seconds, until the underside shows brown freckles.
Flip and cook the second side 90 seconds, pressing the edges down with a cloth so it puffs slightly.
Brush with a little coconut oil, stack in a covered box and repeat with the rest.
steps.tip: Stacking them covered lets the steam soften each one; left out singly they stiffen fast.

recipes.storage: Best hot off the griddle. Keeps a day wrapped in a cloth in a covered box; reheat 30 seconds a side on a dry griddle. Do not refrigerate, they turn brittle.

recipes.name: Pandi Curry
recipes.subtitle: the Coorg pork curry, black with pepper and sharpened with kachampuli

ingredients.qty: 1 kg shoulder with its fat and skin, cut into 3 cm cubes
ingredients.note: fat matters here. A lean cut gives a thin curry
the backbone of the dish, not a garnish
for colour without extra heat
stands in for kachampuli, the dark Coorg sour vinegar pressed from wild garcinia; use it sparingly and only at the end, as a sour finish rather than a marinade
only if your pork is lean; a fatty cut renders plenty of its own

prepNotes: Cut the pork the evening before if you can and keep it refrigerated, uncovered, so the surface dries. It browns far better.
Crush the black pepper in a mortar rather than a grinder. You want gritty, uneven pieces, not powder.
Have the vinegar measured and standing by the stove; it goes in off the heat and the timing is easy to miss.

steps.text: Put the pork, turmeric, 1 tsp of the crushed pepper and 1 tsp salt in a heavy pot over medium heat, with no oil and no water.
steps.tip: Coorg pork starts dry so it renders its own fat. Adding liquid now gives you boiled meat.

steps.text: Cover and cook 20 minutes, stirring twice; the pork throws off a lot of cloudy grey liquid.
Uncover, raise the heat and boil that liquid away until the fat starts spitting and the cubes catch gold at the edges, about 15 minutes.
Push the meat to one side and add the onion, ginger, garlic, green chilli and curry leaves to the rendered fat.
Fry the aromatics until the onion is soft and evenly gold, about 10 minutes, then stir everything together.
Add the coriander powder, crushed cumin, chilli powder, kashmiri chilli, cinnamon and cloves and fry 3 minutes until the pot smells toasted.
steps.tip: Keep the heat moderate. Powdered spice burns in hot pork fat in under a minute and turns the curry bitter.

steps.text: Pour in the hot water, scrape the base clean, cover and simmer on low 45 minutes until the pork cuts with the side of a spoon.
Stir in the remaining crushed black pepper and simmer uncovered 10 minutes, until the gravy is dark and clings to the meat.
Take the pot off the heat, stir in the vinegar, cover and leave it 10 minutes before serving.
steps.tip: Add the sour off the heat. Boiled vinegar goes flat and dull, and the whole point of kachampuli is a bright edge against the fat.

steps.text: Taste and correct salt and sourness, adding vinegar a half teaspoon at a time. Serve with kadambuttu or otti.

recipes.name: Pork Bafat
recipes.subtitle: catholic wedding-table pork stewed in bafat masala and sharpened with vinegar

ingredients.qty: 1kg belly and shoulder with the fat on, cut into 2 inch cubes
ingredients.note: lean pork makes a thin, disappointing bafat
coconut or palm vinegar is what is used at home
they soak up the fat and stretch the dish

prepNotes: Grind the bafat powder a day ahead if you can. Dry-roasted and jarred, it keeps for months and is the shortcut every Mangalorean Catholic kitchen relies on.
Rub the pork with 1 tbsp of the vinegar, the turmeric and 2 tsp salt and leave it at least 2 hours, or overnight in the fridge.
Take the pork out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking.

steps.text: Dry roast the chillies, coriander powder, cumin, pepper, cloves, cinnamon and mustard seeds separately over low heat until each smells toasted, 1 to 2 minutes each.
steps.tip: Roast them separately. Cloves and mustard are done long before the chillies are, and one burnt spice ruins the batch.

steps.text: Cool completely and grind to a fine powder. This is your bafat masala.
steps.tip: Grinding warm spices makes a damp, clumping powder that will not keep.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the onion over medium heat for 12 minutes, until soft and evenly gold.
Add the crushed garlic and ginger and cook 2 minutes more, until the raw edge is gone.
Stir in 4 tbsp of the bafat masala and fry for 2 minutes with a splash of water so it does not catch.
Add the marinated pork and turn it over high heat for 8 minutes, until the cubes are sealed and coated.
Pour in 2 cups water, cover and simmer on low for 50 minutes, or pressure cook for 4 whistles and let the pressure fall on its own.
steps.tip: The fat must render properly. If the pork is still firm at 50 minutes, give it another 15. This is not a dish to rush.

steps.text: Add the potatoes and cook uncovered 15 minutes, until they are tender and the gravy has thickened around them.
Stir in the remaining 3 tbsp vinegar, check the salt, and simmer 5 minutes more.
steps.tip: Vinegar goes in at the end. Boiled long it turns flat and loses the sharpness that cuts the fat.

steps.text: Rest the pot off the heat for 20 minutes before serving with sanna or plain rice.

recipes.name: Pundi Gatti
recipes.subtitle: steamed tulu rice dumplings speckled with coconut and mustard, eaten with curry or chutney

ingredients.qty: 1 1/2 cups short-grain raw rice, soaked 4 hours
ingredients.note: the coarse grind is what gives pundi its bite. Do not use rice flour

prepNotes: Soak the rice at least 4 hours, or overnight. It must grind coarse but soft, like wet semolina.
Set the steamer water boiling before you shape the dumplings so they go in hot and do not sit and dry out.
Keep a small bowl of water beside you for wetting your palms while rolling.

steps.text: Drain the soaked rice well and grind it coarse with 1/2 cup water. Aim for the texture of wet rava, not a smooth batter.
steps.tip: Stop while you can still feel grains between your fingers. Ground smooth, the dumplings turn gluey.

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp coconut oil in a heavy pan, pop the mustard seeds and fry the urad dal until it turns light gold, about 1 minute.
Add the green chilli and curry leaves and let them crackle for 20 seconds.
Pour in 1 cup water with the salt and bring it to a rolling boil.
Tip in the ground rice and the grated coconut all at once and stir hard over low heat.
Keep stirring for 6 to 8 minutes until the mixture pulls away from the sides in one lump and no longer sticks to the spoon.
steps.tip: If it still smears the pan, it needs another 2 minutes. A wet dough gives dumplings that collapse in the steamer.

steps.text: Cover the pan and let the dough cool for 10 minutes, until it is warm enough to handle but not cold.
steps.tip: Roll while it is still warm. Cold pundi dough cracks and will not hold a ball.

steps.text: With wet palms roll the dough into 12 smooth balls the size of a lime, pressing out any cracks.
Steam them in a single layer for 12 to 15 minutes, until they are glossy and a skewer comes out clean.
Rest 5 minutes off the heat before lifting them out, and serve hot with chicken curry, chana gashi or coconut chutney.
steps.tip: Lifting them straight from the steamer tears the skin; the 5 minute rest firms them up.

recipes.name: Ragi Mudde
recipes.subtitle: smooth finger-millet balls, the everyday staple of the southern Karnataka plate

image.alt: Ragi mudde, finger millet balls, with chicken curry

ingredients.note: fine, freshly milled if you can get it

prepNotes: Keep a bowl of cold water beside the stove. You shape the mudde with wet hands.
Mix 2 tbsp of the ragi flour into 1/2 cup cold water to a lump-free slurry before you start; this goes in first and stops the whole pot from seizing.
Have a heavy wooden spatula or a mudde kolu ready. A thin spoon will bend.

steps.text: Bring 4 cups water to a hard rolling boil with the salt in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Stir in the cold ragi slurry and let it boil 3 minutes until the water turns opaque brown and thickens slightly.
steps.tip: This pre-thickened base is what stops raw lumps forming later.

steps.text: Lower the heat to minimum and tip in the remaining ragi flour all at once, in a mound in the centre. Do not stir.
Cover and let it steam 5 minutes. The mound cooks through from the sides in.
steps.tip: Stirring now is the classic mistake. Let the steam do the work.

steps.text: Uncover and beat hard with the wooden spatula, pressing the dough against the side of the pot, for 4 to 5 minutes until it is one glossy, uniform mass with no pale flecks.
Cook another 3 minutes on low, folding the mass over itself, until it pulls cleanly away from the pot.
Wet your hands in the cold water, scoop out a fistful and roll it into a smooth ball the size of a small orange.
steps.tip: Work fast while it is hot; a cooled mass cracks instead of rounding.

steps.text: Serve immediately with hot saaru or bassaru, swallowing the pieces rather than chewing them.

recipes.storage: Best eaten within the hour. Leftover mudde stiffens; steam it for 5 minutes to soften, or crumble it into hot saaru.
