the body of the sauce, not a garnish
for colour without much heat
the flavour people cannot place
balances the tomato, it should not taste sweet

prepNotes: The gravy is boiled and blended, not fried in the usual bhuna way. That is what keeps it smooth and bright rather than dark.

steps.text: Simmer 10 minutes until it thickens and the butter shows at the edges. Season with salt and the sugar.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 230C with a rack in the upper third.
Thread the paneer and vegetables alternately onto skewers, leaving a small gap between pieces.

Rest 3 minutes, then dust with chaat masala and squeeze over lemon.
Serve hot with sliced onion and mint chutney.

recipes.name: Pindi Chole
recipes.subtitle: dark, dry rawalpindi chickpeas soured with pomegranate seed and amchur, no onion or tomato

ingredients.note: softens the skins in the cooker
tied in the boil, this is what blackens the chickpeas
in the boil
in the boil
in the boil
the defining sourness
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free
or ghee, which takes it out of vegan
half in, half over the top
to scatter over

prepNotes: Soak the chickpeas overnight in plenty of water with a pinch of salt. Under-soaked chana takes much longer to go floury, and some of it never quite gets there while the rest collapses.
Traditionally a tea bag or a few dried amla pieces are dropped into the boil to blacken the chickpeas. Whole black cardamom, cinnamon, cloves and bay do the same job and taste better.
Grind the anardana coarsely just before cooking. Ready-ground pomegranate powder goes flat within weeks.

steps.text: Tie the black cardamom, cinnamon, bay and cloves in a small muslin bundle. Pressure cook the drained chickpeas with the bundle, the baking soda, salt and 1 litre of water for 5 whistles, then 15 minutes on low.
steps.tip: The chickpeas should crush to paste between thumb and finger. If they still have a bite, cook them longer before you go anywhere near the masala.

steps.text: Lift out the spice bundle and squeeze it against the side of the pot. Drain the chickpeas but keep 300ml of the black cooking liquor.
Dry-roast the ground anardana, coriander powder, cumin powder, crushed pepper, dry ginger and amchur in a kadhai over low heat for 90 seconds, until the pan smells sharp and toasty. Tip onto a plate.
steps.tip: This is the whole flavour of pindi chole. Off the heat the second it smells nutty. Burnt anardana turns acrid.

steps.text: Heat the oil in the same kadhai, add the ajwain and asafoetida and let them foam for 10 seconds.

Scatter the remaining ginger matchsticks, coriander and pomegranate seeds over the top and serve with lemon wedges and kulcha or bhatura.

recipes.name: Punjabi Chana Dal
recipes.subtitle: nutty split gram dal cooked to just-holding grains under a garlic tadka

ingredients.qty: 1 cup (200g), rinsed until the water runs clear

ingredients.note: use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free. Most brands are cut with wheat flour

prepNotes: Soak the chana dal 45 minutes in warm water and drain. It cooks unevenly otherwise, some grains mush and some still hard.

steps.text: Pressure cook the drained dal with 3 cups water and the turmeric for 12 minutes at full pressure, then let the pressure fall on its own.

Add the onion and fry 7 minutes until soft and gold at the edges.
Stir in the ginger, half the garlic and the green chillies, and fry 90 seconds.

Tip in the cooked dal with its liquid, add 1/2 cup hot water, and simmer 12 minutes so the flavours settle in.

steps.text: Stir in the garam masala and amchur and taste for salt.

steps.text: Pour the garlic ghee over the dal, scatter the coriander, and serve with roti.

recipes.name: Punjabi Kadhi Pakora
recipes.subtitle: tangy yogurt and gram flour gravy simmered thick, with soft onion fritters dropped in

ingredients.note: the sourer the better. Leave it out of the fridge overnight

ingredients.qty: 1 cup (100g) total: 6 tbsp for the kadhi, the rest for the pakoras

ingredients.note: for the pakoras
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Leave the yogurt out of the fridge overnight so it sours properly. Fresh sweet yogurt makes a flat, milky kadhi.
Whisk the yogurt and besan together until there is not a single lump before any heat touches it.
Fry the pakoras while the kadhi simmers, and add them only at the end so they keep some structure.

steps.text: Whisk the sour yogurt with 6 tbsp besan, the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and 1 tsp salt until completely smooth, then whisk in 4 cups water.
steps.tip: Any lump you leave now will still be there an hour later. Push it through a sieve if in doubt.

steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a heavy pot, crackle the fenugreek and cumin seeds for 30 seconds, then add the asafoetida, half the ginger, the garlic and half the green chillies.
Pour in the yogurt mixture and bring it to a boil on medium, stirring constantly in one direction.
steps.tip: Do not stop stirring until it boils, or the yogurt will split into curds and whey.

steps.text: Once it boils, drop to the lowest heat and simmer uncovered 40 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes.
steps.tip: The kadhi should reduce by a third and turn from milky to a deep gold. This slow cook is the whole dish.

steps.text: Meanwhile make the pakora batter: mix the remaining besan with the sliced onion, remaining ginger and chilli, 1/2 tsp salt and just enough water to bind, about 4 tbsp.
Heat the oil in a kadhai to 175C and drop in rough spoonfuls of batter, 6 at a time.
Fry 4 minutes, turning, until deep gold and firm, then drain on a rack. Loose, craggy spoonfuls fry lighter than neat balls.
Slide the pakoras into the simmering kadhi and cook 8 minutes more so they drink up the gravy but keep their shape.
Taste for salt. Sour kadhi needs a firm hand with it.
For the final tempering, heat the last tablespoon of ghee, take it off the heat, stir in the kashmiri chilli and broken red chillies, and pour it over the kadhi.

recipes.name: Rajma Chawal

ingredients.note: the small dark Jammu variety if you can find it

crushed, not mashed
for deep frying

prepNotes: The pastry is short, not soft: rub plenty of oil into the flour until it holds a shape when squeezed. That is what makes it crisp rather than chewy.

steps.text: Rub 6 tbsp of the oil and the ajwain into the maida until the mixture holds together when pressed in your fist.

steps.tip: Warm filling makes the pastry damp and it splits in the oil.

steps.text: Roll a ball of dough into an oval, cut it in half, form a cone from each, fill, and seal the edge with a wet finger, pressing firmly.
steps.tip: Any gap and the samosa drinks oil.

steps.text: Meanwhile heat the ghee in a small pan and fry the chopped onion until golden brown, about 8 minutes.

prepNotes: Water is the enemy. Squeeze the grated onion until it is genuinely dry, or the mince slides off the skewer.

recipes.subtitle: yogurt and chilli marinated chicken charred hard at the edges, done in a home oven

200g, thick and hung 30 minutes in a cloth
2 inch, made into a paste with the garlic

ingredients.qty: 2, one juiced and one in wedges
3 tbsp, heated to smoking and cooled

recipes.name: Aam ki Launji
recipes.subtitle: raw mango cooked down with jaggery, fennel and nigella into a sweet-sour relish

ingredients.note: firm and sour, not turning ripe
adjust to how sour the mangoes are
just a few seeds, for the bitter note
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Taste a sliver of the raw mango before you start. A very sour mango needs the full 180g of jaggery; a milder one needs closer to 120g.

steps.text: Add the jaggery and stir until it melts completely. Uncover and simmer 8-10 minutes.

steps.text: Cool completely before jarring. Serve alongside dal baati, puri or paratha.

recipes.name: Bajre ki Raab
recipes.subtitle: a thin savoury millet gruel loosened with buttermilk and warmed with dry ginger

the warming element the dish is drunk for

prepNotes: Bring the buttermilk to room temperature. Fridge-cold buttermilk hitting hot flour makes lumps instantly.
This is drunk from a glass or a bowl, not eaten with a spoon, so aim for the consistency of thin cream.
In Rajasthani homes raab is made in winter and given to new mothers and to anyone with a cold, which is why the dry ginger is not optional.

steps.text: Pour in 400ml water a little at a time, whisking hard after each addition so the flour stays smooth.
steps.tip: Water in stages, not all at once. Once lumps form you cannot whisk them out.

steps.text: Bring to a boil, then simmer on low 8 minutes, stirring often, until it thickens to a pourable gruel.
Take the pan off the heat and let it cool for 2 minutes.
Whisk the buttermilk smooth and stir it in gradually. Return to the lowest heat for 3 minutes, stirring, and do not let it boil.
steps.tip: A boil will split the buttermilk into curds and whey.

steps.text: Season with salt, the dry ginger powder and the turmeric. Stir in the jaggery now if you want the sweet version.

ingredients.note: buy it fresh. Bajra flour goes bitter within a few weeks
a lump melted on each hot roti

recipes.subtitle: dense granular fudge of ghee-roasted gram flour, sweet and toasty

sprinkled in mid-roast to form the granules

recipes.name: Gatta Pulao
recipes.subtitle: basmati layered with fried besan dumplings and whole spices, a marwari one-pot

ingredients.note: binds the gatta dough
1 in the dough, 3 for frying the gatte
split between dough and rice

ingredients.qty: 1 litre for boiling the gatte, plus 550ml for the rice

prepNotes: Soak the rice 30 minutes and drain it well. Wet rice steams unevenly and the grains break when you fold in the gatte.
Make and fry the gatte first, before anything else goes on the stove. They need to be cool enough to handle when you cut them.
Measure the water for the rice by volume against the drained rice: a shade under 2 parts water to 1 part rice, since the gatte give off none.

steps.text: Rub the besan with 1 tbsp oil, the yogurt, ajwain, 1/4 tsp turmeric, half the chilli powder and salt, then knead into a stiff dough with a splash of water. Rest 10 minutes.
Roll into 3 ropes about 1.5cm thick and drop them into 1 litre of boiling salted water. Boil 10 minutes until they float and feel firm. Lift out, cool, and cut into 2cm pieces.
steps.tip: Boil, do not simmer. A slack boil leaves the centres pasty.

steps.text: Fry the pieces in 3 tbsp oil over medium heat until golden on all sides, about 5 minutes. Drain and set aside.
In a heavy pot heat the ghee and add the cumin, bay leaf, cloves, cinnamon and black cardamom. Wait for the cumin to darken and the spices to smell sweet, about 30 seconds.
Add the sliced onion and fry 8 minutes on medium until evenly golden brown at the edges.
steps.tip: Golden, not brown-black. Burnt onion turns the whole pot bitter and there is no hiding it in a pulao.

steps.text: Add the ginger and green chilli, fry 1 minute, then the remaining turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder with 2 tbsp water. Cook 2 minutes.
Tip in the drained rice and turn it gently in the masala for 2 minutes until every grain is coated and looks glassy at the edges.
steps.tip: Use a flat spatula and fold rather than stir, or you will snap the grains.

steps.text: Add 550ml hot water and salt. Bring to a rolling boil, then scatter the fried gatte over the top without stirring them in.
Cover tightly, drop to the lowest heat and cook 12 minutes. Do not lift the lid.
Rest off the heat, still covered, 10 minutes. Then fold through the coriander, garam masala and lemon juice with a fork.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat covered with 2 tbsp water sprinkled over, on low or in a steamer, so the rice does not dry out. Freezes poorly. The gatte go spongy.

recipes.name: Gatte ki Sabzi
recipes.subtitle: steamed gram-flour dumplings simmered in a tangy yogurt gravy

ingredients.note: coarse besan gives a better bite than fine
sour yogurt is better than fresh here
for the dough. It keeps the gatte from sitting heavy
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

ingredients.qty: 1.2 litres for boiling, plus 250ml for the gravy

prepNotes: Take the yogurt out of the fridge 30 minutes ahead. Cold yogurt splits the moment it hits hot fat.
Whisk the yogurt with the turmeric, chilli and coriander powders before you start cooking, so it goes into the pan as one smooth slurry.
Keep the boiling water at a proper rolling boil before the gatte go in. Slack water makes them soggy.

steps.text: Knead the besan with 2 tbsp ghee, the ajwain, 1/2 tsp salt and about 4 tbsp yogurt into a stiff, smooth dough. It should feel like firm putty, not sticky.
steps.tip: Too much liquid and the gatte turn spongy. Add yogurt a spoon at a time.

steps.text: Rest the dough 10 minutes, then roll into 4 ropes about 1.5cm thick.
Slide the ropes into rolling boiling water and cook 12-14 minutes, until they float and the surface looks matte rather than shiny.
steps.tip: They puff slightly; a clean skewer pushed in should come out dry.

steps.text: Lift out, cool 5 minutes, and cut into 2cm pieces. Save 250ml of the cooking water. It is the body of the gravy.
Heat the remaining 2 tbsp ghee, crackle the cumin, add the hing and broken red chilli, and let them darken for 10 seconds.
Pour in the spiced yogurt and stir continuously on low heat for 4-5 minutes until it stops looking grainy and a film of ghee shows at the edge.
steps.tip: Do not stop stirring before it comes to a simmer, or it will curdle.

steps.text: Add the reserved cooking water and salt, and simmer 8 minutes until the gravy coats a spoon.
Slip in the gatte and simmer another 5 minutes so they drink up the gravy.
steps.tip: Add them late. Long boiling in the gravy makes them fall apart.

steps.text: Crush in the kasuri methi, sprinkle the garam masala and coriander leaves, and rest 5 minutes off the heat before serving with bajre ki roti.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated; the gatte keep absorbing gravy, so loosen with 3-4 tbsp hot water when reheating on low heat. Do not freeze. The yogurt gravy separates.

recipes.name: Govind Gatte
recipes.subtitle: besan dumplings stuffed with khoya and nuts, simmered in a yogurt gravy

ingredients.note: the gatta dough

ingredients.qty: 2 tbsp thick, for the dough plus 250g whisked for the gravy

ingredients.note: keeps the gatte from turning rubbery
the stuffing
for the stuffing
for finishing
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free
for colour without heat

ingredients.qty: 1.2 litres for boiling, plus 300ml for the gravy

prepNotes: Take the yogurt out of the fridge an hour ahead. Cold yogurt splits the moment it meets a hot pan.
Mix the stuffing first and chill it 15 minutes. A firm filling is far easier to seal inside the dough.
The gatta dough should be stiff, like a puri dough. Wet dough will not hold a stuffing.

steps.text: Rub the besan with 2 tbsp oil, the thick yogurt, ajwain, baking soda, 1/4 tsp turmeric and salt until it looks like coarse crumbs, then bring it together with a tablespoon or two of water into a stiff dough. Knead 2 minutes and rest 10 minutes.
steps.tip: Add water a teaspoon at a time. Besan takes up far less than you expect.

steps.text: Mash the khoya with the cashew, raisins, dried coconut, cracked pepper and a pinch of salt into a coarse, sticky filling. Chill it.

Divide the dough into 8. Flatten each into a 7cm disc on your palm, place a teaspoon of filling in the centre, draw the edges over and roll into a smooth cylinder about 5cm long. Seal any cracks with a wet fingertip.
steps.tip: A cracked gatta leaks its stuffing into the boiling water and collapses.

steps.text: Lower the cylinders into 1.2 litres of gently boiling salted water. Cook 12 minutes. They will bob to the surface and firm up. Lift out, cool 5 minutes, then cut each into 3 thick pieces. Keep 300ml of the cooking water.
Fry the pieces in the remaining 2 tbsp oil over medium heat, turning, until they are freckled gold on the cut faces, about 4 minutes. Set aside.
In the same kadhai heat the ghee, crackle the cumin, add the hing, and one second later the onion paste. Cook 8 minutes until it stops smelling raw and pulls away from the pan.

Add the ginger and garlic and fry 2 minutes, then the kashmiri chilli, coriander powder and remaining turmeric with a splash of water. Bhuno until the oil separates and rims the masala, about 4 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat, wait 30 seconds, then pour in the whisked yogurt in a thin stream, stirring constantly. Return to low heat and keep stirring until it comes to a bare simmer.
steps.tip: Off the heat, thin stream, constant stirring. This is the only place this dish goes wrong.

steps.text: Add the reserved cooking water, salt and the fried gatte. Simmer uncovered 10 minutes until the gravy coats a spoon and darkens.
Finish with garam masala and crushed kasuri methi, rest 5 minutes off the heat, and scatter coriander over. Serve with plain phulka or rice.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated; the gatte drink up the gravy, so loosen with hot water when reheating. Do not freeze. The yogurt gravy turns grainy.

recipes.name: Haldi ki Sabzi
recipes.subtitle: winter curry of fresh turmeric root and peas cooked down in yogurt and ghee

ingredients.qty: 250g fresh root, peeled and coarsely grated
ingredients.note: fresh haldi, not powder. The root is the whole dish, and it is only around in winter
fresh turmeric drinks fat; cutting this down makes the dish harsh
a spoonful a head, alongside rather than in the pan. The last step calls for it and it was missing from this list
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Wear gloves to peel and grate the turmeric, and do it on a board you do not mind staining. It dyes everything it touches for days.
Bring the yogurt to room temperature and whisk it smooth before you begin.
Grate the turmeric just before cooking; grated root dries out and darkens fast.

steps.text: Heat 4 tbsp ghee on low and add the grated turmeric.
Fry gently for 12-15 minutes, stirring often, until the raw earthy smell turns sweet and the ghee runs clear orange at the sides.
steps.tip: Low heat throughout. Browned turmeric turns bitter and there is no fixing it.

steps.text: Push the turmeric aside, add the remaining 2 tbsp ghee and crackle the cumin, then the hing, ginger and green chillies.
Stir in the coriander and chilli powders off the heat for 10 seconds.
Take the pan right off the flame, add the whisked yogurt, then return to the lowest heat and stir continuously 5-6 minutes until it thickens and the ghee separates.
steps.tip: This gravy splits easily. Off the heat first, and never stop stirring until it simmers.

steps.text: Add the peas, salt and water, cover and simmer 10 minutes until the peas are tender and the gravy is thick.
Stir in the cream and garam masala and cook 2 more minutes.
Rest 5 minutes, scatter the coriander leaves and serve with bajre ki roti and a spoonful of jaggery on the side.
steps.tip: The jaggery is not a garnish. The sweetness is what makes the turmeric bearable in quantity.

recipes.name: Junglee Maas
recipes.subtitle: a hunter's mutton cooked with almost nothing but ghee, whole red chillies and salt

ingredients.note: this much is not a mistake; it is the cooking medium and the sauce

ingredients.qty: 14 whole, stems snapped, seeds shaken out
ingredients.note: Mathania chillies for colour without brutal heat

prepNotes: Take the mutton out of the fridge 30 minutes ahead so it browns instead of stewing.
Shake the seeds out of the chillies. Fourteen chillies with seeds in is inedible; without, it is deep and warm.
This dish was cooked in hunting camps with whatever was carried on the horse: meat, ghee, chilli, salt. Resist adding onion, tomato or garam masala. The point is what is missing.

steps.text: Warm the ghee in a heavy pot over medium heat and add the whole red chillies. Fry 40 seconds until they swell and darken, then lift them out and set aside.
steps.tip: Chillies go from fragrant to acrid in seconds. Get them out early; they go back in later.

steps.text: Add the crushed garlic to the ghee and fry 1 minute until it is pale gold and perfumed.
Raise the heat, add the mutton in a single layer and let it sit undisturbed 4 minutes before turning. Brown all over, about 12 minutes total.
steps.tip: Crowding the pot steams the meat grey. Brown in two batches if your pot is small.

steps.text: Return the chillies to the pot with the salt and turn everything over the heat for 3 minutes so the ghee takes on the chilli colour.
Add 300ml water, bring to a boil, then cover and drop to the barest simmer.
Cook 55-65 minutes, turning the meat every 15 minutes, until it pulls away from the bone under a fork.
steps.tip: A trembling surface, never a boil. Boiled mutton goes stringy and no amount of extra time fixes it.

steps.text: Uncover, raise the heat and cook off the remaining liquid, stirring, until the ghee separates out clear and red and clings to the meat, about 8 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes off the heat, then tilt the pot and spoon off any ghee you do not want. Serve with bajre ki roti.

recipes.storage: Better on the second day. Keeps 3 days refrigerated under its layer of set ghee, which seals it. Reheat gently on the stove; freezes well for 2 months.

recipes.name: Ker Sangri
recipes.subtitle: dry desert-style beans and berries, tart with amchur and hot with whole red chilli

ingredients.note: stands in for dried sangri pods, which are hard to find outside Marwar. If you have sangri, use 100g soaked overnight instead
the sweet counterweight to the chilli; traditionally these stand in for ker berries
the sharpness is part of the dish
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Soak the raisins in warm water 15 minutes so they plump rather than scorch in the oil.
If you are using real dried sangri and ker, soak them overnight and boil 20 minutes with a pinch of salt before they go anywhere near the pan.
Heat the mustard oil to smoking, then cool it slightly before cooking. Raw mustard oil tastes bitter.

steps.text: Boil the cluster beans in salted water 8 minutes, until just yielding but still squeaky. Drain well and pat dry.
steps.tip: Dry beans fry; wet beans steam and go limp.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil until it smokes, take it off the flame for 30 seconds, then return it to medium heat.
Crackle the cumin and ajwain, add the whole red chillies and hing, and fry 20 seconds until the chillies swell and darken.
Stir in the turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder off the heat for 5 seconds so they bloom without burning.
Add the drained beans and toss over high heat 4-5 minutes until they take on brown blistered patches.
Fold in the raisins and apricot, add the water and salt, cover and cook 8 minutes on low.
Lower the heat right down, stir in the whisked yogurt and cook 4 minutes until it clings to the beans and no liquid pools at the base.
steps.tip: Yogurt on high heat will split. Keep the flame at its lowest.

steps.text: Finish with the amchur, toss once, and serve dry alongside bajre ki roti and a spoon of ghee.
steps.tip: This dish is meant to be dry and oily, not saucy. Cook off any remaining water.

recipes.storage: Keeps 4-5 days refrigerated and genuinely improves by day two. Reheat dry in a pan over medium heat; the oil re-coats the beans as it warms.

recipes.name: Khoba Roti
recipes.subtitle: a thick wheat flatbread pinched into ridges that hold pools of ghee

ingredients.note: 1 in the dough, 2 for brushing

prepNotes: Khoba means a cavity. The pinched pits are not decoration. They catch ghee and stop the thick bread from drying out, which matters in a desert.
Knead the dough stiffer than you would for a chapati and rest it at least 20 minutes, or the pinched ridges slump flat on the tawa.
Traditionally the roti is finished over dying coals. A gas flame or a very hot tawa does the same job.

steps.text: Mix the atta with the salt, ajwain and 1 tbsp ghee, rubbing until it feels like breadcrumbs.
Add the warm water in stages and knead 8 minutes into a firm, smooth dough. Noticeably stiffer than chapati dough. Cover and rest 20 minutes.
steps.tip: Warm water makes a stiff dough pliable. Cold water leaves it tight and it will crack at the edges.

steps.text: Divide into 4. Roll each into a thick disc about 15cm across and a full 1cm deep. Do not roll it thin.
Working from the centre out, pinch the surface between thumb and forefinger to raise ridges, leaving a pattern of small pits across the whole disc. Leave a 1cm plain border.
steps.tip: Pinch, do not press. You want raised walls and hollows, not dents.

steps.text: Heat a tawa on medium until a drop of water skitters. Lay the roti pinched side up and cook 3 minutes until the base is set and pale brown in patches.
Flip and cook the pinched side 2 minutes, pressing only the plain border with a cloth so the ridges keep their shape.
Flip back and cook the base another 3-4 minutes on low, turning the roti a quarter turn twice so it cooks evenly. It should sound hollow when tapped.
steps.tip: Low and slow. A thick roti browned fast is raw in the middle.

steps.text: Finish the pinched side directly over a low open flame for 30 seconds until the ridge tips char in spots.
Brush generously with the remaining ghee while hot so it runs into the pits. Serve with lehsun ki chutney or ker sangri.

recipes.storage: Best eaten straight off the tawa. Keeps 1 day wrapped in a cloth; revive on a dry tawa for 2 minutes a side and re-brush with ghee. Do not microwave, it goes leathery.

recipes.name: Laal Maas
recipes.subtitle: fiery mutton curry stained deep red by whole chillies and slow-cooked in ghee

ingredients.qty: 800g, on the bone, cut into 4cm pieces
ingredients.note: shoulder and ribs. The bones make the gravy
stands in for Mathania chillies; they give colour more than heat
add these for the actual heat
laal maas is not a lean dish; the ghee carries the chilli

prepNotes: Soak the Kashmiri chillies in hot water for 30 minutes, then grind to a smooth paste with a little of the soaking water. This paste is the dish.
Bring the mutton to room temperature 30 minutes before cooking so it browns instead of steaming.
Whisk the yogurt with the chilli paste ahead of time. Added separately, the yogurt splits.

steps.text: Heat the ghee and fry the whole spices (cloves, cinnamon, black cardamom, bay leaf and cumin) for 30 seconds until they smell toasted.
Add the sliced onion and cook 12-14 minutes over medium heat until deep gold and collapsed.
steps.tip: Do not rush this; pale onion makes a thin, raw-tasting gravy.

steps.text: Stir in the garlic and ginger pastes and fry 3 minutes until the raw smell goes.
Add the mutton and brown over high heat 8 minutes, turning the pieces so they seize on all sides.
Turn the heat to low, add the yogurt-and-chilli paste with the coriander powder and turmeric, and bhuno for 12-15 minutes, stirring, until the ghee separates and pools red at the edges.
steps.tip: This is the whole recipe in one step. If the ghee has not separated, keep going.

steps.text: Add the whole dried red chillies, salt and water, and pressure-cook 5 whistles, or cover and simmer 60 minutes, until the meat pulls off the bone.
Uncover and reduce 10 minutes until the gravy is glossy and clings to the meat.
Optional dhungar: set a small steel bowl in the pan, drop in a red-hot coal, pour a teaspoon of ghee over it and cover for 4 minutes to smoke the curry.
steps.tip: Four minutes is plenty. Longer and it tastes like an ashtray.

steps.text: Sprinkle the garam masala, rest 10 minutes, and serve with bajre ki roti or plain rice.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and tastes better on day two once the chilli settles. Reheat gently on the stovetop with a splash of water; freezes well for a month.

recipes.name: Lehsun ki Chutney
recipes.subtitle: a fierce red garlic and chilli chutney pounded with mustard oil and lemon

ingredients.note: Mathania chillies if you can get them
for colour only

prepNotes: Soak the dried chillies in hot water for 20 minutes before you start. Dry chillies grind into gritty flakes; soaked ones grind into a paste.
Wear gloves or oil your hands before handling this quantity of chilli, and grind in a well-ventilated kitchen.
Mustard oil must be heated until it just smokes and then cooled. Raw mustard oil tastes acrid in an uncooked chutney.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil until it smokes faintly, then take it off the heat and let it cool to warm, about 5 minutes.
steps.tip: This one step is the difference between a chutney that tastes sharp and one that tastes round.

steps.text: Drain the soaked chillies, keeping 4 tbsp of the soaking water.
Grind the chillies, garlic, cumin and salt to a thick, coarse paste with the soaking water. Stop while it still has some texture. This is not a smooth sauce.
steps.tip: Pulse rather than run the blender; a continuous grind heats the garlic and makes it bitter.

steps.text: Return 2 tbsp of the mustard oil to the pan on medium heat and fry the paste, stirring, for 6-8 minutes until it darkens and the raw garlic smell is gone.
Stir in the kashmiri chilli in the last minute for colour, then take the pan off the heat.
Cool completely, then beat in the lemon juice and the remaining tablespoon of mustard oil.
steps.tip: Add the lemon only when cold, or the chutney loses its brightness.

steps.text: Taste for salt. It should be hot, sour, garlicky and just loose enough to spoon.

recipes.storage: Packs into a clean jar with a film of oil on top and keeps 3 weeks refrigerated. Always use a dry spoon. Serve with bajre ki roti, dal baati or khichdi.

recipes.name: Mangodi ki Sabzi
recipes.subtitle: sun-dried moong dal nuggets fried crisp and stewed in a tart tomato masala

ingredients.qty: 150g split moong dal, soaked and ground into nuggets
ingredients.note: or 120g ready-made mangodi from the shop
3 for frying the mangodi, 2 for the masala
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free
the sourness that makes this a desert dish

prepNotes: To make mangodi from scratch: soak the moong dal 4 hours, grind to a thick fluffy paste with almost no water, beat in a pinch of salt, then drop pea-sized blobs onto a cloth and dry them in full sun for 2-3 days until they rattle. They keep a year in a jar, which is the whole point of them.
If you are using shop-bought mangodi, sort out any broken crumbs first. They burn in the oil and turn the sabzi bitter.
Puree the tomatoes ahead; chopped tomato leaves lumps that never break down in the short cook.

steps.text: Heat 3 tbsp oil in a kadhai over medium heat and fry the mangodi in two batches, stirring constantly, until they turn a deep reddish brown and smell nutty, about 3 minutes a batch. Drain on paper.
steps.tip: They colour all at once at the end. Stand over them.

steps.text: Tip out all but 2 tbsp of oil. Crackle the cumin and mustard seeds, then add the hing and let it foam for a second.
Add the garlic, ginger and green chilli and fry 90 seconds until the garlic is pale gold at the edges.
Stir in the turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder with 2 tbsp water so they do not scorch, then pour in the tomato puree.
Cook the masala on medium heat 8-10 minutes, stirring, until it thickens, darkens and the oil pools at the sides.
steps.tip: No oil at the sides means the tomato is still raw and the sabzi will taste sharp.

steps.text: Add 600ml water and salt, bring to a boil, then slide in the fried mangodi.
Simmer uncovered 12-15 minutes until the mangodi have swollen to twice their size and are soft right through but still hold their shape.
steps.tip: Bite one at 12 minutes. Overcooked mangodi dissolve into the gravy.

steps.text: Stir in the amchur and garam masala, simmer 2 minutes more, and finish with coriander. Serve with bajre ki roti.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and thickens considerably; loosen with hot water and re-simmer 3 minutes. Uncooked mangodi keep a year in an airtight jar.

recipes.name: Mawa Kachori
recipes.subtitle: jodhpur's sweet kachori. Khoya and nuts in flaky pastry, drowned in syrup

ingredients.qty: 60ml for the dough, plus 700ml for frying

ingredients.note: the filling. Use fresh, crumbly khoya if you can get it

ingredients.qty: 100g, powdered for the filling, plus 350g for the syrup
175ml for the syrup, plus about 100ml for the dough

ingredients.note: half in the filling, half to garnish

prepNotes: Roast the grated khoya and cool it completely before filling. Warm khoya melts, runs and bursts the pastry in the oil.
Rub the ghee into the flour until a squeezed fistful holds together. This is what makes the crust flaky rather than hard.
Have the syrup made and just warm. Kachoris are dipped hot from the fryer.

steps.text: Rub the 60ml ghee into the maida with the pinch of salt for 3 minutes, then add water gradually to a soft dough. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
Roast the grated khoya in a dry pan over low heat 6-8 minutes until it smells nutty and turns pale gold. Spread on a plate and cool fully.
steps.tip: Cool means cold. This is the step people skip and then wonder why the kachoris leak.

steps.text: Mix the cold khoya with the powdered sugar, cardamom, almonds, cashew, half the pistachios, raisins and dried coconut.
Boil the 350g sugar with 175ml water 6 minutes to a one-string syrup, add the saffron, and keep it warm.
Divide the dough into 8. Roll each into a 9cm disc, thicker in the middle than at the rim.
Place a heaped tablespoon of filling in the centre, gather the edges up over it, pinch tightly shut and twist off the excess dough.
steps.tip: Any gap in the seal and the filling escapes into the ghee. Pinch hard and check each one.

steps.text: Flatten each gently with your palm into a 7cm disc and rest them seam-down for 10 minutes.
Heat the frying ghee to a low 140C. A kachori should take a good 10 seconds to float up.
Fry 4 at a time for 12-14 minutes on low, spooning ghee over them, until blistered and pale gold all over.
steps.tip: If they brown in under 8 minutes the ghee is too hot and the pastry inside stays raw.

steps.text: Drain briefly, then dip each hot kachori in the warm syrup for 30 seconds and lift onto a plate.
Crack open the top, spoon a little extra syrup inside, scatter the remaining pistachios and serve warm.

recipes.storage: Best the day they are made. Keeps 2 days at room temperature, syrup kept separate; warm 6 minutes in a 170C oven and dip again before serving.

recipes.name: Methi Bajra Puri
recipes.subtitle: millet and fenugreek puris, crisp-edged and faintly bitter

ingredients.note: binds the millet. Bajra alone will not roll into a puri

ingredients.qty: 2 tbsp for the dough, plus 600ml for frying

prepNotes: Toss the chopped methi with 1/2 tsp salt and leave 10 minutes, then squeeze hard. This pulls out the water and much of the bitterness.
Knead with warm water. Bajra needs the heat to come together, even with the wheat flour in it.
Rest the dough 15 minutes before rolling, no longer; the methi keeps weeping and the dough goes slack.

steps.text: Squeeze the salted methi dry and put it in a bowl with both flours, ajwain, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, sesame and salt.
Rub in the 2 tbsp oil, then add warm water a little at a time to make a stiff dough, firmer than chapati dough.
steps.tip: Stiff dough gives puffed puris; soft dough soaks up oil.

steps.text: Knead 5 minutes until smooth, cover and rest 15 minutes.
Divide into 16 balls and roll each into a 10cm disc on a lightly oiled surface, about 3mm thick.
steps.tip: Oil the surface rather than dusting with flour. Loose flour burns and blackens the frying oil.

steps.text: Heat the oil to 180C. A scrap of dough should rise to the surface in about 2 seconds.
Slide in one puri, press it under with the back of a slotted spoon for 3 seconds until it puffs.
Flip and fry the second side 30-40 seconds until the edges are crisp and the colour is deep brown-green.
steps.tip: Bajra puris go darker than wheat ones. Judge by the crisp edge, not the colour.

steps.text: Drain upright in a colander so the oil runs off, and serve hot with aloo pyaaz ki sabzi or plain yogurt.

recipes.storage: Best within 2-3 hours. They soften as they cool; keep 2 days in an airtight tin and crisp for 5 minutes in a 180C oven before serving.

recipes.name: Mirchi Vada
recipes.subtitle: jodhpur's fat green chillies stuffed with spiced potato and fried in gram-flour batter

ingredients.note: the big mild ones, roughly 10cm. Thin hot chillies are inedible here

ingredients.qty: 700ml for deep frying, plus 2 tbsp for the filling

ingredients.note: use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free
in the batter
for a lighter crust

prepNotes: Boil the potatoes an hour ahead and let them cool completely. Warm potato makes a wet filling that leaks into the oil.
Slit each chilli lengthways down one side only, from just below the stem, and scrape out the seeds and white pith with a small spoon. The pith is where the heat sits.
Mix the batter thick, then let it sit 10 minutes so the besan hydrates and clings.

steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp oil, crackle the cumin and fennel, add the hing and grated ginger, and fry 30 seconds.
Add the turmeric, chilli and coriander powders off the heat, then fold in the mashed potato and salt.
Cook 4 minutes over medium heat, then stir in the amchur and coriander leaves and cool completely.
steps.tip: The filling should taste distinctly sour and slightly over-salted. The chilli and batter mute it.

steps.text: Whisk the besan with the ajwain, baking soda, a pinch of salt and enough water to make a batter that thickly coats a spoon and does not run off it.
steps.tip: Runny batter slides off the chilli in the oil. It should be the consistency of soft-set honey.

steps.text: Pack each chilli firmly through its slit with the potato filling and press the slit closed.
Heat the frying oil to 175C. A drop of batter should rise steadily and sizzle without browning instantly.
Dip each stuffed chilli in the batter, turning to coat completely including the ends, and lower it into the oil.
Fry 4-5 minutes, turning once, until the crust is pale gold and crisp. Do no more than three at a time.
steps.tip: Crowding the pan drops the oil temperature and the vadas turn greasy.

steps.text: Drain on paper and serve hot with tamarind or mint chutney, or pushed into a soft bun as Jodhpur does.

recipes.storage: Best within an hour of frying. Refrigerate up to 2 days and re-crisp in a 200C oven for 8 minutes. Never the microwave, which turns the crust to paste.

recipes.name: Moong Dal Halwa
recipes.subtitle: a slow-roasted lentil halwa, grainy and deeply nutty, eaten in the cold months

ingredients.qty: 200g split yellow moong dal, soaked 4 hours

ingredients.note: less than this and it will catch and taste scorched

ingredients.qty: a generous pinch, soaked in 2 tbsp warm milk

prepNotes: Soak the moong dal 4 hours, then drain it very well and grind it coarse with barely a tablespoon of water. A wet, smooth paste makes gluey halwa; a coarse, thick one makes grainy halwa, which is what you want.
Heat the milk and keep it hot on the side. Cold milk added to roasting dal seizes it into lumps.
Clear an hour for this. The roasting cannot be hurried and cannot be left alone, and every recipe that claims otherwise is describing a worse halwa.

steps.text: Grind the drained dal to a coarse, thick paste. It should hold a ridge when you drag a spoon through it.
Melt the ghee in a heavy kadhai over low-medium heat and add the dal paste. It will seize into a solid mass immediately, this is normal.

Roast, stirring and scraping constantly with a flat spatula, for 35-45 minutes. It moves through pale lumps, then a sandy crumble, then a loose glossy mass that smells like toasted besan and turns golden brown.
steps.tip: This is the whole recipe. Stop stirring for two minutes and the base scorches; stop roasting early and the halwa tastes of raw lentil.

steps.text: Fry the almonds, cashews and raisins in a spoonful of the separating ghee for 1 minute and lift them out.
Keep going until the ghee visibly separates and pools around the edges of the mass. Do not move on before this happens.
Meanwhile bring the sugar and 200ml water to a boil in a small pan and simmer 3 minutes into a thin syrup. Keep it hot.
Pour the hot milk into the roasted dal in three additions, stirring hard after each, and let it be absorbed before the next.
steps.tip: It will spit. Stand back and add it slowly.

steps.text: Add the hot syrup and the saffron milk. Stir continuously 8-10 minutes until the halwa drinks it up and thickens.
Cook until the halwa comes together and slides as one mass, leaving a clean film of ghee on the pan, about 5 minutes more.
Fold in the crushed cardamom and the fried nuts and raisins. Rest 5 minutes off the heat and serve hot.

recipes.storage: Keeps 5 days refrigerated. Reheat portions in a pan with 1 tsp ghee and a splash of milk until loose again; it sets solid when cold. Freezes 1 month.

recipes.name: Panchmel Dal
recipes.subtitle: five lentils cooked together and finished with a ghee, hing and red chilli tadka

ingredients.note: split and skinned
half in the dal, half in the final tadka
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free
or a squeeze of lemon at the table

prepNotes: Rinse the five dals together until the water runs clear, then soak 30 minutes. Chana dal is the slowest of them and soaking evens out the cooking.
This is the dal that goes with dal baati, so make it thinner than you think. It should pour, not sit.
Keep the tadka ingredients within reach; the last step takes under a minute.

steps.text: Drain the soaked dals and pressure-cook with the turmeric, 1 tbsp ghee and 900ml water for 4 whistles, then let the pressure drop naturally.
steps.tip: The ghee in the cooker stops the dal frothing up into the vent.

steps.text: Whisk the cooked dal briefly. It should be soft but the chana dal still recognisable, not a puree.
Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a separate pan, crackle 1 tsp cumin with the bay leaf and cloves.
Add the ginger and green chilli and fry 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the coriander powder, chilli powder and half the hing off the heat for 10 seconds, then add the tomato and cook 4 minutes until it breaks down.
steps.tip: Ground spices burn in hot ghee. Always take the pan off the flame first.

steps.text: Pour this into the dal with the salt and the remaining water, and simmer 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until it thickens to a pouring consistency.
Stir in the amchur and garam masala and taste for salt and sourness.
For the final tadka, heat the last 2 tbsp ghee, crackle the remaining cumin, add the broken red chillies and the rest of the hing, and pour it over the dal while it is still foaming.
steps.tip: Pour it on at the table. The noise and the smell are half the point.

steps.text: Scatter the coriander leaves and serve with baati or bajre ki roti.

recipes.storage: Keeps 4 days refrigerated and thickens considerably. Reheat with 100ml water per portion and refresh with a small ghee-and-cumin tadka. Freezes for a month.

recipes.name: Pyaaz Kachori
recipes.subtitle: flaky fried pastry packed with a dark, heavily spiced onion and besan filling

ingredients.qty: 60ml for the dough, plus 700ml for frying
ingredients.note: the dough fat is what makes the crust flake
binds the filling and stops it going watery

prepNotes: Rub the oil into the flour until a fistful holds its shape when squeezed. If it crumbles apart, add more oil. This test decides whether the kachori flakes or goes hard.
Make the filling first and cool it completely. Warm filling steams inside the pastry and bursts it in the oil.
Rest the dough 30 minutes under a damp cloth before rolling.

steps.text: Rub the 60ml oil into the maida with 1/2 tsp salt for 3 minutes, then add water a little at a time to make a soft, smooth dough. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
steps.tip: Softer than roti dough. A tight dough gives a hard, blistered kachori.

steps.text: Heat 3 tbsp oil in a kadhai and crackle the cumin, fennel and nigella, then add the hing.
Add the chopped onion and cook 12-15 minutes over medium heat until it loses all its water and turns light brown.
steps.tip: Keep going until the pan is dry. Wet filling is the single most common reason kachoris split.

steps.text: Stir in the ginger, green chilli and besan and roast 4 minutes until the besan smells nutty.
Add the ground spices, amchur and salt and bhuno 3 more minutes, then spread the filling on a plate to cool.
Divide the dough into 8, roll each into a ball, and flatten into a 8cm disc thicker at the centre than the edge.
Place a heaped tablespoon of filling in the middle, gather the edges over it, pinch shut and pull off the excess knot of dough.
Flatten each stuffed ball gently with your palm into a 7cm disc. Rest them 10 minutes, seam down.
steps.tip: Press with the palm, not a rolling pin. A pin tears the pastry and the filling leaks.

steps.text: Heat the frying oil to just 140C, low enough that a kachori dropped in takes 8-10 seconds to float. Slide in 3 or 4.
Fry very slowly, 12-14 minutes, spooning oil over the tops, until they are covered in blisters and pale gold. Raise the heat for the last 2 minutes to crisp them.
steps.tip: Low and slow is what makes the layers. Hot oil browns the outside and leaves raw dough inside.

steps.text: Drain and serve warm, cracked open with tamarind chutney poured in.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in an airtight tin at room temperature. Re-crisp in a 180C oven for 6-8 minutes. The filling alone freezes for a month.

recipes.name: Rajasthani Kadhi
recipes.subtitle: thin, sour buttermilk kadhi sharpened with a chilli and hing tempering

ingredients.note: day-old and tart is what you want; sweet buttermilk makes a flat kadhi
just a few seeds. More turns it bitter
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Leave the buttermilk out for a few hours, or overnight in a warm kitchen, to sour it properly. Rajasthani kadhi is meant to be sharp.
Whisk the besan into a little of the buttermilk first to make a lump-free slurry, then add the rest. Dumping besan into all the liquid guarantees lumps.

steps.text: Whisk the besan, turmeric, chilli powder and salt into the buttermilk until completely smooth. Strain it if you can see any lumps.
steps.tip: Ten seconds with a sieve now saves a lumpy kadhi later.

steps.text: Pour into a heavy pan and bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly in one direction.
steps.tip: Stop stirring before it boils and it will split into curds and whey.

steps.text: As soon as it boils, drop the heat to low and simmer 15 minutes, stirring every couple of minutes, until it thickens slightly and loses its raw besan smell.
Add the slit green chillies and cook another 2 minutes.
In a small pan heat the ghee, crackle the mustard seeds, then the cumin, then the fenugreek seeds for 10 seconds.
Add the broken red chillies, curry leaves and hing, and pull off the heat the moment the chillies darken.
steps.tip: Fenugreek and hing burn in seconds. Have the kadhi ready and waiting.

steps.text: Pour the tempering over the kadhi, cover for 2 minutes to trap the aroma, then stir through with the coriander leaves.
Serve loose and pourable over steamed rice, or with bajre ki roti.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and thickens as it sits. Reheat on low with a splash of water or buttermilk, stirring; a fresh tadka on top revives it.

recipes.name: Rajasthani Malpua
recipes.subtitle: fennel-scented pancakes fried in ghee and steeped in cardamom syrup

ingredients.note: gives the chewy centre; at a pinch use 4 tbsp milk powder
for crisp lacy edges
the flavour that makes it Rajasthani rather than generic
ghee, not oil. The flavour of the fat is most of the dish

prepNotes: Rest the batter 45 minutes at room temperature. It hydrates the khoya and gives the malpua their chew.
Make the syrup first and keep it warm on the lowest flame. Malpuas go into warm syrup straight from the pan.
The batter should pour off a ladle in a steady ribbon. Thicker than a crepe batter, thinner than pancake batter.

steps.text: Boil the sugar and water 5-6 minutes to a sticky syrup just short of one string, add the saffron and cardamom, and keep warm.
steps.tip: A thick syrup will not soak in; too thin and the malpua go soggy. It should feel tacky between the fingers.

steps.text: Mash the grated khoya with 4 tbsp of the milk until lump-free.
Whisk in the maida, rava and crushed fennel, then the rest of the milk, a little at a time, into a smooth pouring batter.
Rest the batter 45 minutes, then check it. It should coat a spoon and drip in a ribbon. Loosen with milk if needed.
Heat 2cm of ghee in a shallow kadhai over medium heat until a drop of batter sizzles immediately.
Pour a small ladleful into the centre of the pan. Do not spread it. Let it settle into a 8cm disc with frilled edges.
steps.tip: Spreading it tears the malpua. Let the ghee do the work.

steps.text: Fry 2 minutes, spooning hot ghee over the top, until the edges are deep gold and lacy, then flip and fry 1 minute more.
Lift out, drain for a few seconds, and drop straight into the warm syrup. Soak 3-4 minutes, then lift onto a plate.
steps.tip: Longer than 5 minutes and they turn to mush.

steps.text: Repeat with the rest of the batter, frying two at a time, and serve warm with rabri or on their own.

recipes.storage: Best warm, within a few hours. Keeps 2 days refrigerated in a little syrup; warm through in a pan or a low oven. The microwave makes them rubbery.

recipes.name: Safed Maas
recipes.subtitle: pale, creamy mutton braised with cashew, yogurt and white pepper instead of red chilli

ingredients.qty: 800g, on the bone, cut into 4cm pieces

ingredients.note: the skins would speckle the white gravy
boiled, never browned. Brown onion would colour the gravy
the heat of this dish

prepNotes: Soak the cashew, almonds, poppy and melon seeds together in hot water for 20 minutes, then blend to a completely smooth paste with 100ml water. Any grit shows in the finished gravy.
Boil and grind the onion in advance and let it cool. Hot onion paste added to yogurt encourages splitting.
Bring the yogurt to room temperature and whisk it until pourable before you start.

steps.text: Heat the ghee on medium and fry the cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and mace 30 seconds, without letting them colour.
steps.tip: Any browning at this stage tints the gravy; keep the flame moderate.

steps.text: Add the ginger and garlic pastes and cook 2 minutes until the raw edge goes but no colour develops.
Stir in the boiled onion paste and cook 5 minutes on low, stirring, until it thickens and smells sweet.
Add the mutton and turn it in the paste 6 minutes over medium heat, sealing, not browning.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the whisked yogurt, then return to the lowest flame and cook 8 minutes until it thickens and the ghee edges out.
steps.tip: Off the heat first, always. This is where safed maas is usually lost.

steps.text: Add the nut paste, white pepper, green chillies, salt and water. Pressure-cook 5 whistles, or cover and simmer 60 minutes until the meat is tender.
Uncover and simmer 8 minutes to reduce until the gravy coats the back of a spoon.
Stir in the cream and kewra water, warm through 2 minutes without boiling, and rest 10 minutes before serving.
steps.tip: Boiling after the cream goes in makes the gravy grainy.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat over low heat only, stirring, with a splash of milk to bring the gravy back together. Do not freeze. The nut and cream gravy turns grainy.

recipes.name: Aloo Tuk
recipes.subtitle: twice-fried smashed potatoes, crisp outside and floury within, dusted with amchur

ingredients.qty: 600g small potatoes, peeled and halved (or large ones in 3cm chunks)

ingredients.note: check the blend if you need this strictly gluten-free, as some brands carry compounded hing

prepNotes: Peel and halve the potatoes and keep them in cold water until you fry, then drain and dry them completely on a cloth. Wet potatoes spit violently in hot oil.
Tuk is fried twice with a cooling gap in between. Budget 10 minutes of rest between the two fries; skipping it gives you soft, oily potatoes.
Mix the amchur, chaat masala, chilli powder, black salt, pepper and salt in a small bowl before you start frying.

steps.text: Heat the oil to medium. A potato piece dropped in should bubble steadily around the edges, not fizz furiously.
Fry the potatoes in two batches for 8-10 minutes each, until pale gold and a skewer slides in easily. They should be cooked through but not coloured much.
steps.tip: Too hot here and the outside seals before the inside softens, which is the classic tuk failure.

steps.text: Lift them out onto a rack and let them cool for 10 minutes.
Flatten each piece with the heel of your hand or the flat of a knife to about 1.5cm, so the edges crack open.
steps.tip: Press firmly but stop before it falls apart. Those cracked edges are where the crispness comes from.

steps.text: Raise the oil to high, until a scrap of potato surfaces immediately.
Fry the flattened pieces again in batches, 3-4 minutes, until deep golden and audibly crisp when knocked against the ladle.
Drain on a rack rather than paper so the undersides do not steam soft.
While still very hot, toss with the spice mix and taste for salt.
steps.tip: Season them hot. Once they cool, the powder sits on top instead of sticking.

steps.text: Serve at once, alongside sindhi kadhi and rice as tradition has it, or on their own with tea.

recipes.storage: Best within the hour. Fried, unflattened potatoes hold 4 hours at room temperature and can be smashed and given their second fry just before eating; leftovers go soft and reheat poorly.

recipes.name: Bhee Patata
recipes.subtitle: rhizome and potato braised down in a dry onion-tomato masala until the edges catch

ingredients.note: sliced into coins; keep in water so it does not brown

prepNotes: Scrub the lotus stem hard before peeling. The hollow channels running through it trap river mud, and it is gritty if you skip this. Slice into 5mm coins.

Boil the lotus stem coins in salted water for 20 minutes, until a knife enters against slight resistance. It stays crisp however long you cook it, so do not wait for soft. Drain and dry them well. Wet slices will never brown.
Cut the potato thick, in fingers rather than cubes, so it survives the long braise without disintegrating.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadhai and crackle the cumin seeds, about 20 seconds.
Fry the par-boiled lotus stem coins and the potato fingers on medium-high for 8 minutes, turning once or twice, until patched with gold. Lift them out.
steps.tip: Do this in two batches if the pan is crowded. Steamed vegetables here mean a bland, pallid dish.

steps.text: In the same oil, fry the onion 8-10 minutes until properly brown at the edges, not merely soft.
Add the garlic, ginger and green chilli and fry 1 minute, until the raw garlic smell goes.
Stir in the tomato, turmeric, coriander powder, chilli powder and salt and cook 6-8 minutes, until the mass darkens and oil pools at the sides.
steps.tip: Wait for the oil to separate. This is the point at which the masala stops tasting of raw tomato.

steps.text: Return the vegetables, turn them through the masala, add the water and cover.
Cook on low 12-15 minutes, shaking the pan rather than stirring, until the potato is tender and almost no liquid remains.
steps.tip: Stirring breaks the potato into mush. Shake and tilt the pan instead.

steps.text: Uncover, raise the heat and let it fry dry for 2-3 minutes so the underside catches and crusts.
Sprinkle over the amchur and coriander leaves, toss once and take it off the heat.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat uncovered in a pan over medium heat so it crisps again rather than sweating. This is a dry dish and it suffers in the microwave.

recipes.name: Bhee ji Bhaji
recipes.subtitle: dry-cooked lotus stem, crisp at the edges and sharp with amchur

ingredients.note: bhee. Scrub the hollows out under running water
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free
the sourness bhee needs

prepNotes: Peel the lotus stem and slice it, then wash the rounds twice. The hollow channels hold silt that no amount of cooking will remove.
Slice evenly at 5mm. Thicker rounds stay woody in the middle while the thin ones fall apart.
Have everything chopped before you start; once the bhee is parboiled the dish moves quickly.

steps.text: Pressure cook the lotus stem rounds with the water and 1/2 tsp salt for 8 minutes, about 2 whistles, then drain and reserve 1/4 cup of the cooking water.
steps.tip: Bhee is stubborn. Test a round. It should give under a fork but still hold its shape, never mash.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a heavy pan and crackle the ajwain and cumin for 30 seconds.
Add the asafoetida, then the crushed garlic, and fry 45 seconds until it turns pale gold.
Add the onion, ginger and green chilli, and fry 7 minutes until the onion is golden at the edges.
Add the tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder, and cook 6 minutes until the tomato collapses and the oil separates.
Tip in the drained lotus stem and toss to coat every round in masala.
Add the reserved cooking water, cover, and cook 8 minutes over low heat.
Uncover, raise the heat and fry 6-8 minutes without stirring much, until the rounds catch and brown in patches.
steps.tip: The browned edges are the whole point of a bhaji. Stir every 2 minutes at most, or nothing will colour.

steps.text: Sprinkle over the amchur and salt, toss once, and take off the heat.
steps.tip: Amchur goes in at the end. Cooked long it turns flat and slightly bitter.

steps.text: Finish with coriander leaves and serve with phulka.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. Reheat dry in a hot pan rather than a microwave so the edges crisp again.

recipes.name: Bhuga Chawal
recipes.subtitle: brown onion rice, sweet and savoury at once, the plate that sindhi kadhi is poured over

ingredients.note: the entire flavour of the dish, so slice them evenly

prepNotes: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then soak it 20 minutes and drain thoroughly. Drained rice fries; wet rice steams and breaks.
Slice the onions on a mandoline or as thinly as you can by hand. Thick slices will still be raw-tasting when the thin ones have burnt.
Have the water hot. Adding cold water to the browned onions stalls the pot and the grains cook unevenly.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onion over medium heat, stirring often.
Keep going 18-20 minutes. The onions will go translucent, then straw, then a deep mahogany brown and sticky-sweet.
steps.tip: This is the dish. There is no shortcut. High heat gives you black edges and a raw centre.

steps.text: Push the onions aside, add the cumin, bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves and peppercorns and let them sizzle 20 seconds.
Add the drained rice and turn it gently through the onions and oil for 2 minutes, until every grain is glossy and faintly brown.
steps.tip: Fold with a flat spoon, do not stir hard. Soaked basmati snaps easily at this stage.

steps.text: Pour in the hot water, add the salt and bring to a hard boil.
As soon as the water level drops to the surface of the rice, about 5 minutes, cover tightly and drop the heat to its lowest setting.
Cook undisturbed 12 minutes, then take the pot off the heat and let it stand, still covered, 10 minutes.
steps.tip: The standing time is not optional. It is when the last of the steam finishes the grains.

steps.text: Fluff with a fork from the edges inward and serve with sindhi kadhi ladled over.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. Reheat with 2 tbsp water in a covered pan on low, or in a steamer for 8 minutes; the onions keep it from drying out as fast as plain rice.

recipes.name: Dal Pakwan
recipes.subtitle: soft chana dal under a shower of chaat masala with crisp fried maida discs to break over it

image.alt: Dal pakwan, crisp fried discs with chana dal

ingredients.note: for the pakwan
keeps the pakwan crisp for hours

ingredients.qty: 3 tbsp for the dal, 4 tbsp for the pakwan dough, plus 600ml for frying
4 cups for the dal, plus 3/4 cup for the dough

prepNotes: Soak the chana dal 2 hours, or overnight if you are cooking this for breakfast. Drain before cooking.
Make the pakwan dough first and rest it 30 minutes. Resting is what stops it puffing up like a puri.
Sindhi dal pakwan is a breakfast dish; both parts can be made the night before and the dal reheated.

steps.text: Knead the maida, rava, 1/2 tsp ajwain, 1/2 tsp salt and 4 tbsp oil with about 3/4 cup water into a firm, smooth dough. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
Pressure cook the drained dal with the turmeric, 1/2 tsp salt and 4 cups water for 2 whistles, then 4 minutes on low. The grains should be soft but still separate, not a puree.
steps.tip: Chana dal for pakwan must hold its shape. One whistle too many and you have gravy.

steps.text: Heat 3 tbsp oil in a small pan, crackle the remaining cumin and ajwain, add the hing, green chilli and half the ginger.
Add the tomato, chilli powder and amchur and cook 3 minutes until the oil separates, then pour the whole tempering into the dal.
Simmer the dal 8-10 minutes, mashing a ladleful against the side to thicken it. It should be spoonable, like loose porridge.
Divide the dough into 12. Roll each into a thin 12cm disc and prick it all over with a fork, 20 or 30 holes, right through.
steps.tip: Every unpricked patch will balloon. Prick more than you think you need.

steps.text: Heat the frying oil to medium. A scrap of dough should rise slowly, not race to the top. Fry each pakwan 2-3 minutes a side until pale gold and rigid.
steps.tip: Hot oil gives you a puri: puffed, soft, wrong. Medium oil is what makes it snap.

steps.text: Drain the pakwan upright in a colander so they stay crisp rather than steaming on kitchen paper.
Ladle the hot dal into bowls, top with chopped onion, remaining ginger, coriander, chaat masala and black salt, and squeeze over lemon.
Serve at once with the pakwan alongside, to be cracked and dipped.

recipes.storage: The dal keeps 3 days refrigerated and thickens; reheat with a splash of water. Pakwan keep a week in an airtight tin once completely cool. Any residual warmth and they go soft overnight.

recipes.name: Koki
recipes.subtitle: thick crumbly onion flatbread cooked twice on the tawa, the Sindhi breakfast bread

ingredients.note: dried pomegranate seed, the sour note koki is known for

ingredients.qty: 4 tbsp for the dough, plus 4 tbsp for cooking

prepNotes: Chop the onion as finely as you can and toss it with the salt 10 minutes ahead, then squeeze out the water. Wet onion tears the dough.
The dough must be stiffer than roti dough. Closer to shortcrust. Add the water a tablespoon at a time.
Rest the kneaded dough 15 minutes, covered, before rolling.

steps.text: Rub 4 tbsp ghee into the atta with your fingertips until the flour clumps when squeezed. This moyan is what makes koki crumbly rather than chewy.
steps.tip: Under-rubbed flour gives a bready koki. You want it to feel like damp sand.

steps.text: Mix in the squeezed onion, green chilli, coriander, anardana, ajwain, cumin, chilli powder and salt.
Add water a spoonful at a time and knead to a stiff, tight dough. Cover and rest 15 minutes.
Divide into 4 balls. Roll each one about 1cm thick and 12cm across. Much thicker than a roti.
Cook the first side on a medium-hot tawa, dry, for about 1 minute, until it turns opaque and speckles lightly. Flip and give the other side 1 minute.
Lift the half-cooked disc off, let it cool a minute, then roll it again to about 7mm thick. Prick all over with a fork.
steps.tip: This double-rolling is the whole technique. It breaks the gluten and gives koki its short, crumbly crumb.

steps.text: Return it to the tawa on low-medium heat, spoon a tablespoon of ghee around the edge and cook 3-4 minutes a side, pressing with a cloth, until deep gold with brown blisters.
steps.tip: Low and slow. A koki browned fast is raw and doughy in the middle.

steps.text: Repeat with the remaining dough and serve hot with plain yogurt, mango pickle or sweet tea.

recipes.storage: Koki keeps 2 days at room temperature in a cloth-lined box and travels well. It is the traditional train-journey bread. Refresh on a dry tawa for a minute a side; do not microwave, it goes leathery.

recipes.name: Mitho Lolo
recipes.subtitle: sweet fennel-scented ghee flatbread, made for Cheti Chand and eaten with plain yogurt

ingredients.qty: 4 tbsp for the dough, plus 5 tbsp for cooking

ingredients.note: the defining flavour
traditional, and it cuts the sweetness
keeps the lolo soft the next day

prepNotes: Dissolve the grated jaggery in 1/2 cup warm water and strain it. Jaggery often carries grit that will tear the dough.
Rub the ghee into the flour before any liquid goes in; this moyan is what makes lolo short and flaky.
Rest the dough 20 minutes covered. It is a stiff, sweet dough and needs the time to relax before rolling.

steps.text: Rub 4 tbsp ghee into the atta with your fingertips for a couple of minutes, until the flour holds its shape when pressed in a fist.
steps.tip: This is the step that decides the texture. Skimp on it and you get a sweet chapati, not a lolo.

steps.text: Mix in the fennel, ground cardamom, cracked pepper and salt.
Pour in the strained jaggery water and the milk and bring it together into a stiff dough. Softer than pastry, firmer than roti dough. Add flour by the spoonful if it sticks.
steps.tip: Jaggery loosens the dough as it stands, so err on the firm side now.

steps.text: Cover and rest 20 minutes.
Divide into 6 balls. Roll each to about 8mm thick and 12cm across, dusting with flour. Thicker than a paratha, and no need to be neat.
Cook on a medium-low tawa for about 2 minutes, until the surface dries and small blisters appear. Flip.
Spoon a tablespoon of ghee around the edge and cook 2-3 minutes a side, pressing gently with a cloth, until both faces are freckled deep brown.
steps.tip: Keep the heat medium-low. Jaggery burns long before the middle of an 8mm bread is cooked.

steps.text: Stack the cooked lolos under a cloth so they steam and soften, and serve warm with plain yogurt or a glass of milk.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in an airtight box at room temperature. Mitho lolo is deliberately made to travel and is often eaten cold. Warm briefly on a dry tawa to bring it back.

recipes.name: Sai Bhaji
recipes.subtitle: spinach and chana dal cooked down with vegetables into a soft green mash, eaten with rice most weeknights

image.alt: Sai bhaji, the spinach and dal one-pot

ingredients.note: the herb that makes it Sindhi rather than generic palak

prepNotes: Rinse the chana dal and soak it 30 minutes while you chop everything. Unsoaked dal will still be gritty when the spinach has gone to mush.
Wash the spinach in three changes of water. Sindhi sai bhaji is mashed, so grit has nowhere to hide.
Chop the vegetables small and roughly the same size; nothing here gets browned, it all cooks together.

steps.text: Heat the oil in the pressure cooker and crackle the cumin seeds, about 20 seconds.
Add the onion, garlic, ginger and green chilli and fry 4 minutes, until the onion is translucent. You are not browning it.
Stir in the tomato, turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder and cook 3 minutes until the oil beads at the edges.
Add the drained chana dal, potato, eggplant and carrot and turn everything through the masala for a minute.
Pile in the spinach and dill with the water and salt. It will look impossibly full; press it down and it collapses within a minute.
steps.tip: Go light on the water. The spinach releases a great deal of its own and a watery sai bhaji cannot be rescued.

steps.text: Close the cooker and cook on high for 3 whistles, then lower the heat and give it 5 minutes more. Let the pressure drop on its own.
Open up and mash everything against the side of the pot with the back of a ladle until it is coarse and green, not smooth.
steps.tip: Mash by hand, never in a blender. Blended sai bhaji turns a flat, unpleasant khaki.

steps.text: Simmer uncovered 5-8 minutes, stirring, until it holds its shape on a spoon. Check the salt.
steps.tip: If it looks loose, this is where you fix it. It should mound, not pour.

steps.text: Serve hot with steamed rice, a spoon of raw onion and a wedge of lemon.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. It stiffens when cold; reheat in a pan with 2 tbsp water, stirring, rather than in the microwave where it dries at the edges.

recipes.name: Sanna Pakora
recipes.subtitle: thin, shatteringly crisp gram flour fritters shot through with sliced onion

ingredients.note: sanna means fine. The thinner the slice, the crisper the pakora

ingredients.qty: 1 medium, sliced into 2mm rounds then halved

ingredients.note: or 1 tsp amchur
for lift, not more

ingredients.qty: 500ml for deep frying, plus 1 tbsp hot for the batter

prepNotes: Salt the sliced onion and let it sit 10 minutes. It releases water that becomes most of your batter liquid, which is why the batter is so thick.
Have the oil heating while you mix, and the batter mixed only just before frying. It slackens and goes limp if it stands.
Set a rack, not paper, for draining. Paper traps steam under the pakoras and softens them.

steps.text: Toss the sliced onion with 1 tsp salt in a wide bowl and leave 10 minutes, then squeeze it lightly over the bowl and keep the liquid.
Add the potato, green chilli, coriander leaves, ajwain, crushed anardana, crushed coriander powder, chilli powder and turmeric to the onion and mix.
Sprinkle the besan and baking soda over the top and rub everything together with your fingers for 2 minutes without adding water.
steps.tip: The vegetables should be coated in dry besan first. Adding water too early makes a smooth batter that fries heavy.

steps.text: Add water a tablespoon at a time until the mixture just clumps in your hand. Thick and shaggy, nothing pourable.
Heat the frying oil in a kadhai to 170C. A pinch of batter should rise to the surface in about 4 seconds.
Stir 1 tbsp of the hot oil into the batter. It lightens the crumb.
Drop rough, loose spoonfuls into the oil, 6 or 7 at a time, and fry 4 minutes until pale gold. Lift and drain on a rack.
steps.tip: Do not press them into neat balls. Ragged edges are what turn crisp.

steps.text: Rest the first batch 5 minutes while you fry the rest.
Return all the pakoras to the oil, now raised to 185C, and fry 90 seconds more until deep gold and hard to the touch.
steps.tip: This double fry is the difference between a crisp pakora and a soggy one twenty minutes later.

steps.text: Drain and serve immediately with tamarind or tomato chutney.

recipes.storage: Eat within the hour. Leftovers keep 1 day in an airtight box and can be crisped in a 200C oven for 6 minutes; never microwave them.

recipes.name: Seyal Bhaji
recipes.subtitle: potato and cauliflower smothered in a wet green coriander masala, quick and everyday

ingredients.qty: 2 large bunches (about 100g), chopped with the tender stalks
ingredients.note: seyal means smothered in green. This is not a garnish quantity

prepNotes: Wash and chop the coriander, stalks included, and keep it ready. It goes in as a bulk vegetable, not a finish.
Cut the cauliflower florets and potato cubes to the same size so they finish together.
Soak the cut potato in cold water while you chop the rest, then drain and pat dry.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadhai and crackle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds.
Add the onion and fry 6-7 minutes, until soft and just turning gold at the edges.
Add the garlic, ginger and green chilli and fry 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato, turmeric, coriander powder, chilli powder and salt and cook 5 minutes until pulpy and oil-flecked.
Tip in the chopped coriander and cook 3-4 minutes, stirring, until it wilts right down and the masala turns dark green.
steps.tip: Let the coriander actually cook into the masala. Thrown in at the end it tastes soapy and raw.

steps.text: Add the potato, cauliflower and peas and turn them through until every piece is coated green.
Add the water, cover and cook on low 15 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally, until the potato gives to a knife.
steps.tip: Half a cup of water is enough. The vegetables release their own and seyal bhaji should cling, not swim.

steps.text: Uncover, raise the heat and cook 3 minutes more to dry off any loose liquid.
Squeeze over the lemon, check the salt and serve with phulka or plain rice.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated, though the green dulls by day two. Reheat in a pan with a tablespoon of water over medium heat.

recipes.name: Seyal Gosht
recipes.subtitle: mutton braised down into a thick green coriander and mint masala

ingredients.qty: 2 large bunches, about 100g with tender stalks
ingredients.note: the body of the masala, not a garnish

prepNotes: Bring the mutton to room temperature 30 minutes before cooking. Cold meat straight from the fridge seizes and stays tough.
Wash the coriander and mint and shake them properly dry. Wet greens water down the paste and it will never fry.
Seyal means cooked in its own thick masala, so keep the water measured. This is not a gravy you ladle.

steps.text: Blend the coriander, mint, green chilli, 8 garlic cloves and the ginger with 3 tbsp water to a coarse green paste.
steps.tip: Stop while it is still slightly grainy. A smooth puree turns muddy brown once it hits the pan.

steps.text: Heat the oil in the pressure cooker and fry the 6 sliced garlic cloves for 40 seconds, until pale gold and fragrant.
Add the onion and cook 8 minutes over medium heat until soft and translucent.
steps.tip: Do not brown it. Sindhi seyal wants sweetness from soft onion, not the deep caramel of a bhuna curry.

steps.text: Add the mutton, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt. Fry over high heat 10 minutes until the meat has released its juices and taken them back, and the pan looks dry.
Stir in the tomato and cook 6 minutes, until it collapses and oil beads at the edge of the mass.
Add the green paste and fry 5 minutes, stirring, until the colour shifts from bright grass green to deep olive.
steps.tip: This is the step people rush. Underfried coriander tastes raw and grassy through the whole dish.

steps.text: Pour in the hot water, close the cooker and cook on high pressure 18 minutes, about 4 whistles. Let the pressure fall on its own.
Open, and boil uncovered 6-8 minutes until the masala clings to the meat and there is no loose liquid in the pan.
steps.tip: The fork test: drag one through and the gravy should close slowly behind it.

steps.text: Stir in the garam masala and lemon juice, cover and rest 5 minutes off the heat before serving with phulka.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and tastes better on day two. Reheat covered over low heat with 2 tbsp water; freezes well for a month.

recipes.name: Sindhi Besan Bhaji
recipes.subtitle: potatoes in a roasted gram flour gravy, tangy and thick enough to scoop

ingredients.note: roasting it dry first is what makes this dish

ingredients.qty: 4 medium, peeled and cut into 2cm cubes

prepNotes: Cube the potatoes and keep them in cold water until the moment they go in, or they will grey.
Measure the besan before you start roasting. Once it is in the dry pan you cannot leave it for a second.
Keep the water hot. Cold water hitting roasted besan sets it into lumps you will never whisk out.

steps.text: Dry roast the besan in the kadhai over low heat for 5 minutes, stirring constantly, until it smells nutty and darkens by a shade.
steps.tip: Low heat and no walking away. Scorched besan is bitter and there is no rescuing the dish.

steps.text: Tip the roasted besan onto a plate and set it aside to cool.
Heat the oil in the same pan and crackle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds.
Add the garlic, ginger and green chilli, fry 45 seconds, then add the onion and cook 8 minutes until golden.
Add the tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder, and cook 6 minutes until the tomato breaks down completely.
Add the potato cubes and toss for 3 minutes so they take on the masala.
Sprinkle the roasted besan over the potatoes and stir for 1 minute to coat them evenly.
Pour in the hot water in a thin stream while stirring continuously, then add salt.
steps.tip: Stream and stir at the same time. Dumping the water in at once is how you get lumps.

steps.text: Cover and simmer 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the gravy has thickened enough to hold a spoon mark.
Stir in the amchur, cook 1 more minute, and finish with coriander leaves.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. It sets almost solid when cold. Reheat with 1/3 cup water per portion, whisking as it loosens.
